"Ānanda! Compared to the great ocean, which of these is greater: that drop of water or the great ocean? Ānanda replied:
"Suppose one were to take water from a thousand *yojanas* deep, yet still consider it insufficient; how much more so when comparing it to a single drop on the tip of a hair!
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"Suppose there were as many bhikṣus as the number of hundreds of thousands of *koṭi-nayuta*, all equal to Mahāmaudgalyāyana, who for hundreds of thousands of *koṭi-nayuta* years together calculated the number of śrāvakas in the first assembly of that Tathāgata Amitāyus; the quantity they could know would be like a single drop of water on the tip of a hair, while the remainder they could not fathom would be like the great ocean."
The assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas is likewise; it cannot be known through calculation.
Their lifespan is immeasurable. (13) "Ānanda!..."
The lifespan of that Buddha is immeasurable and boundless; one cannot know the number of kalpas it comprises.
The lifespans of his śrāvakas, bodhisattvas, and all devas and humans are likewise so.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How much time has elapsed since that Buddha appeared in the world, such that he is able to attain such immeasurable life span?”
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“That Buddha has been born for ten kalpas now.
Section Fourteen: The Adorned Purity of His Realm. Furthermore, Ānanda!”

That realm of Sukhāvatī is adorned with the perfection of immeasurable merits; its lands are bountiful and its devas and humans are flourishing. Their aspirations are harmonious and contented, and they always enjoy peace and security; therein there are no hells, no animals, and no realm of King Yama.
Various fragrances pervaded the air with their exquisite scent, and all kinds of wondrous flowers filled the space.
Seven-jeweled banners were arrayed in rows; atop these banners hung various streamers, canopies, and clusters of precious bells, complete with hundreds of thousands of exquisite colors.
Chapter Fifteen: Adorned with Jewel Trees “Ānanda!

In that Tathāgata’s land, there are many jewel trees. Some are made of pure gold, white silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, red pearls, agate, or jade; some are formed from a single jewel without being mixed with others, while others are adorned with two jewels up to seven jewels.”
Ānanda! Those trees made of gold have roots and trunks of gold, with leaves, flowers, and fruits of white silver.
The trees made of white silver have roots and trunks of silver, with leaves, flowers, and fruits of gold.
The agate trees have agate roots and trunks, with beautiful jade for their leaves, flowers, and fruits.
As for the beautiful jade trees, they have jade for their roots and trunks, and the seven treasures for their leaves, flowers, and fruits.
There were some golden trees, with roots of yellow gold, trunks of white silver, branches of lapis lazuli, twigs of crystal, leaves of red pearls, flowers of agate, and fruits of fine jade.
There were some silver trees, with roots of silver and trunks of gold; the remaining branches, fruits, and so forth were adorned in the same manner as the golden trees.
As for the lapis lazuli trees, they had roots of lapis lazuli, trunks of gold, branches of white silver, twigs of crystal, leaves of red pearls, flowers of agate, and fruits of beautiful jade.
There were trees of crystal, pearl, agate, and other such gems; all their various ornamental decorations were like lapis lazuli.
Furthermore, there were jade trees, with roots of jade, stems of gold, branches of white silver, twigs of lapis lazuli, leaves of crystal, flowers of red pearls, and fruits of agate.
Furthermore, there were immeasurable jewel-adorned trees made of mani-gems and other precious substances that surrounded the entire land.

The radiance of these various jewel-trees was so brilliant and magnificent that nothing in the world could compare to it; they were covered above by nets of the seven treasures, which were as soft and supple as tūla-cotton.
The Sixteenth Chapter on the Bodhi Tree of the Buddha:
"Furthermore, Ānanda, the Buddha Amitāyus has a bodhi tree that is sixteen hundred million yojanas in height, with branches and leaves extending downward for eight hundred million yojanas."
The base of the tree rises five thousand yojanas high, and its circumference is likewise.

Its branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits are constantly adorned with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of varieties of exquisite colors and rare jewels of supreme splendor—namely, moonlight *maṇi* jewels, *śakrābhilagna* jewels, heart-king *maṇi* jewels, and ocean-flowing *maṇi* jewels—their radiance shining everywhere, surpassing that of humans and devas.

Upon those trees hang various golden chains and precious necklaces that adorn them completely; these necklaces are made of *lucaka* gems, *mace* gems, and precious pearls of red, white, and blue colors.
There were lion-clouds and clusters of jewels that served as its chains, adorning the various jeweled pillars.

Furthermore, nets made of pure gold, pearls, and various other gems, along with bells and chimes, were hung as ornaments; these jeweled chains completely covered the structure above. Crystals, the "myriad-character" (*vajra*) jewel, crescent moon jewels, and others reflected one another in mutual brilliance. When stirred by a gentle breeze, they produced all manner of sounds, causing sentient beings throughout the thousandfold world-system to realize the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*) within the profound Dharma according to their respective inclinations.

Ānanda! When all the sentient beings within those thousand worlds hear this sound, they shall abide in non-retrogression from unsurpassed bodhi, and immeasurable, incalculable sentient beings shall attain the patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

If there are sentient beings who see the Bodhi tree, hear its sound, smell its fragrance, taste its fruit, touch its light and shadow, or contemplate the merits of the tree—for these causes and conditions, until they reach Nirvana—their five faculties will be free from affliction and their minds will be undistracted; they shall all attain non-retrogression from Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
Furthermore, by beholding that Bodhi tree, one attains three kinds of patience (*kṣānti*).
What are these three?
First, the patience of following sounds; second, the patience of conformity; and third, the patience of the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).

All of this is due to the majestic spiritual power added by the original vows of Amitāyus Buddha, as well as because his former cultivation of meditative concentration was beyond comparison, free from deficiency, well-practiced, well-sustained, and well-accomplished.
The Great Treasure Accumulation Sutra, Volume Seventeen;
The Great Treasure Accumulation Sutra, Volume Eighteen.
Translated by the Tang Dynasty Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci by Imperial Decree.
The Fifth Assembly on Immeasurable Life, Part Two:
Chapter Seventeen, "The Level Ground Without Mountains.
"Furthermore, Ānanda, in that realm of Sukhāvatī, there are no Black Mountains, Iron Ring Mountains, Great Iron Ring Mountains, or Mount Sumerus."
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
Since the gods of the Four Great Kings and the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven have no mountains, upon what do they rely for their dwelling?"
The Buddha said to Ānanda: "What do you think?
As for the Yāma Heaven up to the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven above Mount Sumeru, as well as the various devas of the Form Realm—upon what do they dwell?"
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This is brought about by inconceivable karmic power.”
The Buddha said to Ānanda,
"Can you understand this inconceivable karma? He replied:
"No," [Ānanda replied]. The Buddha told Ānanda:
"Do you know the power of the roots of goodness and the karmic force of all Buddhas and sentient beings?"
He replied, “No, World-Honored One.”
"I have no actual doubt regarding this Dharma; I have asked this question only to shatter the net of doubts for those in the future.
The eighteenth Buddha, River-Flowing Sublime Sound, told Ānanda:

"In that realm of Ultimate Bliss, there is no ocean, yet there are many rivers. The narrowest of these rivers is ten yojanas wide, and the shallowest is twelve yojanas deep. The depth and breadth of such rivers may be twenty, thirty, or even up to a hundred yojanas, and some are so extremely deep and wide as to reach a thousand yojanas."

The water is clear and cool, endowed with the eight meritorious qualities; its deep currents flow constantly, producing a subtle and wondrous sound like the hundreds of thousands of musical performances of the devas, which is heard everywhere throughout the Land of Peace and Bliss.
Various named flowers float downstream, their diverse fragrances wafting forth as a gentle breeze stirs them.

Along both banks stand many sandalwood trees; their long branches and dense foliage overlap to form a canopy over the river, bearing fruit and blossoming with flowers whose radiant beauty is a delight to behold.

The multitudes of living beings roam and sport, coming and going as they please; some wade into the river to bathe and frolic, moved by the celestial waters which accord perfectly with the needs of things—deep or shallow, cold or warm—yielding in every detail to human preference.

Ānanda! Beneath the great river, the ground is strewn with golden sand; there are various celestial fragrances beyond compare in this world, which disperse their rich scent with the wind and mingle with the flowing current.
Celestial māndārava flowers, utpala flowers, padma flowers, kumuda flowers, and puṇḍarīka flowers completely covered its surface.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

When the people of that country sometimes gather together by the riverbank for recreation, there may be those who do not wish to hear the sound of the rushing current; even if they possess the divine ear, they will ultimately not hear it."

Or there may be those who, upon hearing, immediately comprehend hundreds of thousands of millions of kinds of delightful sounds—namely, the sounds of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha; the sound of cessation; the sound of the absence of intrinsic nature; the sound of the *pāramitās*; the sound of the ten powers and four fearlessnesses; the sound of supernormal powers; the sound of non-action; the sound of neither arising nor ceasing; the sound of tranquility; the sound of ultimate tranquility; the sound of supreme tranquility; the sound of great loving-kindness and great compassion; the sound of the patient acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*); and the sound of the empowerment and conferral of office.

Having heard these various sounds, they attain vast affection, joy, and delight, which correspond to contemplation, renunciation, destruction, tranquility, ultimate tranquility, supreme tranquility, the savor of the meaning, the Buddha-Dharma-Saṅgha, the powers and fearlessnesses, the supernormal knowledges, cessation, bodhi, the śrāvakas, and nirvāṇa.
The Nineteenth: Not Hearing Evil Names. "Furthermore, Ānanda! In that Land of Ultimate Bliss, one does not hear the names of the various evil realms;

there are no names for the afflictions of obstruction at the boundaries; there are no names for hell, Yama, or the animal realm; and there are no names for the eight difficulties. Furthermore, there are no names even for feelings of suffering or neither-suffering-nor-pleasure, let alone actual suffering; therefore, that land is called 'Ultimate Bliss.'"
Ānanda! I have now briefly explained the causes and conditions for Sukhāvatī; were I to explain them in detail, they would not be exhausted even at the end of an eon.
Section Twenty: The Spontaneity of Enjoyment. "Furthermore, Ānanda!"

All sentient beings in that Land of Ultimate Bliss—whether already born, currently being born, or yet to be born—all obtain such wondrous physical bodies, with upright features and sovereign supernatural powers, fully endowed with the power of merit. They enjoy various palaces, gardens, clothing, food, drink, incense, flowers, and necklaces; whatever they require according to their wishes is entirely fulfilled as they think of it, just like the gods of the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Transformations.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

In that buddha-field there is subtle food; none of the sentient beings therein ever consume it by chewing. Just as in the sixth heaven, whatever food or drink they think of appears and is as if already eaten; their physical strength and vitality increase, yet they have no excrement or urine."
Furthermore, there were immeasurable wonderful incenses, ointments, and powdered perfumes of various kinds, whose fragrance universally permeated that Buddha-land;
likewise, scattered flowers, banners, and streamers filled it entirely.
Those who wish to smell fragrances shall smell them immediately according to their wishes, while those who do not delight in them shall never experience them.

Furthermore, there are immeasurable, most excellent garments, jeweled crowns, bracelets, armlets, earrings, necklaces, flower garlands, sashes, and chains—all adorned with various jewels and fully endowed with immeasurable radiance and hundreds of thousands of exquisite colors—which appear spontaneously upon their bodies.
Furthermore, there are nets of gold, silver, pearls, and exquisite jewels, from which various precious bells hang, adorning the surroundings on all sides.

Whatever palaces, towers, and pavilions sentient beings require—whether they desire them to be high or low, long or short, wide or narrow, square or round—and whatever couches and seats with exquisite garments spread upon them, all adorned with various kinds of jewels, appear spontaneously before those beings. Each person thinks to themselves that they are individually residing within their own palace.

21. Humans are like those of the Sixth Heaven. Furthermore, Ānanda, all sentient beings in the Land of Ultimate Bliss have no marks of distinction; they follow the customs of other regions and possess the names "deva" and "human."
Ānanda! It is like a lowly paṭaccara who, in the presence of a wheel-turning monarch, has nothing by which to be compared; his majestic radiance and virtuous renown are entirely lacking.

Furthermore, just as Śakra, compared to those in the sixth heaven, surpasses them all in terms of majestic radiance and its like; his gardens, groves, palaces, garments, various ornaments, noble sovereignty, rank, supernormal powers, and transformations cannot be equaled by theirs—only in the enjoyment of the bliss of the Dharma is there no difference.
Ānanda, you should know that the sentient beings in that land are like the devas of the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Transformations.
Rain of Flowers Spreads Upon the Ground, Twenty-second: “Ānanda!

In that Land of Ultimate Bliss, at the time of dawn, gentle breezes stir from all four directions—neither contrary nor chaotic—blowing the fragrances of various kinds of flowers; these scents pervade and fill the entire realm.

When all sentient beings have their bodies touched by the wind, they experience a state of peace, harmony, and well-being, just like a bhikṣu who has attained the meditative absorption of cessation (*nirodhasamāpatti*).

As that wind blows through the groves of trees made of the seven precious gems, flowers drift down and form mounds reaching the height of seven men; various colored lights illuminate the Buddha-field.
It is as if someone were to spread flowers upon the ground and press them down with their hands to make it level, distributing various colored flowers in an intermingled pattern.

Those clusters of flowers are likewise: they are exquisite, vast, and soft like *tūla* cotton; when sentient beings step upon those flowers, they sink down four finger-widths, and as soon as they lift their feet, the flowers restore themselves to their original state.

Once the morning had passed, those flowers naturally sank into the earth; when the old flowers had vanished, the great earth became pure and clear, and new flowers rained down once more, again covering it everywhere.
In this manner, during the midday, the afternoon, and the first, middle, and last watches of the night, the falling flowers gather into heaps in the same way. Ānanda!
Among all vast and wondrous jewels, there is none that does not arise in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Chapter Twenty-Three: The Buddha Flower-Light Emerges “Ānanda!

In that buddha-field there are lotus flowers made of the seven treasures. Each lotus flower has immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of petals, and those petals possess immeasurable hundreds of thousands of rare and extraordinary colors. They are adorned with hundreds of thousands of exquisite maṇi jewels and covered with jeweled nets that reflect and embellish one another.”
Ānanda! Those lotus flowers are half a yojana in size, or one, two, three, four, or even up to a hundred thousand yojanas.

From each individual flower, thirty-six billion nayutas of hundreds of thousands of rays of light emerge. Within each ray of light, there appear thirty-six billion nayutas of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, their bodies golden in color, endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man and the eighty secondary signs, supremely adorned, emitting hundreds of thousands of rays that universally illuminate the world.
These Buddhas are currently traveling to the eastern direction to preach the Dharma for the multitudes, establishing immeasurable sentient beings within the Buddha-dharma;
it is likewise so in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir.
Chapter Twenty-Four: Free from Discriminatory Marks "Furthermore, Ānanda, in the World of Ultimate Bliss there is no darkness nor is there the light of fire.

There are no surging springs, ponds, or lakes; nor are there names for dwellings, houses, or groves, nor any images representing them. There are no classes of beings such as children, nor are there images of the sun and moon, day and night."
In all places, there are neither signs nor names, except for those empowered by the Tathāgata.
This is the twenty-fifth ultimate fruit: "Ānanda!..."
Any sentient beings who are born in that land will all ultimately reach unsurpassed bodhi and the state of nirvāṇa.

Why is this? Because those in the group of the definitely wrong (mithyātva-niyata-rāśi) and the group of the undetermined (aniyata-rāśi) are unable to understand and establish the causes for that [attainment].
Chapter Twenty-Six: The Buddhas of the Ten Directions Praise Him. “Ānanda!

In the eastern direction, there are worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; in each of these worlds, there are Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. Each of those Buddhas individually extols the immeasurable merits of Amitābha Buddha.
The same is true for the Buddhas in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir.”

Why is this? Because all sentient beings in the Buddha-lands of other directions who hear the name of the Tathāgata Amitāyus, and are able to give rise to even a single thought of pure faith, joy, and delight, and dedicate all their roots of goodness toward the vow to be born in the Land of Amitāyus—they shall all be born there according to their vows and attain the stage of non-retrogression, leading ultimately to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, with the sole exception of those who have committed the five heinous crimes, who have slandered the True Dharma, or who have reviled the noble ones.
The Twenty-Seventh: Rebirth in the Three Grades. “Ānanda!

If there are sentient beings who, in another Buddha-field, resolve their minds on Bodhi, single-mindedly recollect Amitāyus Buddha, and constantly plant numerous roots of goodness, then they shall resolve their minds to dedicate these merits toward the vow to be born in that land.”

When this person is on the verge of death, Amitāyus Buddha, surrounded by a multitude of bhikṣus, will appear before them; they shall then follow the Tathāgata to be reborn in that land and attain the stage of non-retrogression, destined to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Therefore, Ānanda!

If there are good men or good women who wish to be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss and desire to see Amitāyus Buddha, they should resolve their minds upon unsurpassed bodhi. Furthermore, they should single-mindedly contemplate the land of Sukhāvatī, accumulate roots of goodness, and dedicate them toward this goal. By means of this, they will see the Buddha, be born in that land, and attain the stage of non-retrogression up to unsurpassed bodhi.

Ānanda! If sentient beings in other lands give rise to the bodhicitta, even if they do not single-mindedly keep Amitāyus Buddha in mind nor constantly plant a multitude of roots of goodness, yet according to their own practice of various virtuous merits, they dedicate them toward that Buddha, wishing to be reborn there.

When this person is on the verge of death, Amitāyus Buddha immediately dispatches a transformation body, surrounded before and behind by a multitude of bhikṣus. This manifested Buddha, with its radiance and marks of excellence no different from the real one, appears before that person to receive and guide them.
They will immediately follow the transformation Buddha to be reborn in that land, attaining non-retrogression from unsurpassed bodhi. Ānanda!

If there are sentient beings who abide in the Mahāyāna and, with a pure mind, direct themselves toward the Tathāgata Amitāyus—even if they do so for as few as ten moments of thought—vowing to be born in his land, hearing the profound Dharma and immediately giving rise to faith and understanding, their minds free from doubt or confusion.

Even if one attains but a single thought of pure mind and gives rise to a single thought of mindfulness toward Amitāyus Buddha, at the time of death this person will see Amitāyus Buddha as if in a dream; they will certainly be born in that land and attain non-retrogression on the path to unsurpassed bodhi.

Ānanda! For this reason and for these benefits, the Buddhas, Tathāgatas of immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, peerless, and boundless worlds all together praise the merits possessed by the Buddha Amitāyus.
The twenty-eighth Buddha, whom [the assembly] of the ten directions prostrates to and visits, addressed Ānanda:

“In every world-system of the eastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, there are Bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges who come to the place where this Buddha resides, desiring to behold, pay homage to, and make offerings to Amitāyus Buddha and the assembly of holy ones.
It is likewise in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir.”
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
“In the Buddha-fields of the eastern direction, As numerous as the sands of the Ganges River,
Within such buddha-lands, There are bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.”
All manifest supernatural powers as they come, To pay homage to the Buddha of Immeasurable Life;
The holy multitudes from the three directions, In their worshipful audiences, likewise return together.
Within those sands of worlds, They illuminate the Way with light and various eloquent discourses.
Abiding in the bliss of profound meditative concentration, with a mind of the four fearlessnesses,
each brought various wonderful flowers and renowned incenses that bring delight,
while playing all manner of celestial music— hundreds of thousands of harmonious and elegant sounds.
Offered to the Teacher of Gods and Humans, whose fame resounds throughout the ten directions;
possessing ultimate majestic power and having skillfully studied all dharma-gates,
he diligently practices among all manner of offerings without weariness.
The radiance of merit and wisdom can shatter all darkness;
with hearts of reverence, they present various rare and wondrous offerings.
They behold that sublime realm, where the assembly of Bodhisattvas is boundless.
May we swiftly attain Bodhi, and may our pure realm be like Sukhāvatī.
Knowing their aspirations and desires— vast and inconceivable—
the World-Honored One revealed his golden countenance with a smile and declared that it shall be fulfilled according to their wishes.
Realizing that all phenomena are like illusions, That Buddha-lands are like dreams and echoes,
One constantly makes vows to adorn them, So as to achieve a subtle and wondrous land.
Through the power of their vows, Bodhisattvas Cultivate the supreme practices for enlightenment.
Knowing that lands are like reflections, one gives rise to the heart of great vows.
If one seeks universally pure and most excellent, boundless realms,
upon hearing the name of the Buddha’s holy virtue, one should aspire to be born in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
If there are bodhisattvas who, Aiming to seek a pure land, Thoroughly understand that dharmas have no self, And vow to be born in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
[The Twenty-ninth: Those in Their Last Birth] "Furthermore, Ānanda!..."

All the bodhisattvas in the Land of Ultimate Bliss are established in the stage of being born only once more before attaining supreme enlightenment, with the sole exception of those mahāsattvas who possess great vows, who can roar the lion’s roar, who don the great armor, and who cultivate the Great Nirvana for the sake of delivering all living beings.
The Radiance of the Bodies of the Noble Assembly, Number Thirty: "Furthermore, Ānanda!
All the śrāvaka assembly in that buddha-field possess bodily radiance capable of illuminating a fathom."
The light of a bodhisattva shines for a hundred thousand fathoms; however, with the exception of two bodhisattvas, whose light constantly illuminates the trichiliocosm.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
"What are the names of those two bodhisattvas?
The Buddha told Ānanda,
"Listen attentively now."
Those two bodhisattvas are named Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
Ānanda! These two bodhisattvas, having relinquished their life-spans in this Sahā world, have been reborn in that land.
Chapter Thirty-one: The Supreme Virtue of Sublime Marks “Ānanda!

All the bodhisattvas born in that realm of Sukhāvatī are endowed with the thirty-two marks. Their bodies are supple and soft; their faculties are keen and sharp; they possess skillful wisdom and have no lack of understanding regarding the various distinct dharmas. They are adept at sporting in meditative concentration and supernormal powers, and none among them belong to the class of those with meager merit or dull faculties.”

Among those bodhisattvas, there were immeasurable and boundless numbers who attained the first or second patience (*kṣānti*), and some even realized the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
They constantly understood their past lives. (32) "Ānanda!..."

The bodhisattvas in that land do not fall into the evil realms until they attain enlightenment; in every place where they are born, they are able to know their past lives, except when they appear in the world within lands of the five turbidities.
Making Offerings to Buddhas in Other Directions, Chapter Thirty-Three: “Ānanda!

All the bodhisattvas in that land, at the break of dawn, make offerings to immeasurable hundreds of thousands of buddhas in other directions. Whatever various flower garlands, ointments, powdered incense, banners, pennants, silk canopies, and musical instruments they desire appear in their hands through the buddhas’ spiritual power, and they offer them to those buddhas.”
Such offerings as these were vast and numerous, incalculable, boundless, and inconceivable.

Furthermore, if they sought various kinds of named flowers, there appeared within their hands immeasurable hundreds of thousands of radiant colors of blossoms, which they scattered as offerings to all the Buddhas.

Ānanda! Those flowers which were scattered immediately transformed into flower canopies in mid-air; the smallest of these canopies measured ten yojanas across. Unless new flowers were scattered again, the previously scattered flowers would never fall.

Ānanda! There may be flower-canopies twenty yojanas in extent, or likewise thirty, forty, even up to a thousand yojanas; or they may equal the four continents, or pervade the small chiliocosm, the medium dichiliocosm, and even the great trichiliocosm.

These bodhisattvas, having conceived a sense of wonder and attained great joy and affection, served, made offerings to, honored, and praised immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of buddhas during the morning hours; and having planted various roots of goodness, they immediately returned to their own lands that very morning.

All of this is due to the empowerment of the original vows of Amitāyus Buddha, as well as because their roots of goodness from having made offerings to the Tathāgatas have continued without interruption, been well-cultivated, well-accumulated, and well-accomplished.
The Thirty-Fourth Chapter on the Merits of Bodhisattvas:

"Furthermore, Ānanda, the speech uttered by the assembly of bodhisattvas in that realm of Ultimate Bliss is in accord with omniscience; regarding all that they enjoy, they maintain no sense of grasping; they travel throughout the buddha-fields without love or aversion, nor do they harbor any longing."
One does not harbor thoughts of seeking, nor thoughts of a self, nor thoughts of afflictions, nor thoughts of a personal ego, nor thoughts of strife, opposition, enmity, or anger. Why is this?

Because those bodhisattvas possess a mind of great compassion and the intent to benefit all sentient beings, they have a supple and unobstructed mind, an unturbid mind, and a mind free from anger and resentment;
they possess a mind of impartiality, subduing, and tranquility, a mind of patience, and a mind of patient subduing; they possess a state of meditative equipoise that is clear, pure, and undistracted.
A disordered mind, an unobscured mind, a pure mind, an extremely pure mind, a luminous mind, a dustless mind,
a mind of great majesty, a virtuous mind, a vast mind, an incomparable mind, a profoundly deep mind, a mind that loves the Dharma,
a mind that rejoices in the Dharma, a well-intentioned mind, and a mind that has relinquished all attachments.
Because they have focused their minds on severing the afflictions of all sentient beings and closing off all evil destinies,
they have practiced the conduct of wisdom and accomplished immeasurable merit. They are well able to expound upon the branches of dhyāna and awakening,
and they constantly sport within unexcelled bodhi, diligently cultivating and propagating it.

The fleshly eye arises with the capacity for discernment; the divine eye appears to perceive all Buddha-fields; the Dharma-eye is purified and able to remain free from all attachments; the wisdom-eye penetrates and reaches the further shore; the Buddha-eye achieves awakening and provides instruction, giving rise to unimpeded wisdom to expound extensively for others.
Practicing with equanimity within the three realms, they have already disciplined themselves and are likewise able to discipline all sentient beings, enabling them to attain supreme śamatha.

Having realized the non-apprehensibility of all phenomena, they are skillful in preaching the Dharma with eloquent speech; they diligently cultivate offerings to all Buddhas, subdue all afflictions of sentient beings, and are approved by all Tathāgatas, being able to contemplate in such and such a manner.

While engaging in such reflection, one is able to gather and perceive that all phenomena are ultimately unattainable; through the wisdom of skillful means, one practices the dharma of cessation, skillfully knowing the principles of what is to be adopted and what is to be rejected, and attains mastery over both the path of principle and that which is not the path of principle.

Their minds take no pleasure in worldly discourse; they sincerely and diligently cultivate the supramundane scriptures, skillfully seeking all dharmas, and in their quest for all dharmas, they increase their thorough understanding.

Knowing that all phenomena are fundamentally without reality and cannot be apprehended, they neither grasp nor reject anything within the sphere of their practice; liberated from old age and illness, they abide in all meritorious virtues. Having dwelt in spiritual powers since the very beginning, they diligently cultivate the profound Dharma, never regressing from this most profound teaching. They are able to fully penetrate even the most difficult-to-understand teachings and attain the path of the One Vehicle without any doubt.

Regarding the teachings of the Buddha, he attained awakening through his own insight rather than by depending on others; his wisdom was vast and profound like the great ocean, his bodhi was lofty and expansive like Mount Sumeru, and the majestic radiance of his own body surpassed that of the sun and moon.
All contemplation and discernment associated with wisdom are like the Snowy Mountains, their minds pure and white.
Their radiance illuminates boundless merit, and they burn the fuel of afflictions like fire.
Unshaken by good or evil, the mind is ever tranquil and stable like the great earth;

it washes away afflictions and delusions like pure water; the mind has no fixed master like fire; it is unattached to the world like wind; it nurtures all sentient beings like the earth; and it contemplates all worlds like space.

He carries sentient beings like an excellent vehicle; he is unstained by worldly dharmas, comparable to a lotus flower; he proclaims the sound of the Dharma afar like a thunderclap; he rains down all dharmas like a great rain; his light eclipses the worthy and holy ones like that Great Sage; he is well able to subdue others like a great dragon-elephant; he is courageous and fearless like a lion king; he protects and shelters sentient beings like a nyagrodha tree; he is immovable by the arguments of others like the Iron Ring Mountains; and he cultivates immeasurable loving-kindness like the Ganges River.

The King of All Wholesome Dharmas is able to act as a precursor like Mahābrahmā; he is without accumulation like a bird in flight; he subdues the arguments of others like the king of golden-winged garuḍas; and he is rare and difficult to encounter like the udumbara flower.

This supreme person possesses a straightforward mind; being free from indolence, he is able to practice skillfully, possessing skillful certainty regarding all views, and is gentle, patient, and free from envy.
He discusses the Dharma without weariness and seeks the Dharma without fatigue, constantly and diligently expounding it to benefit sentient beings.

His precepts are as pure and transparent as lapis lazuli, both inside and out; he is skilled in hearing all dharmas, regarding them as supreme jewels, and his spoken words cause the multitude to rejoice and submit.
By the power of wisdom, they raise the great Dharma banner, blow the great Dharma conch, and beat the great Dharma drum; they always delight in diligently constructing the symbols of all dharmas.
Through the light of wisdom, their minds are free from delusion; they remain far removed from all faults and are without harm.
With a pure mind free from all defilements, they constantly practice giving and forever abandon stinginess and greed; by nature gentle and mild, they always maintain a sense of shame and remorse.

Their minds are tranquil and stable, their wisdom is clear and discerning; acting as lamps for the world, they shatter the darkness of sentient beings, becoming preeminent fields of merit worthy of receiving offerings and support, and serving as great guides who provide universal relief to all creatures.

Distant from hatred and attachment, with a pure mind free from sorrow, he advances with valor and fearlessness as a great general of the Dharma. Fully understanding the hells, he tames both himself and others; benefiting sentient beings, he extracts all their poisonous arrows. He is the Knower of the World and the Teacher of the World, guiding the masses of living beings to abandon all attachments.

Forever free from the three defilements, they sport with supernatural powers (*abhijñā*). They possess the power of causes, the power of conditions, the power of vows, the power of initiation, the power of the mundane, the power of birth, the power of roots of goodness, the power of *samādhi*, the power of hearing, the power of relinquishment, the power of ethical discipline, the power of patience, the power of diligence, the power of concentration, the power of wisdom, the power of *śamatha*, the power of *vipaśyanā*, the power of supernatural faculties, the power of mindfulness, the power of awakening, and the power to crush all great demonic armies. Furthermore, they possess the power of other dharmas, the power to destroy all enemies that are afflictions, and supreme great power; they are fully endowed with majestic majesty and adorned with the marks and signs of excellence, their wisdom, eloquence, and roots of goodness being perfectly complete.
His eyes were pure, long, and wide, beloved by all people; his body was clean and free from arrogance.

With a heart of deep respect, he served all Buddhas and planted many roots of goodness under them. Having uprooted pride and abandoned greed, hatred, and delusion, he was supremely auspicious and foremost among those worthy of offerings.

Abiding in the realm of supreme wisdom, they radiate brilliant light of insight; their hearts give rise to joy, being heroic and fearless; endowed with both merit and wisdom, they are without obstruction or limitation; they speak only of what they have heard to instruct and reveal to all beings, and they are able to understand and comprehend every dharma they hear.

They courageously and diligently cultivate the factors of enlightenment, constantly abide in emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, as well as in the various samādhis of non-arising and non-ceasing; they traverse all sites of awakening and remain far removed from the realms of the two vehicles.
Ānanda! I have now briefly described how the true merits of the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas born in that realm of Ultimate Bliss are all exactly like this. Ānanda!

Even if my own body were to remain for hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of kalpas, I would be unable to exhaustively proclaim the true merits of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, even with unimpeded eloquence.
"Ānanda! Even those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, throughout the full extent of their lifespans, would be unable to know it.
[The Thirty-fifth Chapter: Sukhāvatī Manifesting Before One] At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
"This is the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha Amitāyus.
You should rise from your seats, join your palms in reverence, and prostrate yourself with your five limbs touching the ground to pay homage to the Buddha."
“The fame of that Buddha fills the ten directions; in each and every direction, the Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges all join in praising him without obstruction or interruption.
At that time, Ānanda rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, joined his palms facing west, prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

I now wish to behold the Tathāgata Amitāyus of the Land of Utmost Bliss, and to make offerings to and serve hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddhas and their assemblies of Bodhisattvas, thereby planting various roots of goodness.
At that time, Amitāyus Buddha immediately emitted a great radiance from the palm of his hand, which shone throughout hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of buddha-fields.

All the mountains—large and small—within those buddha-fields, including the Black Mountains, the Jewel Mountains, Mount Sumeru, Mount Meru, Mount Mahāmeru, Mount Mucilinda, Mount Mahāmucilinda, the Iron Ring Mountains, and the Great Iron Ring Mountains, as well as thickets, groves, gardens, and all palaces, celestial beings, and other such things, were all clearly seen illuminated by the Buddha’s light.
It is, for example, as if a person with the pure divine eye were to observe everything within a distance of one fathom; or as when the sun rises, all things are clearly seen.

In those lands, the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās all see the Tathāgata Amitāyus illuminating the buddha-fields like Mount Sumeru, the King of Mountains. At that time, all those buddha-fields appear as clearly manifest as if they were within a single fathom.
Because the sublime light of the Tathāgata Amitāyus is utterly pure, one beholds that high throne as well as the assembly of śrāvakas, bodhisattvas, and others.
It is like the great earth when it is filled with a flood of water; the forests, mountains, and rivers are all submerged and no longer appear, leaving only the vast expanse of water.
"Thus it is, Ānanda!

In that buddha-field there are no other discourses nor any diverse forms, except for the fathom-wide radiance of all the great śrāvakas and the hundreds of thousands of yojanas of radiance of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas."
The light of that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Amitāyus eclipsed all the śrāvakas and bodhisattvas, enabling all sentient beings to see him clearly.

All the bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, humans, devas, and other assemblies in that Land of Ultimate Bliss behold Śākyamuni Tathāgata in the Sahā world, surrounded by a multitude of bhikṣus as he preaches the Dharma.
Maitreya’s Account of What Was Seen, Chapter Thirty-Six. At that time, the Buddha addressed Maitreya Bodhisattva, saying:
"Do you see the Buddha-land, complete with its pure majesty and adornments, as well as the groves, gardens, springs, and ponds appearing in the sky?"
You see the great earth and all the way up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven adorned with groves of trees scattering flowers in the midst of space.
Furthermore, there are flocks of birds dwelling in the realm of space that produce various sounds, which, like the voice of a Buddha, are heard throughout the world.
"All these birds are merely conjured transformations; they are not actual animals.
Do you see this? Maitreya addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Yes, indeed, I have seen it.
The Buddha again addressed Maitreya Bodhisattva, saying:

“Having seen these sentient beings enter hundreds of thousands of *yojana* palaces, traveling through space without attachment or obstruction, and making offerings to all Buddhas throughout all lands—do you also see those sentient beings maintaining a continuous mindfulness of the Buddha day and night?”
Maitreya replied, "Indeed, I see them all.
The Buddha spoke again:
"Do you see any difference between the enjoyments and requisites of the gods of the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Emanations and those of the people of Sukhāvatī?
Maitreya replied, "I do not perceive even the slightest difference between them."
The Buddha said to Maitreya,
“Do you see anyone in the world of Sukhāvatī dwelling in a womb? Maitreya replied:
“World-Honored One!

It is, for example, like the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the Yāma Heaven, and others, who enter palaces measuring one hundred or five hundred yojanas in extent to sport and enjoy themselves within them.”

I see that those in the world of Sukhāvatī who dwell in the womb do so as if in the palaces of the Yāma Heaven; furthermore, I see sentient beings spontaneously born within lotus flowers, sitting cross-legged.
At the thirty-seventh stage, the period of doubt and regret while dwelling in the womb, Maitreya Bodhisattva again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
For what causes and conditions do the sentient beings in that land have both those born from wombs and those born by transformation?"
The Buddha told Maitreya:

"If there are sentient beings who, having fallen into doubt and regret, nevertheless accumulate roots of goodness and aspire for the Buddha-wisdom, the universal wisdom, the inconceivable wisdom, the unequaled wisdom, the wisdom of majestic virtue, and the vast wisdom."

Because they could not produce faith in their own roots of goodness, for this reason they remained within palaces for five hundred years, neither seeing the Buddha, nor hearing the Dharma, nor seeing the assembly of bodhisattvas and śrāvakas.
If there are sentient beings who have severed doubt and regret, accumulated roots of goodness, and aspire for the Buddha’s wisdom up to the vast wisdom, having faith in their own roots of goodness—
such persons will be born by transformation within a lotus flower, sitting cross-legged, and emerge in an instant.
Just as someone might come from another country, so too it is with this bodhisattva:

having resolved their mind in other lands, they come to be born in Sukhāvatī, where they behold Amitāyus Buddha, serve and make offerings to him, and [behold] the assembly of bodhisattvas and śrāvakas.
Ajita! Behold this person of superior wisdom; by virtue of the power of his vast intelligence, he has undergone transformational birth, sitting cross-legged within a lotus flower.

Observe these inferior beings who, for five hundred years, shall neither see the Buddha nor hear the Dharma, nor see the assembly of Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas; because they do not know the rules of conduct for Bodhisattvas and cannot cultivate various merits, they lack the cause to serve the Buddha Amitāyus.
All these people have fallen into this state because of the doubts and regrets caused by their past conditions.

It is like a Kṣatriya king whose son has committed a crime; he is confined within the inner palace and lodged in a flower-viewing pavilion, where multi-storied towers and ornate halls are exquisitely adorned with rare treasures. Precious curtains and golden beds are layered with thick rugs and cushions, famous flowers are strewn upon the ground, and great precious incense is burned; all necessities for his service and enjoyment are fully provided, yet his two feet are bound with a chain of Jambū-river gold.
The Buddha said to Maitreya:
"What do you think? Does that prince's heart truly delight in this?"
He replied, “No, World-Honored One.”
While bound in confinement, he constantly thought of liberation and sought out his kinsmen, acquaintances, householders, officials, elders, and close ministers.
Although the prince longed for escape, it did not accord with his wishes; only when the Kṣatriya king’s heart was filled with joy did he finally attain release.
The Buddha told Maitreya: “It is so, it is so.

If there are those who fall into doubt and regret, planting various roots of goodness while aspiring for the Buddha’s wisdom and even the vast wisdom, yet they are unable to give rise to faith in their own roots of goodness.”
Because they have given rise to faith upon hearing the Buddha’s name, although they are born in that land, they do not emerge from within the lotus flowers.
Those sentient beings remain within the flower-wombs, perceiving them as if they were garden groves or palaces.
Why is this? Because that realm is pure and free from all defilement and evil; there is nothing therein that is not delightful.

Nevertheless, for five hundred years, those sentient beings do not see a Buddha, do not hear the Dharma, do not see Bodhisattvas or the assembly of Śrāvakas, do not obtain the opportunity to make offerings to or serve the Buddhas, and do not get to inquire about the treasury of the Bodhisattva Dharma.
Having become estranged from all supreme roots of goodness, they find no joy therein and are unable to emerge or cultivate wholesome dharmas;

only after their faults from past lives have been exhausted do they eventually emerge, yet at the time of emergence, their minds are bewildered regarding the zenith, nadir, and the four cardinal directions.

If one remains free from doubt and confusion for five hundred years, one shall immediately make offerings to immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of buddhas and plant immeasurable and boundless roots of goodness.
"You, Ajita! You should know that doubt and uncertainty cause great harm to all bodhisattvas.
At that time, when the thirty-eighth [thought] had arisen, the Bodhisattva Maitreya addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Within this realm, how many bodhisattvas who have not yet regressed shall be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss?
The Buddha told Maitreya:

“In this buddha-field there are seventy-two billion bodhisattvas who, having planted roots of goodness under immeasurable billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of buddhas, have attained non-retrogression and shall be born in that land.”
How much more so for other bodhisattvas who, by means of even small roots of goodness, are born in that land; they are beyond calculation. Ajita!
From the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Duṣprasaha, eighteen hundred million non-retrogressive bodhisattvas shall be born in the world of Sukhāvatī.
In the land of the Buddha Ratnagarbha to the northeast, there shall be nine billion non-retrogressive bodhisattvas who will be born in that realm.
From the land of the Tathāgata Anantaghoṣa, there shall be twenty-two billion non-retrogressive bodhisattvas who will be born in that realm.
From the land of the Tathāgata Prabhāsa, thirty-two billion non-retrogressive bodhisattvas shall be born in that land.
From the land of the Tathāgata Nāgadeva, fourteen billion non-retrogressive bodhisattvas shall be born in that land.
From the land of the Tathāgata Jyeṣṭhadeva, twelve thousand non-retrogressive bodhisattvas shall be born in that land.
From the land of the Tathāgata Siṃha, five hundred non-retrogressive bodhisattvas shall be born in that land.
From the land of the Tathāgata Virajaska, eighty-one billion non-retrogressive bodhisattvas shall be born in that land.
From the land of the Tathāgata Lokendra, sixty billion non-retrogressive bodhisattvas shall be born in that land.
From the land of the Tathāgata Jina-śikharasaṃcaya, sixty billion non-retrogressive bodhisattvas shall be born in that land.
From the land of the Tathāgata Manuṣyarāja, ten koṭis of non-retrogressive bodhisattvas shall be born in that land.

From the land of the Tathāgata Supuṣpa, five hundred bodhisattvas endowed with great diligence have set out upon the Single Vehicle; within seven days, they are able to cause sentient beings to leave behind the cycle of birth and death for hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of kalpas, and they too shall be born in the realm of Sukhāvatī.

From the land of the Tathāgata Prasthita-vīrya, sixty-nine billion non-retrogressive bodhisattvas shall be born in that land; having arrived there, they shall make offerings and pay homage to the Tathāgata Amitāyus and the assembly of bodhisattvas.

Ajita! If I were to describe in detail all the bodhisattvas from the various directions who have been born, are currently being born, or will be born in the realm of Sukhāvatī—those who go there to make offerings, prostrate, and gaze upon the Buddha Amitāyus and his retinue—I could not finish reciting their names even if I spoke for an entire kalpa.
The Thirty-ninth Entrustment to Maitreya: "Ajita!

Behold those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have well obtained benefit; if there be anyone who, upon hearing the name of that Buddha, can give rise to even a single thought of joy and affection, they shall obtain the merits as described above. Their minds will be neither base nor arrogant, and their roots of goodness will all be fully enhanced."
Ajita! For this reason, I declare to you, as well as to the devas, humans, worldly beings, and asuras: I now entrust this Dharma-gate to you.

You should cherish and cultivate it; even for the duration of a single day and night, you should uphold, recite, and maintain it with a heart of aspiration, and explain it to others within the great assembly. You should cause it to be written down and held in hand, and regarding this sutra, you should conceive of it as the Guide.

“Ānanda! For this reason, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who wish to cause immeasurable sentient beings to swiftly and securely abide in non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and who wish to behold those vast adornments, the gathering of supreme buddha-fields, and the perfection of merit, should exert the power of diligence and listen to this dharma-gate.”

Even if one must pass through a great trichiliocosm filled with raging fires, for the sake of seeking the Dharma, one should not give rise to a mind of despondency, flattery, or deceit. One should read, recite, receive, uphold, and copy the sutra scrolls, and even for a mere moment explain them to others, encouraging them to listen without giving rise to anxiety or distress; even if entering a great fire, one should harbor no doubt or regret.
Why is this? Because those immeasurable billions of bodhisattvas all seek this subtle and wondrous Dharma-gate; they listen with reverence and do not give rise to opposition.
Therefore, you all should seek this Dharma. Ajita!

Those sentient beings will obtain great and beneficial merit if, in future ages until the time when the True Dharma perishes, there are those who plant roots of goodness and have already made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas; through the empowerment of that Tathāgata, they shall be able to attain such a vast Dharma gate, which is praised and approved by all Tathāgatas.
If one takes up and maintains those teachings, one shall obtain the vast wisdom of omniscience and plant various roots of goodness according to one’s wishes.

If sons or daughters of good family possess great resolute conviction in those teachings, they shall be able to hear them and attain great joy; they shall take them up, read, recite, and extensively explain them to others, always delighting in their practice.

Ajita! Countless billions of bodhisattvas have sought this Dharma without ever becoming weary or turning away from it. Therefore, you sons and daughters of good family—whether you have already sought, are currently seeking, or will seek this Dharma in the present or future ages—all shall obtain excellent benefit.
“Ajita! That which the Tathāgata ought to do has all been accomplished.

You all should dwell securely in freedom from doubt and plant the roots of all manner of goodness; you should constantly practice and study so as to remain free from hesitation and obstruction, and not enter the prison of the accomplishment of all kinds of precious jewels.”

Ajita! Beings of such great majesty and virtue as these are able to give rise to the various gateways of the vast Buddha-dharma; yet because they have not heard this Dharma, one hundred million bodhisattvas have regressed from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Ajita! It is rare for a Buddha to appear in the world, and it is likewise difficult to obtain a body free from the eight difficulties.

The unsurpassed Dharma of the Buddhas, Tathāgatas—the profound Dharma of the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the unimpededness, and the non-attachment—as well as the bodhisattva dharmas such as the pāramitās, and the person who can explain them, are all difficult to encounter and difficult to reveal.
Ajita! Those who skillfully expound the Dharma are not easily encountered, and times of firm and deep faith are likewise difficult to find.
Therefore, I now proclaim this according to the truth; you should practice it and abide in accordance with these instructions.
“Ānanda! I entrust this Dharma-gate and all the teachings of the Buddhas to you; you should practice them so that they do not perish or disappear.
Such a vast and subtle Dharma-gate is praised by all Buddhas.”
Do not violate the Buddha’s teaching by abandoning it; for that would cause you to obtain what is unwholesome and lead you to sink into the long night, fully beset by manifold perils and sufferings.
Therefore, I now entrust this to you as a great charge: you must ensure that this Dharma remains long and does not perish, and you should diligently practice in accordance with my instruction.
The Fortieth Chapter: Earnest Exhortation through Verse. At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"If one has not previously cultivated merit, One shall never hear this subtle and wondrous Dharma;
Only those who are courageous and capable of accomplishing all wholesome benefits Shall hear such a profound sutra."
That person has once beheld the various World-Honored Ones, Who are able to emit great light to rescue the turbid world;
With vast learning and dhāraṇī-retention like a great ocean, They have attained the hearts of love and joy cherished by the sages and saints.
Those who are indolent, hold wrong views, and are base do not believe in this true Dharma of the Tathāgata;
yet those who have previously planted many roots of merit under the Buddhas are able to cultivate the conduct that saves the world.
Just as one born blind, dwelling perpetually in darkness, cannot guide others along the path;
so it is with the śrāvakas regarding the Buddha’s wisdom—how much less can other sentient beings attain such awakening and understanding?
The Tathāgata’s merits are known only by the Buddha himself; only the World-Honored One can reveal them.
They are beyond the reach of devas, nāgas, and yakṣas, and for those of the two vehicles, they are cut off from all names and words.
If all sentient beings were to become Buddhas, Their conduct surpassing Samantabhadra as they reach the other shore,
And were to expound the merits of a single Buddha Throughout inconceivable eons of time,
Even if their bodies were to pass into parinirvāṇa during that interval, The supreme wisdom of the Buddha could not be measured.
Therefore, by being fully endowed with faith and learning, and through the guidance of virtuous friends,
one hears such profound and wondrous Dharma, and shall obtain the love and respect of all the Noble Ones.
The Tathāgata’s supreme wisdom pervades all space; the meaning of his spoken words is realized only by the Buddha.
Therefore, those wise ones of vast learning should have faith in my teaching as words of truth.
A human body is extremely difficult to obtain; likewise, encountering the appearance of a Tathāgata in the world is rare.
Faith and wisdom are acquired only after a long time; therefore, those who practice should be diligent.
Having heard such a sublime Dharma, they constantly mind the Buddhas and give rise to joy;
those people were truly my friends in the past, for they were well able to delight in the Bodhi of the Buddha.

41. Gaining Benefit from Hearing the Sūtra. At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished speaking this sūtra, twelve thousand nayutas of koṭis of sentient beings among the devas and humans became free from dust and removed from defilement, attaining the pure Dharma-eye;
twenty koṭis of sentient beings attained the fruit of Anāgāmin;
and six thousand eight hundred bhikṣus, having exhausted all outflows, attained liberation of mind.
Four billion bodhisattvas abide in non-retrogression regarding unsurpassed bodhi; donning the great armor, they shall attain perfect enlightenment.
Twenty-five billion sentient beings attain the patience of non-retrogression.

Four hundred trillion nayutas of koṭis of sentient beings, who had never before resolved their minds toward unsurpassed bodhi, now for the first time resolve to plant various roots of goodness, vowing to be born in the world of Ultimate Bliss to behold Amitābha Buddha; all shall be reborn in that Tathāgata’s land and, each in a different direction, successively attain buddhahood under the same name, Wondrous Sound (Ghoṣa).
There were eighty trillion nayutas of sentient beings who, having received the prediction of their attainment of the dharma-patience, achieved unsurpassed bodhi.

These beings, whom the Buddha Amitāyus had previously matured while practicing the bodhisattva path, shall all be born in the World of Ultimate Bliss; they shall remember their former aspirations and vows, and all shall be fully realized.

Forty-second: The Earthquake as an Auspicious Omen. At that time, the trichiliocosm shook in six ways, manifesting various rare and miraculous transformations, and emitting a great radiance that illuminated the world everywhere.

Simultaneously, hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of devas and humans had musical instruments sound of their own accord without being struck, and they rained down *mandārava* flowers that reached up to the knees;
even as far as the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, all performed various kinds of sublime and wondrous offerings.

When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, Maitreya Bodhisattva and the others, as well as the Venerable Ānanda and the entire great assembly, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, were all filled with great joy.
The Great Treasure Accumulation Sutra, Volume Eighteen;
The Great Treasure Accumulation Sutra, Volume Nineteen.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang, by Imperial Decree.
6. The Assembly of Akṣobhya Tathāgata, Part One of Six. Chapter One: The Adornment of Prophecy. Thus have I heard:

At one time the Buddha was staying at Rājagṛha on Vulture Peak Mountain, together with a great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus. All were arhats, renowned among the masses; their outflows were exhausted and they were free from further afflictions. Their minds and wisdom were liberated, sovereign and unimpeded like great dragons; they had accomplished what was to be done and laid down the heavy burden. Having attained their own benefit, they had exhausted all fetters of existence and reached the further shore through the penetration of the True Teaching.
Only Ānanda remained in the stage of training.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed him, saying:
“World-Honored One!

How did the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past set out for anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, practicing universally pure conduct and adorning themselves with the armor of diligence and meritorious qualities?
Because these bodhisattvas have donned this armor, they shall attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
World-Honored One!
May Your Great Compassion reveal and expound upon such practices, vows, and the arousal of the resolve for enlightenment.

"Bhagavān! Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, for the sake of benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to the world of devas and humans, diligently cultivate the practice of universal purity and don the armor of vigor. By means of this, they benefit and bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings, and act as the light of the Buddha-dharma for present and future bodhisattvas, so that their merits may be extolled and their roots of goodness realized."
May all bodhisattvas, having heard this Dharma, diligently practice and study the nature of true thusness (tathatā-dharmatā), and thereby attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The Buddha said:
"Excellent, excellent, Śāriputra!"

It is because you are able to inquire about the vast armor of the light of pure conduct and the proclamation of merits of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past and future, for the sake of gathering in and supporting the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the future.
"Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon this according to the truth;
I shall speak for your sake. Śāriputra said, "So be it, World-Honored One!"
"I wish to hear it with joy.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"From here, passing through a thousand worlds to the east, there is a buddha-field named Abhirati."
In the past, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Viśvabhū appeared there and expounded the subtle and wondrous Dharma for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, beginning with the six pāramitās.
"Śāriputra! At that time, a certain bhikṣu rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and said:
'World-Honored One!'"
"I shall aspire to practice the teachings of the Bodhisattva Dharma as taught by the Buddha. The Buddha said, "Good son!
You should now know that the teaching of the bodhisattva is difficult to practice.
Why is this? Because a bodhisattva does not give rise to thoughts of anger or harm toward sentient beings.
Then that bhikṣu addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

From this day forth, I shall resolve upon the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. With no guile, no deception, truthful speech, and non-contradictory speech, I shall seek the knowledge of all-knowledge until I have attained unsurpassed bodhi. If I should give rise to a mind of anger or malice toward sentient beings, I would thereby be in violation of the present Buddhas, Tathāgatas, who are preaching the Dharma throughout immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless worlds."

"Bhagavān! I now generate this mind of omniscience and dedicate it in this manner; if, in the interim, I should give rise to the mind of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha, I would then be deceiving all the Buddhas."

"Bhagavān! I now generate this mind of omniscience and dedicate it in this way: until I have attained unsurpassed bodhi, if I should give rise toward sentient beings to a mind of desire, hatred, or delusion, or if I should be associated with torpor, arrogance, or remorse, then I would be deceiving all the Buddhas."
“World-Honored One!

I now give rise to this mind of omniscience and dwell in dedication; until I have attained unsurpassed bodhi, if I should give rise to a doubting mind, or if such thoughts as killing or taking what is not given arise, or if I engage in wrong views, unchaste conduct, lying, double-tongued speech, or harsh speech, or if I engage in harmful actions, then I shall be deceiving all the Buddhas.”
"Śāriputra! At that time, there was a certain bhikṣu who had this thought:

'This bodhisattva-mahāsattva, having donned the armor of diligence from the very first production of the thought of awakening, is not shaken by anger or other such afflictions toward any sentient being.'"
"Śāriputra! Because of this thought, that bodhisattva was named 'Aksobhya' (Immovable) in the land of Abhirati.
When the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Viśālanetra saw that the bodhisattva had received the name 'Aksobhya,' he rejoiced and praised him."
When the Four Great Heavenly Kings, Śakra, Brahmā, and the Lord of the World heard his name, they also rejoiced. "Śāriputra!
That Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Acala spoke these words before that Buddha:"
“World-Honored One!

I now give rise to this mind of omniscience and dedicate it thus toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Until I have realized unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, should any of the deeds I practice contradict these words, I would then be deceiving the immeasurable and incalculable Buddhas, Tathāgatas, who dwell and preach the Dharma throughout all worlds.”
World-Honored One!

I now give rise to this great resolve and dedicate it in this manner: until I have realized bodhi, if there is even a single word that is not in accord with mindfulness of the Buddha and omniscience, then I would be deceiving all the Buddhas.

"Bhagavān! If I now dedicate my resolve in this manner, yet fail to realize unsurpassed bodhi and instead remain a householder throughout all future births without ever leaving the home life, I would be in violation of all the Buddhas."
World-Honored One!

I now resolve upon this mind of omniscience; until I have attained unsurpassed bodhi, if in every birth I do not leave the home life, or if I do not practice begging for food, or do not eat in a single sitting, or do not moderate my food intake, or eat a second meal, or do not maintain the three robes, or do not wear rag-robes, or do not sit wherever I happen to be, or do not remain in constant sitting, or do not dwell in an araṇya, or do not reside beneath a tree, or do not sit in the open air, or do not dwell among the tombs, then I would be deceiving all the Buddhas.

"Bhagavān! I now generate this great bodhicitta and dedicate it in this way: until I have attained the knowledge of all modes, if I do not achieve unimpeded eloquence to preach the sublime Dharma, I would be deceiving countless Buddhas."
World-Honored One!

I now resolve my mind in this way: until I have attained unsurpassed bodhi, if I do not abide in three of the modes of deportment—whether standing, sitting, or walking—to do so would be to deceive immeasurable Buddhas.

"Bhagavān! Having now aroused such a mind as described above, until I have attained the knowledge of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), if I should commit a root offense against sentient beings, or utter false speech or other worldly, distracting words, or give rise to a mind intent on refuting the arguments of others, I would then be deceiving countless Buddhas."
World-Honored One!

I have now resolved upon this mind of omniscience and abide in its dedication toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. If, while preaching the Dharma to women, I do not give rise to the marks of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self, but instead grasp at their physical forms and smile with bared teeth, I would be deceiving all the Buddhas.

"Bhagavān! If, having generated this mind of omniscience and abiding in its dedication toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, I should look about or point with restlessness while preaching the Dharma, or should fail to conceive the thought of a Great Teacher upon seeing other bodhisattvas, then I would be deceiving countless Buddhas."
World-Honored One!

Having now resolved upon this mind of omniscience until the attainment of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, if I were to sit and listen to the Dharma or pay homage to non-Buddhist śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas—excluding only the śramaṇa-disciples of the Buddhas—I would be deceiving all the Buddhas.
"World-Honored One!

I have now resolved upon this great mind for the sake of reaching unsurpassed enlightenment. If, while practicing the giving of wealth or the Dharma, my mind harbors distinctions between self and other, or if I harbor a discriminatory mind regarding those who should be honored, I would then be deceiving all the Buddhas."
World-Honored One!

I now resolve upon the mind of omniscience until reaching unsurpassed bodhi; if, upon seeing those who have committed offenses and are about to be punished, I do not sacrifice my own body and life to rescue and protect them, then I would be deceiving all the Buddhas.

"Śāriputra! When that bodhisattva practices this great conduct, until he has realized unsurpassed bodhi, there shall not be a single sentient being who is subjected to punishment and left unprotected."
"Śāriputra! At that time, there was a bhikṣu who thought thus:
'The Tathāgata shall bear witness to this practitioner; those gods, humans, asuras, and others shall also witness it.'"
"Śāriputra! At that time, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Viśālanetra, knowing what was in that bhikṣu’s mind, said to him: 'So it is, so it is.'"
That which has been realized and perceived by the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, is likewise realized and perceived by the worldlings, including gods, humans, and asuras.
"Monks! If there are further bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who don such great armor of diligence and advance toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, they shall all attain unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment."
"Śāriputra! At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Acalo addressed the Buddha, saying:
'World-Honored One!'"

I have now resolved upon this mind of omniscience; until I have realized unsurpassed bodhi, during that interval, if I were to speak of the offenses or transgressions of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās, I would be acting in opposition to all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas.

"Bhagavān! I cultivate this practice, aspiring to attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, so that my buddha-field shall be vast and pure, and all the assembly of śrāvakas therein shall be entirely free from fault."
“World-Honored One!

If, having generated this mind of omniscience, I should not realize unsurpassed bodhi, and were I to give rise to thoughts of desire and experience an emission even in my dreams, I would be in violation of all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas.”
"Bhagavān! May I cultivate this practice to realize unsurpassed awakening, so that the bodhisattvas who have gone forth in that land shall not experience any leakage even in their dreams."

"Bhagavān! If, having resolved upon this mind of omniscience, I should not attain perfect awakening until I have realized unsurpassed bodhi, provided that within my buddha-field there are women who possess the faults of women as found in other lands, may I never attain perfect awakening;
if I were to attain perfect awakening under such conditions, I would be deceiving all the Buddhas."

“Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva achieves these seeds of great vows, they will give rise to such dharmas in accordance with their mindfulness, and will be able to preach various teachings for the sake of sentient beings.”
“Śāriputra! At that time, a bhikṣu addressed the bodhisattva Acalā, saying: ‘O Mahāsattva!’”
"If this sincere mind does not regress and these truthful words are not false, I pray that you will cause the great earth to tremble with a single toe.

At that time, by the power of the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority and the force of his own original vows and roots of goodness, the Bodhisattva Acala caused that great earth to shake in six ways: namely, shaking, great shaking, and universal shaking; trembling, great trembling, and universal trembling.
Śāriputra! That Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Acalo has now fulfilled his former vows.
Therefore, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who wishes to realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment should train in the manner of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Acalo.
If there are bodhisattvas who skillfully cultivate their practice, they shall obtain a buddha-field such as that, and will also be able to swiftly realize anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
when the Bodhisattva Acalo first resolved his mind on enlightenment, how many devaputras gathered for the assembly?”
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
“At that time, all the Four Great Heavenly Kings, Śakra, Māra, and Brahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World, within this trichiliocosm, all joyfully joined their palms and spoke these words:
‘What we have now heard regarding the donning of the armor of merit, we have never heard before.’”
"Bhagavān! When that Bodhisattva Acala attains buddhahood, none of the sentient beings within that land shall achieve accomplishment through inferior roots of goodness."
Śāriputra said to the Buddha,
“World-Honored One!
As the Buddha has described, the merit of the Bodhisattva Acalā’s donning of the armor is something that no other bodhisattvas have ever before possessed.”
The Buddha told Śāriputra: “It is so, it is so.
Among all other bodhisattvas who don the great armor and set out for unsurpassed enlightenment, there is none like the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Acalā.”
Śāriputra! The merits accomplished by that Bodhisattva Acala are such that none among all the bodhisattvas within this Bhadrakalpa possess them. Śāriputra!
At that time, the Tathāgata Viśvabhū bestowed upon the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Acala the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, saying:
"O son of good family!..."

In a future age, you shall attain Buddhahood; your name shall be Akṣobhya Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Worthy One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World-Honored One.
"Just as Dīpaṃkara Buddha bestowed the prediction upon me,
Śāriputra! When the Bodhisattva Acalā received his prediction, a great radiance shone universally throughout the world, and at that time the great earth shook in six ways."
"Just as when I realized all-knowledge in the past, this great trichiliocosm shook in six ways.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, at that time all the herbs, trees,
and forests within the great trichiliocosm leaned toward the Bodhisattva, just as when I realized enlightenment in the past, all grasses and trees inclined toward me."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,

when the Bodhisattva Acala received the Buddha’s prediction, all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas within that great trichiliocosm joined their palms and prostrated themselves before the Bodhisattva."
Just as I have realized great bodhi here, all the devas, nāgas, and others in the Sahā world join their palms and pay homage to me.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

When that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Acala received his prediction of enlightenment, all women who were pregnant in that world gave birth with ease and tranquility, free from all suffering and distress; the blind regained their sight, and the deaf were able to hear.
It shall be exactly as when I attain Buddhahood, without any difference. Furthermore, Śāriputra,

from the time that the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Acalo set out for anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi until the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vipula-locana bestowed upon him the prophecy of enlightenment— at those two times, no sentient beings among them shall die an untimely death.
"It is also no different from when I realized all-knowledge myself.
Furthermore, Śāriputra,
at the time that Bodhisattva Acalo received his prediction, a delightful fragrance pervaded the entire world."
"It is also just as when I formerly realized Great Bodhi; the wondrous fragrance was universally perceived, bringing a sense of satisfaction no different from this.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"That Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Acalo has accomplished such vast merit.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"That Bodhisattva Acalo, having received the prediction from the Buddha, possesses not only these merits, but is also able to reach the further shore of boundless merit."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,

when that Bodhisattva Acalo received the prediction of Buddhahood from the Tathāgata Viśvadarśin, all those in the world of devas, humans, and asuras felt joy and celebration in their hearts, becoming gentle, compliant, and well-disciplined."
It was just as when I realized unsurpassed bodhi, and all the devas and humans alike rejoiced together.
Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when that Bodhisattva Acalā received his prediction, there was a great yakṣa holding a vajra who attended and protected the Bodhisattva, no different from my own [attendants].
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,

when the Bodhisattva Acalā received his prediction from the Buddha, the devas and humans scattered various named flowers, unguents, and powdered incense upon the Bodhisattva, just as they scattered various fragrant flowers when I realized great bodhi."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,

when that Bodhisattva Acalo received his prediction, there were twenty billion devas and humans who each resolved their minds toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and received from the Tathāgata Viśālanetra the prediction of attaining buddhahood."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
