when that Bodhisattva Acala received the prophecy from the Buddha, the earth was completely covered with utpala flowers, padma flowers, and puṇḍarīka flowers."
It was also like the various flowers at my place of enlightenment,
which covered everything. Furthermore, Śāriputra,
when that Bodhisattva Acalo received his prediction of enlightenment, immeasurable devas in the midst of the sky scattered celestial garments over the Bodhisattva and all spoke these words:
"May this bodhisattva swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
This was no different from when, in the past, I attained all-knowledge and the devas scattered their robes.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

When the devas, humans, asuras, and others of that world see the Bodhisattva Acalo receive the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, they all rejoice greatly, even more so than worldly parents upon the birth of a son."
It was just as when I realized all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), and all the devas and humans were filled with great joy.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, by the Buddha’s spiritual power, all the devas and humans in that trichiliocosm heard the Bodhisattva Acalo receive his prediction of enlightenment (*vyākaraṇa*); each offered various kinds of superior garments, famous robes, rare jewels, and exquisite delicacies.
For example, Śāriputra, when a bhikṣu reaches the full moon of the month of Kārttika, all people offer him sustenance.
Likewise, Śāriputra,
when that Bodhisattva Acalā receives his prediction of enlightenment, the sentient beings of the desire realm offer him the finest flavors and play celestial music as an act of worship.
“Śāriputra! Once that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Acalo has received his prediction, he will achieve such meritorious qualities as these.
Then the Venerable Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is truly rare and extraordinary; you have excellently explained that the realm of the Buddhas is inconceivable, as well as the inconceivable realm of such meditative concentrations and the inconceivable realms of the nāgas, and the inconceivable karmic retributions of all actions.”

"Bhagavān! That Bodhisattva Acala, dwelling in his initial resolve, has embraced such supreme merits as to receive the prophecy of a Tathāgata, and has further accomplished these inconceivable great merits."
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"So it is, so it is; it is just as you have said.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda addressed Śāriputra, saying:
“Venerable One!

That bodhisattva who has first resolved his mind upon awakening has donned the armor of diligence; the World-Honored One has briefly described but a small portion of his merit, yet it is still not exhausted. Śāriputra said:
"It is so, it is so; thus has the Tathāgata spoken in brief. Why is this?
Those bodhisattvas, dwelling in their initial resolve and donning the armor of diligence, accomplish inconceivable and immeasurable merit."
Then Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
You have now briefly praised the supreme merit of the Bodhisattva Acalā’s donning of armor and his diligent perseverance.”
“I only pray that the World-Honored One, for the sake of gathering in and sustaining all bodhisattvas of the present and future, will extensively proclaim this.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
“The Bodhisattva Acalā, dwelling in the stage of the first resolve and donning the armor of diligence, possesses such inconceivable merit as this.”
"I shall now explain a small portion of it for you; listen closely, listen closely, and reflect upon it well.
Śāriputra said, "So be it, World-Honored One!"
"I wish to hear it with joy.
The Buddha said,
"That Bodhisattva Acalo made such a vow:”
"Even if space were to undergo change, my great vow would never regress.
By virtue of this aspiration, all the merits of the Bodhisattva Acalā were swiftly accomplished.
Śāriputra! Among all the bodhisattvas in this Bhadrakalpa, I do not see anyone who has donned the armor of diligence like the Bodhisattva Acala. Śāriputra!
The practice cultivated by the Bodhisattva Ratnadhvaja, compared to that of the Bodhisattva Acalā, does not equal even a small fraction of it—not even a *kalā* part.
Śāriputra! Regarding the armor of diligence donned by the Bodhisattva Acalā, there are no bodhisattvas among the immeasurable thousands who can equal him. Śāriputra!
By means of this firm and resolute vow, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Acala realized anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
He now dwells in the world-system Abhirati, where he is known as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Acala.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when that Tathāgata Acalo was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path, there were those who begged for his head, eyes, marrow, brain, hands, feet, limbs, or joints; he never opposed their wishes but gave them all entirely."

Śāriputra! From the time that Tathāgata Acalo first resolved upon awakening until he attained unsurpassed bodhi, by virtue of these causes and conditions, he was free from all combined ailments such as wind, bile, phlegm, and headaches.
Śāriputra! When that Tathāgata Acala was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path, he attained such unprecedented dharmas as these. Śāriputra!

Because he had, in his previous lives throughout all his births, made offerings to and served the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, and constantly practiced the holy life (brahmacarya) in the presence of those Buddhas, by virtue of these causes and conditions, in every place of birth he returned to his original name, Acala. Traveling from one Buddha-field to another, he was born into the world of Buddhas and always beheld the Tathāgatas.

Śāriputra! It is like a consecrated Kṣatriya great king who has attained supreme sovereignty over the world; from one palace to another palace, his feet do not touch the ground as he enjoys the pleasures of the five senses.

When that Bodhisattva Acala formerly practiced the bodhisattva path, in every place where he was born, he constantly cultivated pure conduct and made offerings to the Buddhas. According to the teachings he proclaimed, he instructed, inspired, benefited, and gladdened others; all were in accord with the *pāramitās*, while rarely corresponding to the stage of the *śrāvakas*. He was able to cause all bodhisattvas to enter and abide securely in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Because one has generated this mind for the sake of unsurpassed enlightenment, one obtains these vast merits and benefits.
Furthermore, by dedicating the roots of goodness from this gift of Dharma toward enlightenment, one makes this aspiration:

"May I attain Buddhahood such that all bodhisattvas in that land, through the Buddha’s majestic power, shall hear me preach the Dharma, receive, uphold, read, and recite it; and may they be able to serve various Buddhas and Tathāgatas, traveling from one Buddha-field to another, until they have realized unsurpassed enlightenment, never being separated from the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, just as they are with me."
This is except for the stage of being a successor in the Tuṣita Heaven palace. Why is this?
It is the natural law of all Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that when they descend from the assembly of the Tuṣita Heaven into their mother’s womb and are born from her right side, the great earth trembles.
"Śāriputra! A bodhisattva mahāsattva in their final existence possesses such auspicious signs as these, Śāriputra!"

For example, it is like a bhikṣu endowed with the various supernormal powers (*ṛddhipāda*), who enters a palace as if dwelling in open space; he maintains all the dignified postures (*īryāpatha*) without any obstruction.

A bodhisattva in his final existence is likewise: although he is within the mother’s womb, he dwells in open space, such that no impurities or stains of the womb can defile him, nor does he perceive any foul odors.
Śāriputra! In the past, while practicing the bodhisattva path, that Tathāgata Acala made this vow:
"When I realize unsurpassed bodhi, may all those who practice the bodhisattva vehicle or the śrāvaka vehicle within that buddha-field be severed from all demonic activities."
May all classes of sentient beings, at all times and in every way, never allow the hosts of Māras to find an opportunity against them.

Just as I, while practicing the bodhisattva path, severed all demonic activities, so too may those bodhisattvas, until they have perfected all great merits, always diligently embrace and cultivate the practices for awakening.

"Śāriputra! When that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Akṣobhya was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path, his body and mind did not experience weariness while expounding or listening to the various dharmas."
Why is this? Because when they first resolve their minds and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva, they attain the majestic power of the Dharma-body. Śāriputra!
When the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Akṣobhya was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path, he made this vow:
"May all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in my buddha-field attain the perfection of the dharma-body, no different from my own."
2. The Second Chapter: The Array of Meritorious Qualities of the Buddha-field. At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
As the Buddha has already spoken of all the merits possessed by the Tathāgata Akṣobhya while practicing the bodhisattva path,
I further pray that the World-Honored One will reveal and explain in detail the merits and magnificent adornments of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya’s present buddha-field.

Why is this? It is so that those individuals who practice the Bodhisattva vehicle, upon hearing of those merits, may give rise to a heart of love and joy, desiring to see that Buddha and to pay homage and make offerings to him.

When a person dwelling on the stage of a śrāvaka attains the state of one beyond training (aśaikṣa), upon hearing of the meritorious adornments of that buddha-field, they likewise aspire to behold, pay homage to, make offerings to, and serve it.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
“Excellent, excellent!
It is well that you are now able to inquire about such a meaning.”
"Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon it well; I shall now analyze and explain it for you.
Śāriputra said, "So be it, World-Honored One!"
"I wish to hear it with joy.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

"When that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Akṣobhya realized all-knowledge, he emitted a great radiance that universally illuminated the trichiliocosm, and at that time the great earth shook in six ways."

All sentient beings in that world, knowing that the Tathāgata Acala had realized unsurpassed awakening, for seven days and nights had no thought of food, no thought of hunger or thirst, nor any thought of fatigue, reclining, or sleep; they possessed only thoughts of peace, joy, delight, and a virtuous mind.
At that time, among all sentient beings and the gods of the desire realm within that world, there will be no sexual desire.
Why is this? It is because, through the power of that Tathāgata’s original vows, those sentient beings will, in their present lives, be sustained by these various merits.

Śāriputra! When the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Acalā attained all-knowledge, all sentient beings in that world joined their palms with utmost sincerity toward the Tathāgata Acalā. Because of their yearning for the Tathāgata, they were able to acquire such immeasurable merit in this present life.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
The adornments of merit in that Buddha-world are such that no other immeasurable Buddha-lands can equal them. Śāriputra!"
Because that Tathāgata, while practicing the bodhisattva path, made this great vow, the sublime adornments of this buddha-field are now fulfilled according to my original vow as they are today.

Śāriputra! At the moment, or even within a brief instant, when that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Akṣobhya realized unsurpassed bodhi, all sentient beings within the trichiliocosm—whether they possessed the divine eye or not—all were able to see the Tathāgata Akṣobhya.
“Śāriputra! This, too, is the fulfillment of the Tathāgata’s original vow, whereby all sentient beings are caused to obtain this merit.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!”
When the Tathāgata Akṣobhya sat at the seat of enlightenment and realized unsurpassed awakening, the Māra Pāpīyān did not give rise to any thought of creating obstacles.

Furthermore, countless hundreds of thousands of devas made offerings to the Tathāgata with various fragrant flowers and celestial music; each held fine powdered sandalwood and scattered it over the Buddha.
These fragrant powders and flower garlands merged together in the midst of the sky to form a canopy.
"Śāriputra! All of this is due to the power of the original vows of the Tathāgata Acalo, which have now been fully realized.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!"
When that Buddha attained enlightenment, a great light pervaded the trichiliocosm, such that the radiance of the sun, the moon, and all the devas was completely eclipsed.
This was also due to the fulfillment of the former vows of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, whereby he has now obtained this auspicious omen.
Then Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
When that Tathāgata Akṣobhya formerly practiced the bodhisattva path, he truly possessed the armor of vast and great diligence, enabling him to give rise to such a heart of grand vows.”

"Because he has gone forth to cultivate the bodhisattva practices and vows, he is able to cause countless hundreds of thousands of sentient beings to plant the roots of goodness for unsurpassed enlightenment; furthermore, by dedicating these roots of goodness toward the pure buddha-fields of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, his powers of dedication and aspiration are all completely fulfilled."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

In that buddha-field there is a bodhi tree, formed of the seven precious jewels, one yojana in height. The circumference of its trunk is half a krośa, and its branches and leaves cast a shade extending for one yojana all around. Beneath it is a pedestal four yojanas in circumference, upon which the Buddha sat and realized the path of bodhi."

On all four sides of the Bodhi tree, *tāla* and *sumana* trees were arranged in rows; when stirred by a gentle breeze, they produced a harmonious and elegant sound that no worldly music could surpass.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, within that buddha-field there are no three evil destinies.
What are these three? They are as follows:"
These are the realms of hell, animals, and King Yama.

When all sentient beings accomplish the ten wholesome deeds, the earth becomes as level as the palm of a hand and turns the color of gold; it is free from ditches, pits, thorns, and debris. The ground is as soft as *tūla* cotton; when the foot treads upon it, the earth sinks, and as soon as the foot is lifted, it returns to its original state.
Śāriputra! Within that buddha-field there are no three kinds of diseases.
What are these three?
That is to say, diseases arising from wind, bile, and phlegm.

Śāriputra! In that buddha-field, all sentient beings are free from false speech; they are not ugly, their bodies are free from foul odors, and their greed, hatred, and delusion are all extremely slight. Furthermore, there are no prisons or those bound as prisoners.
Śāriputra! In that buddha-field, there are no followers of external paths or heterodox schools.

All the trees that grow there are constantly laden with flowers and fruit; furthermore, there are extraordinary trees called *kalpa* from which superior garments emerge, complete in all five colors. Their radiant blossoms are fresh and pure, and their extraordinary fragrance is exquisite, remaining forever unchanged at all times.
Just as celestial flowers possess various fragrances, so too does the scent of that robe; the fragrance emitted from the bodies of those who wear it is no different from that of the robe itself.
For example, just as those who are wealthy and prosperous in this world have an abundance of fine garments and enjoy whatever they desire, Śāriputra,

the food and drink required by the sentient beings in that land arrive upon their mere thought— just as it is with the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven— and there is no excrement, urine, filth, or impurity.
Śāriputra! The palaces and towers where those beings dwell are all adorned with the seven precious jewels.
On their four sides there are many ponds and pools, filled with water of eight meritorious qualities for enjoyment according to one's heart's desire.
The parks and gardens are numerous and all are utterly pure.
The various classes of sentient beings dwell there mostly in the joy of the Dharma. Śāriputra!

The people of that land are free from envy; all its women surpass the various precious goddesses, having attained celestial virtues with which none can compare. Even if one were to attempt a comparison, they would not equal even a hundredth part, a thousandth part, a hundred-thousandth part, nor even a hundred-thousand-koṭi-nayuta-fold part—nor even a fraction as minute as an *upaniṣad* (a part of a part).

Śāriputra! The people of that land, according to their karmic retributions, experience various couches and seats, all made of the seven treasures, magnificent and complete in every detail; for their reclining, they use pillows of tūla-cotton.
All of this is due to the power of the vows made by the Tathāgata Akṣobhya in the past, which have brought about such various kinds of magnificent adornments.
Śāriputra! The food and drink provided for the people in that land, including their color, fragrance, and flavor, are no different from those of the devas.
Just as the people of Uttarakuru have no separate king, so too it is in that Land of Wonderful Joy; there is only the Tathāgata Acala who serves as the sovereign of the Dharma.
Furthermore, just as the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven serve Śakra, so too do all those people serve the Tathāgata. Śāriputra,
you should know the meritorious adornments of that buddha-field of Akṣobhya.
Śāriputra! The sentient beings in that land have no heedlessness in their minds. Why is this?
"This is also due to the power of the original vow of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya.
At that time, a certain bhikṣu, having heard the Buddha praise the merits of the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, conceived a mind of greedy attachment and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"I now vow to be born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya.
The Buddha told the bhikṣu,
"How could you, being so foolish and deluded, be born there?"
Why is this? It is not by a mind of attachment that one attains rebirth there; rather, it is only by planting the roots of all virtues and cultivating all pure practices that one can be born there.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

According to the inclinations of the sentient beings in that land, there appear pure ponds at their mere thought; they are filled with water possessing the eight meritorious qualities, such that drinking, rinsing, and bathing all accord with human desires.
To those who do not delight in them, these ponds do not appear."

Śāriputra! In that buddha-field, the fragrant winds are harmonious and pleasant, gladdening the hearts of all beings; these fragrant winds perform various functions of fragrance for the devas and humans, conforming to their inclinations, reaching some and not others.
Śāriputra! All of this is due to the power of the original vows of the Tathāgata Acalā and his adornment of merit.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!
In that buddha-field, the clothing and ornaments of women grow from trees and are enjoyed according to their wishes.
The women of that land are free from the faults of women; they do not possess the many jealousies, double-tongued speech, or harsh words found among the women of this world.
Furthermore, from the time of conception until birth, both mother and child remain at ease and free from impurity.
Why is this? It is entirely due to the power of the original vows of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya.
Śāriputra! In that buddha-field there are such things as peace, security, and happiness. Śāriputra!
In that buddha-field of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Akṣobhya, there are no markets, no merchants, and no agricultural labor; it is always filled with happiness.
Śāriputra! In that buddha-field, there is singing and play, yet it is devoid of anything associated with lust; those people experience only the joy of the Dharma. Śāriputra!

In that buddha-field, all the sumanas trees and tala trees stand in rows; when stirred by a gentle breeze, they produce harmonious and elegant sounds such that even the music of devas and humans cannot equal that of those trees.

Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to encompass a buddha-field, they should embrace such merits and purify the buddha-land, just as the Tathāgata Akṣobhya embraced the adornments of his buddha-field while practicing the bodhisattva path.
Śāriputra! In that buddha-field there is no darkness; although the sun and moon exist, they do not manifest their radiance. Why is this?
Because the Tathāgata Akṣobhya constantly possesses radiance that universally illumines the Buddha-field.

Śāriputra, it is like a tall and grand multi-storied pavilion with its doors and windows tightly closed; if a maṇi jewel is placed within the chamber, the sentient beings inside will constantly behold its brilliant light throughout both day and night.
The various classes of sentient beings within that buddha-field who behold the light of the Tathāgata are likewise so.
Śāriputra, as for this great multi-storied pavilion, it is the world of Abhirati in that direction.
The maṇi jewel represents the Tathāgata Akṣobhya;
the light of the maṇi jewel represents the Buddha’s radiance;
and the sentient beings within the pavilion represent the various living beings in that wondrous land.

Śāriputra! Wherever the Tathāgata Akṣobhya goes or stays, there are thousand-petaled lotuses that naturally appear to receive his feet; these flowers are golden in color, beyond all worldly comparison.
"Śāriputra! This, too, is accomplished through the extraordinary power of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Acalamati.
Then Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
When that Tathāgata Acala enters a room, will golden lotuses serve as a footstool for him?
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"This matter is trivial; why do you take such pains to inquire about it?
Whenever that Buddha, the World-Honored One, enters a village or a private residence, those thousand-petaled flowers immediately appear accordingly."
If there are good men or good women who think thus:
"If the Tathāgata were to deign to enter this room, lotus flowers should gather beneath his feet in one place."
According to their thoughts, the flowers would gather together.
If there were another person who wished for the flowers to remain in the air, they would immediately abide in the air just as they had thought,
by virtue of that Tathāgata’s majestic spiritual power.
Śāriputra! Those people will treat that lotus flower upon which [the Buddha] stands as a stūpa for worship. Śāriputra!
For the sake of expounding the Dharma, that Buddha, the World-Honored One, travels throughout the trichiliocosm; wherever he goes, these flowers immediately appear.
Furthermore, wherever the Tathāgata manifests transformations in other buddha-fields, these golden flowers likewise appear there as well.
By the Buddha’s majestic power, the entire trichiliocosm was adorned with golden thousand-petaled lotuses.
Chapter Three: The Assembly of Śrāvakas. "Furthermore, Śāriputra!"

When that Tathāgata Akṣobhya teaches the Dharma, he is able to skillfully subdue immeasurable sentient beings, causing them all to realize the fruit of arhatship for themselves; those who dwell in meditative concentration and the eight liberations are exceedingly numerous.

"Śāriputra! That Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Acalo has an immeasurable and innumerable assembly of śrāvakas; I do not see any master of calculation or his disciple who could calculate that assembly of śrāvakas by such numbers as *vibhava*, *gaṅgā*, *padma*, *araba*, *arbuda*, or *abuda*. Śāriputra!"
No one is able to calculate or determine the number of those śrāvakas by name. Śāriputra,

just as there is no count of the sons of good family in this land of mine who have attained the fruit of srotāpanna, sakṛdāgāmin, or anāgāmin, so too is it with those who realize arhatship in that land.

Śāriputra! For example, suppose there is a lazy stream-enterer who undergoes seven more births; only after preaching the Dharma for him does he attain the supreme fruit. I call such a person a "seven-times-born" individual.

Śāriputra! If there are those who, during the Tathāgata Acalita’s first teaching of the Dharma, attain the fruit of a stream-enterer; at the second teaching, realize the stage of a once-returner; at the third teaching, realize the stage of a non-returner; and at the fourth teaching, realize arhatship—these people are not called "lazy," for they have exhausted all outflows (āsrava) within a single sitting.
Śāriputra! Those who attain the fruit of stream-entry within that buddha-field achieve the exhaustion of outflows in this very body; they do not have to undergo seven more births as in this world.

One who is a Sakṛdāgāmin is able to reach the end of suffering within this very life; it is not that one is called a Sakṛdāgāmin merely because they undergo one more round of coming and going in this realm.
One who is an Anāgāmin achieves Arhatship in that same body; it is not that one is called an Anāgāmin merely because they have been born in a higher plane and do not return here.
Śāriputra! In that land, the Tathāgata Acalā teaches the distinctions among the stages and practices of the śrāvakas, even establishing such noble fruits.

If a son or daughter of good family can understand this Dharma, they will not abide in the various consciousnesses nor in the stage of training; rather, upon the passing away of the body, they will abide in the stage of no-more-learning and there attain parinirvāṇa.

Śāriputra! The stage of one beyond training (*aśaikṣabhūmi*) is a conventional designation established for the stage of an arhat; to speak of "one beyond training" is a conventional designation established for an arhat.
Śāriputra! The assembly of śrāvakas of that Tathāgata Acalo is pure, fully endowed [with virtues], and dwells in firm stability. Śāriputra!

These are the provisional designations established for the assembly of śrāvakas of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya; that is to say, the great arhats whose outflows are exhausted, who have accomplished what was to be done, laid down the heavy burden, attained their own benefit, and through the complete destruction of the fetters of existence, are liberated by perfect knowledge.
These arhats mostly dwell within the eight liberations of meditative concentration. Śāriputra,
that Tathāgata Acalo has such a community of śrāvakas, adorned with the perfection of merit.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
In that buddha-field, there are stairways made of the three treasures—gold, silver, and lapis lazuli—that extend from Jambudvīpa up to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven."

Śāriputra, if the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven desire to see the Tathāgata Acalā, pay him homage, and make offerings to him, those hosts of devas descend by means of jeweled stairways to the place where the Buddha is.
At that time, those devas, seeing that the people of Jambudvīpa were prosperous and fully endowed with wealth, conceived a sense of affection and delight, saying:
"We devas possess the karmic rewards of celestial fortune, while those people of Jambudvīpa possess the karmic rewards of human fortune."

"The superior merit I now behold is no different from my own; yet, there is another merit in Jambudvīpa that surpasses even that of the heavens—namely, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya’s exposition of the True Dharma."
"For this reason, the hosts of devas always delight in the human realm.
Śāriputra, if people of Jambudvīpa were to ascend to heaven, they would have no desire or pleasure there at all."
For what reason?
Although the Tathāgata Acala dwells among humans, constantly expounding the True Dharma for our benefit, my own karmic reward is no different from that of the devas.
Therefore, it is beyond the reach of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.
Śāriputra! By the Buddha’s spiritual power, the humans and devas of that realm are able to see one another, just as the people of Jambudvīpa in this realm see the stars and the moon, Śāriputra!
In the same way, those multitudes of people look up at the celestial palaces of the higher realms.
Śāriputra, this too is the fulfillment of the power of the vows made by the Tathāgata Acalo when he was originally practicing the bodhisattva path.
Śāriputra! The sound of that Buddha’s preaching of the Dharma pervades the entire trichiliocosm, such that there is no gap or vacancy among the fourfold assembly listening to the Dharma. Śāriputra!
That assembly of śrāvakas aspired solely for the food of the Dharma, having no thought of any other sustenance.
When listening to the Dharma, they were single-mindedly tranquil; whether sitting or standing, their bodies and minds remained free from weariness.

Śāriputra! The Tathāgata Acalā resides in mid-air preaching the Dharma for the assembly. Whether those in his śrāvaka community have attained supernormal powers or not, through the Buddha’s majestic power they all abide in mid-air and listen to the essential points of the Dharma while maintaining the three modes of deportment.
What are these three?
They are walking, standing, and sitting.
When those of the śrāvaka class desire nirvāṇa, they enter parinirvāṇa while sitting in the full lotus posture (paryaṅka), at which time the great earth trembles for their sake.
Once they had entered parinirvāṇa, all devas and humans came to make offerings to them.
Some arhats, being about to enter parinirvāṇa, emitted fire from their bodies to cremate themselves;
others vanished spontaneously without leaving any relics behind.
Some, at the time of their parinirvāṇa, travel through the air like five-colored clouds, vanishing in an instant without leaving a trace;
others abide in space like falling rain that, upon reaching the ground, is completely exhausted and disappears.
Śāriputra! This is because when the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Akṣobhya was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path, he made this vow:
"If I attain unsurpassed bodhi, may all my śrāvaka disciples enter parinirvāṇa by means of three modes of deportment."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
In that Buddha-land, the many śrāvakas who have attained the four fearlessnesses and those who have acquired the four bases of supernormal power are even more numerous than this."
"Śāriputra! The assembly of śrāvakas in that buddha-field has accomplished such fully endowed merit.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The assembly of śrāvakas of that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Akṣobhya has achieved a magnificent and vast abundance of merit.
— *Mahāratnakūṭa Sūtra*, Scroll 19.
The Great Treasure Accumulation Sūtra, Volume Twenty, translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of the Great Tang, by Imperial Decree.
Chapter Four: The Assembly of Bodhisattvas; Part Two of the Sixth Section: The Assembly of Akṣobhya Tathāgata. Chapter Four: The Assembly of Bodhisattvas.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra had this thought:
“The World-Honored One has now already spoken of the merits of the śrāvakas; I further pray that he will speak of the merits possessed by the bodhisattvas.”
"Why is this? Because all merits are born from this.
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing what he was thinking, addressed Śāriputra:
"In that buddha-field, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of bodhisattvas have all gathered together.
All those bodhisattvas who have left the household life are able, through the Buddha’s spiritual power, to comprehend, receive, uphold, read, and recite whatever they hear."

Śāriputra! The Dharma I have taught in this world-system is extremely limited; compared to the treasury of Dharma taught by the Tathāgata Acalo, it does not approach even a hundredth part, a thousandth part, a hundred-thousandth part, a ten-million-hundred-thousandth part, nor any part calculable by calculation, number, kalā, or upaniṣad.
Śāriputra! All of this results from the vows made by the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Akṣobhya while he was practicing the bodhisattva path:
"May it be that when I attain buddhahood, all the bodhisattvas in that buddha-field, through my majestic power, shall be able to comprehend, receive, uphold, read, and recite whatever they hear."
"Śāriputra! By virtue of the power of that Tathāgata’s original vows, these bodhisattvas are able to receive, recite, and master everything they hear from the Buddha."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, if that bodhisattva wishes in his own mind to go to another buddha-field, he arrives there as soon as he raises his thought; his appearance, dress, and speech harmonize well with the local customs."
Having paid homage and made offerings to that Tathāgata, heard the True Dharma, and engaged in skillful inquiry, they returned to the presence of the Buddha once their tasks were complete. Śāriputra!

Within this Bhadrakalpa, nine hundred and ninety-six Buddhas shall appear in the world; if there are bodhisattvas who wish to behold these Tathāgatas, they should aspire to be born in that Akṣobhya Buddha-field.

Śāriputra! If any son or daughter of good family, after passing away from this buddha-field or any other buddha-field, has been born, is now being born, or will be born in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Acalā, they will certainly not believe in or abide in the stages of the śrāvakas.

Why is this? Because those who practice the Buddha-way constantly encounter the Tathāgata; Māra, the Evil One, finds no opportunity against them; they forever sever the continuity [of afflictions] within the stages of the two vehicles; they are certain to attain unsurpassed bodhi; and they always abide in the great assemblies of the Tathāgatas.

Śāriputra! You should know that those sentient beings who dwell in the pure buddha-field of the Tathāgata Acalā will never fall back; they cannot be led away nor can they retreat. Abiding in unsurpassed bodhi, they possess great power that cannot be shaken, and they shall never again regress.

Śāriputra! If there are good men or good women in this world or in other worlds who, after their lives have ended, are reborn in that land, at the very moment of birth they will attain such a thought:
"I have already entered the Tathāgata’s chamber and am dwelling in the city of fearlessness."
"Śāriputra! All the discourses of those bodhisattvas are in accord with the prajñāpāramitā; they honor one another and regard each other as spiritual teachers."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Among the assembly of bodhisattvas in that buddha-field, those who are householders are few and those who have left the home life are many; all of them, through the Buddha’s spiritual power, are able to comprehend, receive, uphold, and recite whatever they hear."

Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva living at home does not fix their attention [on it], yet wherever they may be within a Dharma assembly—whether sitting or standing—they are able, through the Buddha’s spiritual power, to hear, comprehend, receive, uphold, recite, and master it thoroughly.
The renunciant bodhisattva is also like this: even when in different regions, there is no difference in their recitation and chanting.

These bodhisattvas do not forget or lose what they have heard throughout the process of casting off one body and receiving another, and they take birth in various buddha-fields according to their vows.
Śāriputra! That, too, is adorned by the merit of the original vows of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya. Śāriputra!

If a bodhisattva wishes, within a single lifetime, to behold immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddhas, they should aspire to be born in the realm of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya.

Once the Bodhisattva has been born there, he immediately beholds immeasurable Buddhas and plants various roots of goodness; furthermore, he is able to expound the essential teachings of the Dharma for countless hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, causing all those beings to increase their roots of goodness.

Śāriputra, when the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, are to appear in this Bhadrakalpa, if bodhisattvas provide the Tathāgatas with offerings of clothing, food and drink, bedding, medicine, and various other requisites, they shall immediately leave the household life.
Having already gone forth, he purified the holy life (brahmacarya) in the presence of various Buddhas.

By virtue of these roots of goodness, compared to other bodhisattvas who, in a single lifetime, were in correspondence with the perfections (pāramitā) in the presence of the Tathāgata Acalo, this mass of merit does not equal even one hundredth part, nor one thousandth part; it cannot be reached by any calculation, fraction, number, analogy, or even by the smallest possible proportion (upaniṣad).
Śāriputra! This, too, is the adornment of the merits of the pure buddha-field of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya. Śāriputra!

If there are bodhisattvas who, after the end of their lives in this world or from other worlds, have been born, are currently being born, or will be born in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, they shall all attain the stage of non-retrogression.
Why is this? Because in that buddha-field, the celestial Māra Pāpīyān does not create obstacles, nor is there any affliction by the works of Māra. Śāriputra!
For example, it is like a venomous snake that, being subdued by a divine mantra, can no longer cause harm; even when all other insects see that venomous snake, they feel no anxiety or fear.
Nevertheless, although this snake no longer possesses the power to inflict poison, it is still called a "venomous snake" because it received this serpent body due to its past karma.
Śāriputra! It is the same with that Māra Pāpīyān. When the Tathāgata Akṣobhya was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path, he dedicated his roots of goodness through such a vow:

"May I, upon realizing unsurpassed bodhi, subdue all māras so that they do not create obstacles or afflictions; and may those bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, ordinary beings, and even the entire trichiliocosm likewise not be obstructed or afflicted."

"However, having received this demonic body as the result of past karma, he was born among those devas and felt self-reproach; because of his beginningless karmic deeds, he obtained this name for such a body, and though he attained mastery over it, he constantly felt weary and disgusted by it."

When that Tathāgata was preaching the Dharma, the retinues of the Māras would constantly attend his teachings; having heard them, their minds became pure, and they conceived a deep affection for the assembly of śrāvakas, thinking:
"How might we come to abide in tranquility, possessing few desires and being content?"
Because those hosts of Māras constantly give rise to the aspiration for renunciation and harbor no thoughts of obstruction,
the śrāvakas, bodhisattvas, and ordinary beings in that land all dwell in peace and happiness through the power of that Buddha’s past diligent efforts and great vows.
“Śāriputra! This, too, is the sublime adornment of Akṣobhya Buddha’s buddha-field.
Then Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If there are good sons or good daughters who fill a trichiliocosm with the seven treasures and offer them as alms, vowing to be born in that land;”

By virtue of these practices and vows, this son or daughter of good family shall never again fall back into the stages of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas. From one buddha-field to another, they will successively serve and make offerings to all the Tathāgatas, hearing the True Dharma in the presence of those Buddhas. Although they have not yet realized unsurpassed bodhi, they will be able to behold immeasurable hundreds, thousands, even up to hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Buddhas, planting various roots of goodness in the presence of those Buddhas.
World-Honored One!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family, by means of this skillful method, takes seven treasures filling a trichiliocosm and offers them as a gift, they shall, through this virtuous relinquishment, be reborn in that land.
The Buddha told Śāriputra: “So it is, so it is.
They are born well and go well; such bodhisattva-mahāsattvas fill that buddha-field.”

Śāriputra! It is like gold ore that, through intensive smelting and refining, has its grit and gravel removed until only pure gold remains, which is then fashioned into various ornaments and articles for adorning the body.
Śāriputra! The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwelling in that buddha-field abide in reality in exactly this same way.
Furthermore, you should now know of the pure assembly of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
all the bodhisattvas in that buddha-field— whether those who have already been born, those currently being born, or those yet to be born— all such bodhisattvas practice a single way."
This is what is called abiding in the conduct of a Tathāgata. Śāriputra,
what is the conduct of a Tathāgata?
This refers to transcending the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
To speak of "practicing a single practice" is merely a provisional designation. Therefore, Śāriputra!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva delights in practicing a single path, they should aspire to be born in that buddha-field. Śāriputra,
those bodhisattva mahāsattvas whom I have prophesied as being non-retrogressive should be born in the presence of the Buddha Akṣobhya.
Śāriputra! Those bodhisattvas who are born in that buddha-field, I shall not abandon or forsake.
It is, for example, like a Kṣatriya anointed great king when an enemy nation comes wishing to invade his wealth and domain.
Having heard this, the king reflected:

"My queens, beloved sons, and all my treasures shall be withdrawn into the inner palace so that they cannot be harmed by enemies; thus the king’s realm will remain peaceful and free from peril, his majesty will awe his powerful adversaries, and he need no longer fear calamities."

"Śāriputra! My not abandoning or forsaking the bodhisattvas is likewise so; those who practice the bodhisattva path should understand it in this way, just as that king [cherished] his precious possessions, beloved son, and queen."

In that buddha-field there is no fear, just as in a royal palace; the enemy king is none other than Māra Pāpīyān, who diligently creates obstacles for the practitioner of the bodhisattva path, yet he cannot harass or disturb them, just as a consecrated great king is not invaded or disturbed by his enemies.
The Tathāgata is also like this, not being disturbed or troubled by the celestial Māras. Śāriputra!
It is, for example, as if there were a person who, fearing his creditors, traveled far to a borderland, where he could no longer be seized or plundered by those creditors or others.
Why is this? Because the road is distant, perilous, and impassable, the creditors and their families cannot reach that place.
It is just the same for Māra Pāpīyān; the path to those bodhisattvas who have been born in the Land of Wonderful Joy is likewise cut off.
Śāriputra! In this trichiliocosm, the celestial Māra Pāpīyān constantly creates various obstacles for bodhisattvas and śrāvakas.

However, the hosts of celestial Māras in the land of Abhirati do not perform the deeds of Māra; those bodhisattvas there—whether already born, currently being born, or yet to be born—are forever free from fear.
Why is this? Because when that Tathāgata was practicing the bodhisattva path in the past, he dedicated all his roots of goodness in this way:
"When I realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, may those hosts of celestial Māras not create obstacles or disturbances, nor perform the works of Māra."
"Śāriputra! It is just as when a man successfully takes a potent poison and is able to digest it; only then does it become food for his meal, devoid of all toxicity.
The devas and māras of that land are likewise: they constantly bestow benefit and do not cause harm."
"Śāriputra, that buddha-field is endowed with such immeasurable merits.
At that time, Śāriputra thought to himself:
"I now wish to see that buddha-world of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Acala, as well as his assembly of śrāvakas."
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the thoughts in Śāriputra’s mind, used his supernormal power to cause them all to see [the assembly] without rising from his seat.
He addressed Śāriputra, saying:
“Do you see them now?”
He replied, “I have seen them.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
"Do you see any slight signs of superiority or inferiority, or any distinct differences among those devas and humans? He replied, "I do not."
Why is this? I see that the clothing, food, drink, and various precious playthings of the people in Abhirati are all like the articles of pleasure belonging to the devas.

That Tathāgata Acala sits amidst the assembly preaching the Dharma, appearing like a mountain of gold with a brilliant and magnificent radiance, surrounded by an immeasurable and boundless multitude of śrāvakas.
It is like a person traveling upon the great ocean; as they look in the four directions from midstream, they cannot discern the shore. The observation of these śrāvakas is likewise.

These śrāvakas, according to the Dharma they hear, remain unmoving in body and mind as if they had entered meditative absorption (*dhyāna*); they are not like those who have entered absorption in this world, who may occasionally shift or waver.

"Bhagavān! If a son or daughter of good family were to fill a trichiliocosm with the seven treasures and offer them as a gift, by virtue of such noble renunciation, those bodhisattvas would successfully attain rebirth in the world of Abhirati."
Why is this? Because they, too, have thus attained non-retrogression,
World-Honored One!

It is like a king’s messenger traveling far to another country; carrying his official seal and credentials, he passes through various checkpoints and barriers without being able to be obstructed by the officials there. Why is this?
Just as no one can obstruct a person by the power of a king’s seal, so it is with those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas:

whether they have already been born, are currently being born, or will be born in that buddha-field after their lives end in this world or another world, they shall all never regress from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. From one buddha-field to another, they shall never be separated from the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and they shall all swiftly realize unsurpassed enlightenment.
Then Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas born in that realm are no different from those who have attained the fruit of a stream-enterer (srotāpanna) in this world.”

Why is this? Just as those who have attained the fruit of a stream-enterer do not fall into the evil destinies, so too those Bodhisattvas in that realm—whether already born, currently being born, or yet to be born—all sever the evil destinies as well as the stages of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas. Until they realize unsurpassed bodhi, they travel from one Buddha-field to another, never being separated from the Buddhas and their assemblies of Śrāvakas.
The Buddha told Śāriputra: “It is so, it is so.

These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, having been born in that land, do not fall to the level of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas; until they have realized unsurpassed bodhi, they shall go from one buddha-field to another, always obtaining the opportunity to make offerings to the Buddhas in their presence, and they shall eventually realize the fruit of a Buddha’s bodhi.”

Śāriputra! Just as one who has attained the fruit of a stream-enterer (srotāpanna) is certain to attain the enlightenment of a śrāvaka and will never fall into the evil destinies, so too it is with these bodhisattvas.

Whether from this world or another, after their lives have ended, they will be reborn in those lands; they are all certain to realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi). From one buddha-field to another, they shall never be separated from unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment in the presence of the Buddhas.
Then Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

All those in this world who are candidates for the fruit of once-returning and those who have attained the fruit of once-returning, up to those dwelling as candidates for arhatship and those who have attained the fruit of arhatship, are no different from the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas born in that buddha-field.”
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"Do not speak such words. Why is this?"
In this buddha-field, those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have received the prediction of Buddhahood are no different from those bodhisattvas born there.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!
The bodhisattvas who sit at the site of enlightenment in this world are no different from those bodhisattvas born there. Why is this?

Those bodhisattvas practice the conduct of the Tathāgatas; they do not provide an opportunity for the celestial Māras to gain an advantage; they have forever severed the continuity [of afflictions] within the stages of the two vehicles; they travel from one buddha-field to another, constantly able to make offerings to all Tathāgatas, until they attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
At that time, Ānanda had this thought:
"I should now examine the power of the elder Subhūti’s eloquence.
Having had this thought, he addressed Subhūti, saying:
"We should now behold the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, his assembly of śrāvakas,
and that buddha-field. Then Subhūti said to Ānanda,
"If you wish to see that Tathāgata, you should for now look toward the zenith."
At that time, Ānanda, having observed the zenith, said to Subhūti:
"I have observed the zenith to its utmost extent, and it is entirely empty and tranquil. Subhūti said:
“The assembly of śrāvakas of that Tathāgata Akṣobhya, as well as his buddha-field, are likewise just as they are seen above.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
As the Buddha has taught, there is no difference between a bodhisattva who receives a prediction in this life and one who is born as such.
World-Honored One!
I do not now know by what they are equal.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
“Because the dharma-realm is equal, there is no difference.
Chapter Five: The Merits of Nirvāṇa At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra again had this thought:

“The World-Honored One has already spoken of the boundless merit of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Akṣobhya’s cultivation of the bodhisattva path, and has further described the vast adornments of the sublime virtues and deeds of the śrāvakas and bodhisattvas in that land.”
"Furthermore, I pray that the World-Honored One will now reveal how that Buddha’s traces of passing into nirvana and his transformative deeds were manifested.
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing what was in Śāriputra’s mind, addressed him, saying: "Śāriputra!"

On the day of the Parinirvāṇa of Tathāgata Akṣobhya, his emanation bodies will be distributed throughout all worlds, preaching the sublime Dharma within the hells. By means of this Dharma, they will subdue immeasurable sentient beings, all of whom shall realize the fruit of Arhatship; yet it is only at this moment that they attain the fruit and enter parinirvāṇa, while those who had previously realized the state of No-more-learning increase in number.
On that very day, he bestowed a prediction upon the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gandhahastin, saying:
"After my parinirvāṇa, you shall attain Buddhahood, and your name shall be Suvarṇapadma Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
The number of śrāvaka disciples in the buddha-field of that Tathāgata Suvarṇapadma is equal to that of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, without any difference."

Furthermore, Śāriputra, when the Tathāgata Acalā enters parinirvāṇa, at that time the great earth will tremble everywhere; the entire trichiliocosm will roar and resound, and its sound will penetrate upward as far as the Akaniṣṭha Heaven. Having heard it, the devas will immediately know that that Buddha has entered nirvāṇa.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
All the groves and medicinal herbs within that buddha-field incline toward the place where Acalanātha Tathāgata entered parinirvāṇa."

At that time, the devas and humans all scattered flower garlands, various incenses, and robes over the Buddha; the incense and flowers thus scattered formed a circular perimeter one yojana high surrounding him.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

At the time of that parinirvāṇa, all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and so forth, throughout this trichiliocosm, will all turn toward the Tathāgata Acalo, join their palms, and pay him homage.
By the Buddha’s spiritual power, the devas from other realms were all able to see him enter parinirvāṇa.

For seven days and nights, these devas and humans were filled with grief and distress; they no longer took pleasure in the amusements and delights of gods or men, nor did they harbor any thoughts of desire.
They said to one another, "The Tathāgata Acalo was the light of the world and the eye of sentient beings; how swift is his passing into extinction!"

“Śāriputra! If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, from this world or from other worlds, are reborn in that buddha-field after their lives end, or are born there in the present, they all receive the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. They cannot be counted by hundreds; they are numbered by thousands and hundreds of thousands.”

Śāriputra! You should know that those who are numbered among these hundreds of thousands of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have entered the number of the Tathāgatas and have all entered the number of Buddhas; having entered the number of Buddhas, they have entered the number of the nature of omniscience.
Śāriputra, if there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are to be born in that land, they too shall all enter the number of those equal to the Tathāgata,
with the exception of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are non-retrogressive.
As for the remaining bodhisattvas in this world, if they do not hear this Dharma-gate that extols the merits of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, they are all under the influence of Māra.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
after the Parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata Acalā, until the True Dharma remains in the world, those Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas born within that Buddha-field shall also be included in this number."
Why is this? It is due to the power of that Tathāgata’s original vows.

If these bodhisattvas are to take birth there at a later time, they should recite and chant one hundred and eight dharma-gates; only after having recited them will they be able to uphold all those dharmas.

The essential nature of the one hundred and eight Dharma gates established by the Tathāgata Akṣobhya shall be such that, after my parinirvāṇa, any bodhisattva mahāsattva who is born in that land shall likewise recite these one hundred and eight Dharma gates and be able to receive and uphold all Dharma gates.

Śāriputra! The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Acalā has skillfully sustained all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; although the Buddha has entered parinirvāṇa, the sound of his preaching and his adorned merits are no different from when the Buddha was in the world.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Akṣobhya emitted fire from his body and performed his own cremation; the remains of his physical relics were all made of golden color."
For example, wherever a *dīpila* tree is cut, the mark of the *svastika* (the "myriad-sound" character) appears; the relics of the Tathāgata are likewise.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!
All the relics of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya are perfectly round and complete; both their inner and outer surfaces bear auspicious signs and patterns, the forms of which are as follows: the svastika.
Śāriputra! It is like the pūlaka tree, at whatever point it is split open, auspicious markings appear both on the inside and the outside.
The śarīra of that Buddha is likewise.

Śāriputra! The sentient beings of that land will erect stupas made of the seven precious substances to enshrine the relics, filling the entire trichiliocosm. They will further make offerings with golden thousand-petaled lotuses, so that the great trichiliocosm is adorned and embellished by those stupas and flowers.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,

if there are bodhisattvas who are about to pass into parinirvāṇa in the land of Akṣobhya Buddha, at the time of their death they will never lose mindfulness and will behold such various auspicious signs."

There may be bodhisattvas who see that in their future birthplace there is no Tathāgata and must become a Buddha themselves; or they may see that a Buddha is already present there and immediately serve him. Or they may see a bodhisattva entering his mother’s womb;

or they may see a bodhisattva donning the great armor; or they may see him leaving home for the homeless life; or they may see him sitting at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) and subduing the armies of Māra; or they may see a bodhisattva realizing the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna); or they may see a bodhisattva attaining equal and perfect enlightenment in a certain world-system and turning the wheel of Dharma.
Or there may be a bodhisattva who dwells in mid-air, his own body gradually vanishing until not even a trace remains.
It is like burning wet grass, where the smoke rises upward and gradually dissipates until it reaches total extinction.
“Śāriputra! Once these bodhisattvas have entered parinirvāṇa, all devas and humans will fully cultivate offerings to them.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!”
"After the Tathāgata Akṣobhya has entered parinirvāṇa through the Great Nirvāṇa, his True Dharma shall remain in the world for hundreds of thousands of kalpas.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“Śāriputra, what kind of kalpa is it in which the True Dharma of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya abides?
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
“Twenty minor kalpas constitute one [major] kalpa; he abides for as many hundreds of thousands of such kalpas.”
Śāriputra! After the True Dharma has been extinguished, there will be a great radiance illuminating the worlds of the ten directions, and the earth will all tremble, emitting a great sound.
Yet that [Dharma] cannot be destroyed by the celestial Māras, nor will it vanish of its own accord through the Tathāgatas or the assembly of Śrāvakas.
However, at that time, people will hear little and have few desires for the Dharma; those capable of preaching the Dharma will all distance themselves from them.
Having heard little of the True Dharma, their lack of faith will further increase; as lack of faith increases, they will lack diligent effort.

"The Dharma-knowing bhikṣus will naturally withdraw into seclusion; observing that there is no joy in desire, they will no longer propagate [the teachings], and those subtle words of the Buddha will gradually vanish.
Chapter Six: Causes and Conditions for Rebirth At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“By what causes, conditions, and power of roots of goodness do Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas attain rebirth in that Buddha-field?
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

“If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva wishes to be born in the world of Abhirati, they should study the past practices of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya as he practiced the bodhisattva path. They should give rise to a great vow of aspiration to be born in that land; through such practice and vows, they can create the causes and conditions for birth in that Buddha-field.”

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā), he dedicates these corresponding roots of goodness toward unexcelled enlightenment, vowing: 'May I meet with the Tathāgata Acala. Śāriputra!"
By these causes and conditions, one shall be born in that realm.
Thus it is for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of ethical discipline (śīlapāramitā), and so it is likewise for the perfections up to the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, the light of the Tathāgata Acala universally illuminates the Buddha-fields of the trichiliocosm. May they, in a future age, behold this light and realize unexcelled enlightenment; having attained great bodhi by virtue of seeing this light, may they further cause their own bodily radiance to pervade the world. Śāriputra!"
By these causes and conditions, a bodhisattva shall be born in that land.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, the assembly of śrāvakas of that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Acalā is immeasurable and boundless; may I behold them, and having beheld them, may I initiate such practices as to realize the Bodhi of a Buddha.
When he realizes enlightenment, there will likewise be such immeasurable and innumerable assemblies of śrāvakas. Śāriputra,
for these reasons, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain rebirth in that buddha-field.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

In that buddha-field, there are immeasurable and boundless bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. Desiring to see these bodhisattvas, I shall practice the path of meditative concentration and vows to follow and learn from them; I shall assemble with these bodhisattvas in various places, studying together, riding the same vehicle, and reaching the ultimate goal together."

May we meet those who seek the fulfillment of their aspirations, who desire great compassion, who seek awakening and the state of a śramaṇa, who have abandoned the mind of the two vehicles, who abide in the reality of true emptiness, and whose mindfulness remains continuous in recollecting the omniscience of the Buddha Tathāgata and the names of the Dharma and Saṅgha.
Śāriputra! If good sons or good daughters hear the names of such bodhisattvas, they shall attain rebirth in those buddha-fields;
how much more so for those who possess roots of goodness associated with the prajñāpāramitā and dedicate them to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Acalā.
Śāriputra! By these causes and conditions, this person will certainly be reborn in that buddha-field.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva wishes to be born in that buddha-field, they should, with respect to the various Buddhas and Tathāgatas in the immeasurable worlds of the eastern direction who are preaching the subtle and wondrous Dharma and their assemblies of śrāvakas, bring those images to mind as being present before them, making this vow: "May I also realize bodhi and preach the subtle and wondrous Dharma, and may my assembly of śrāvakas be exactly like that of those Buddhas."

Śāriputra! These bodhisattvas should cultivate three kinds of roots of goodness through recollection, vowing to practice them equally together with all sentient beings, and dedicate these roots of goodness toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Śāriputra! Such roots of goodness dedicated by a bodhisattva are immeasurable.
Suppose all sentient beings were each to take a vessel equal in capacity to space and say these words:
“O Noble One! Please share those roots of goodness with me. Śāriputra!

If these roots of goodness possessed material form, even if one were to give them to all sentient beings until their vessels were filled and each departed with their share, those roots of goodness would still never be exhausted.
Because it is dedicated toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, which is immeasurable and cannot be diverted.
Śāriputra! That dedication accomplished through the three recollections is directed toward all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*); by means of these roots of goodness, one follows after the Three Jewels.

Śāriputra! If there are bodhisattvas who accomplish these roots of goodness, you should know that they will not fall into any of the evil realms, but will be able to subdue Pāpīyān and all the hosts of Māras, taking birth in whichever Buddha-fields they desire.
Even so it is in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below; in all these places, they are able to take birth according to their vows.

Therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should accumulate these roots of goodness through such recollection. Having accumulated them, they should dedicate them to the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, whereby they shall attain birth in that buddha-field.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
the vast and magnificent adornments of the merits of the Tathāgata Acalā’s buddha-field do not exist at all within any of the immeasurable other buddha-fields."

Therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should give rise to this thought: "By means of these roots of goodness, I vow that I shall see that land; I vow that I shall receive its adornments; and I also vow that I shall see all those bodhisattvas therein."
Śāriputra! By these causes and conditions, a bodhisattva shall be born in that land. Śāriputra!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who wish to be born in that buddha-field should give rise to a mind of superior aspiration.
Śāriputra, if good sons or good daughters give rise to such a superior mind, I shall grant them all the prediction that they will attain birth in that buddha-field.
Śāriputra! It is like a city that has no towers, pavilions, gardens, groves, or ponds, nor any place for elephants and horses to roam.
Although the king of that city possesses the power to dwell there securely, because the city lacks the merits of towers and such, it is not adorned.
Śāriputra! This buddha-field of mine is likewise; because it lacks those merits, it is not adorned. Śāriputra!
If this land of mine were adorned with such merits, it would be as magnificent as the Buddha-field of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya.

Śāriputra, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to embrace a pure Buddha-field, they should cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva just as the Tathāgata Akṣobhya did in the past; having planted the roots of all virtues to adorn and purify a Buddha-field, they should likewise assimilate such merits.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Suppose that at this present time, having attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, I were to tame immeasurable sentient beings so that they all obtain the realization of the fruits of the two vehicles, and were to gather together all those who have been tamed by my śrāvakas; compared to the assembly of śrāvakas belonging to that Tathāgata, these would not equal even one hundredth part, nor one thousandth part, nor one hundred-thousandth part, nor one hundred-billionth part, nor any numerical part, nor any calculable part, nor any figurative part, nor even a *upaniṣad* part."
Why is this? Because their number is immeasurable;
if one speaks of liberation, there is no difference between them.
Let us set aside this matter.

Śāriputra, when that Tathāgata Maitreya appears in the world, the number of his assembly of śrāvakas and the remaining śrāvakas he has disciplined shall not equal even a fraction of the number of śrāvakas of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya; it should be understood as being thus deficient.
Śāriputra! By means of a single teaching of the Dharma, that Tathāgata was able to skillfully discipline immeasurable sentient beings.
Yet, as for those who were gathered and sustained by that Blessed One, no one is able to know their number.

Śāriputra! My own śrāvakas, as well as the assembly of śrāvakas of the Tathāgata Maitreya, and even all the śrāvakas belonging to the Buddha-Bhagavāns of the Bhadrakalpa, along with the other assemblies of śrāvakas who are yet to be disciplined by them—all these taken together do not equal even a hundredth part of the assembly of śrāvakas of the Tathāgata Acalā; they do not even equal a single *upaniṣad* fraction thereof.
Why is this? Because their number is vast,
and because there is no difference in liberation.
Then Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
As I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has taught, one should know that the realm of those arhats is not the realm of foolish commoners.”
"Why is this? Because there are many arhats in that buddha-field.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"It is so, it is so; it is just as you have said, for in that buddha-field there are many arhats whose outflows are exhausted.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, the number of stars in this trichiliocosm does not equal the multitude of śrāvakas in that buddha’s realm."
Because through a single teaching of that Tathāgata, immeasurable sentient beings attain arhatship. Śāriputra!

Although the stars in this trichiliocosm still have a calculable number, because immeasurable sentient beings attain arhatship at each and every assembly, the number of śrāvakas in those assemblies is beyond measure.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
The gods and humans of that land have planted many roots of goodness; even the gods and humans of other realms, though they possess the divine eye, cannot see them. Śāriputra!"

Even if the gods and humans of other realms were to go to where those sons and daughters of good family reside in that land, they would not be able to see them, even with the full extent of their divine eyes.

If any person hears this Dharma-gate of the Praise of Merits, and having heard it, receives, upholds, recites, and masters it, those sons of good family have all previously seen and heard [this] while the Tathāgata Acalā was practicing the bodhisattva path in the past; therefore, upon hearing this Dharma-gate, they immediately attain pure faith.

Śāriputra! Among all the lands in every world-system of the eastern direction, the number of those belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle or the śrāvaka vehicle who read, recite, and have mastered this Dharma-gate is exceedingly great.

Those bodhisattvas and śrāvakas, by the power of their vows, have been born, are currently being born, or will be born within the Akṣobhya realm; this excludes only those bodhisattvas who are non-retrogressive, for such bodhisattvas shall attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment in various other realms.
It is likewise in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below. Śāriputra,
that Tathāgata Akṣobhya, in the world-system of Abhirati and in other lands, serves as the foremost leader among the assembly of bodhisattvas and those of the various vehicles.

Śāriputra! If there are good men or good women who, having heard this Dharma-gate of the merits of the Tathāgata Acalā, are able to properly receive, uphold, read, recite, and master it, and aspire to be born in that land, then until the end of their lives, the Tathāgata Acalā will constantly protect and mind them, ensuring that neither the Māras nor their retinues can cause their resolve to regress.

Śāriputra! You should know that these good sons or good daughters shall have no fear of retrogression until they reach unsurpassed bodhi; furthermore, they shall not be harmed by water, fire, blades, staves, wild beasts, or venomous insects, nor shall they be terrified by humans or non-humans.
Why is this? Because the Tathāgata Akṣobhya constantly protects and keeps them in mind, and they shall be reborn in that buddha-field. "Śāriputra!..."
For example, although the orb of the sun is far away, it provides light for the sentient beings of Jambudvīpa.
The Tathāgata Akṣobhya is likewise; although he remains at a great distance, he is able to provide light for the assembly of bodhisattvas in other realms.
Śāriputra! For example,
just as a bhikṣu who possesses the divine eye can see all forms, whether good or evil, in distant regions,
so too the Tathāgata Acalā, although residing in that land, can see all the various forms and physical appearances of the multitude of bodhisattvas in other worlds.

Śāriputra! Furthermore, it is like a bhikṣu who has attained mastery over the mind and acquired the perfection of supernormal powers (abhijñāpāramitā), who, though situated at a great distance, clearly knows the minds of all sentient beings.
The Tathāgata Akṣobhya is likewise able to know the minds of all bodhisattvas in other realms.
Śāriputra, it is like a bhikṣu who has realized the divine ear; although his body is far away, he can hear all sounds.
Amitābha Tathāgata is likewise; the sentient beings dwelling in other worlds speak thus:
"I vow to be born in that land."
Those Buddhas all heard it.
Śāriputra, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya fully knows the names and surnames of all such sons and daughters of good family.

If there are those who receive, uphold, read, recite, and master this Dharma-gate of merit, all such persons shall be known and seen by the Tathāgata Akṣobhya and shall be protected and mindful of by him.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“It is rare, World-Honored One!
Even that Buddha, the World-Honored One, protects and keeps those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in mind.”
After he had made this request, the Buddha told Śāriputra:
"So it is, so it is; it is just as you have said."
That bodhisattva mahāsattva is protected and sustained by the Tathāgata.
Why is this? Because by protecting and sustaining the bodhisattva, all sentient beings likewise obtain protection and sustenance.

Śāriputra! It is, for example, like a Kṣatriya great king who has been consecrated by coronation, who possesses many granaries filled with stored grains and beans, and who strictly admonishes his officials to ensure they guard them well.
Why is this? Because in an age of famine, one shall provide relief to all living beings. Śāriputra!

After the parinirvāṇa of that Tathāgata, these bodhisattvas shall realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and they will bring about great abundance during times of famine for the True Dharma.
The Tathāgata is likewise; he is well able to protect and shield these bodhisattvas. Śāriputra!

There are bodhisattvas in this world who, upon hearing this Dharma-gate of the merits of the Tathāgata Acalā, are able to properly receive, uphold, recite, and master it, and aspire to be born in that buddha-field—know that such persons have attained non-retrogression.

Śāriputra! If other bodhisattvas are able to properly receive, uphold, read, recite, and master this Dharma-gate, and reveal and expound it for immeasurable, countless hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, causing all those beings likewise to plant the roots of various virtues, so that they may draw near to unsurpassed bodhi.

Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva wishes to swiftly realize unsurpassed bodhi, they should receive, uphold, read, recite, and master such a dharma-gate, and reveal and expound it for the sake of all sentient beings.
Why is this? A bodhisattva-mahāsattva should expound this gateway of merit and the activity of great wisdom in this manner; they should initiate and accumulate it in such and such a way.
Because those people have initiated and accumulated [this practice], their outflows (āsrava) shall be exhausted within their present bodies.
Śāriputra, therefore,
if a follower of the Śrāvaka vehicle hears this Dharma-gate, they should receive, uphold, read, recite, and master it, and extensively reveal and expound it for the sake of sentient beings.
Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family, by upholding such true Dharma, shall realize the state of no-more-learning (*aśaikṣa*) in their very present bodies. Śāriputra!

If there are sons or daughters of noble family with pure faith who, regarding this Dharma-gate of praising these merits, should expound it for others from time to time, those people shall not exceed two more births;
they shall, in their present body, attain the exhaustion of all outflows (*āsrava*).

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, this Dharma-gate of praising the merits of this Tathāgata Acala cannot be received by those who are ignorant or shallow; only those whose wisdom is profound and vast are able to receive and uphold it."
Śāriputra! Those sons and daughters of good family shall behold all the Buddhas; they will surely attain this Dharma-gate of praising merit with their own bodies. Śāriputra!
Suppose a priceless jewel were brought from the ocean.
What do you think?
Who would be the first to obtain this priceless treasure?
Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
There are kings, princes, and great ministers; these people shall obtain it first.”
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
“The Dharma-gate of that Buddha’s merits is likewise; the bodhisattvas obtain it first.

These bodhisattvas shall never regress. If they hear this Dharma, they will surely be able to receive, uphold, read, recite, and master it, and they shall diligently cultivate and study the nature of *tathatā* for the sake of unsurpassed enlightenment.”
Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If bodhisattvas wish to abide in the stage of non-retrogression, upon hearing this Dharma-gate of praise, they should receive, uphold, read, recite, and master it thoroughly.”
Why is this? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva who dwells in this dharma-gate shall not regress within the nature of phenomena.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"Suppose there were someone who, having filled Jambudvīpa with gold and jewels, offered them as a gift in the hope of hearing this Dharma, yet in the end would still not hear it. Why is this? "
This dharma of merit is not for beings of meager fortune to grasp and uphold.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, if a person of the Śrāvaka vehicle hears this dharma-gate of merit and receives, upholds, reads, and recites it, practicing with diligence for the sake of unexcelled bodhi and its correspondence with *tathatā*, they shall achieve accomplishment in their subsequent body; or within two births as a candidate for the place of succession (*upapadya-parivartin*), or at most three births, they shall never exceed that limit and shall attain perfect enlightenment.
If they hear this Dharma-gate of praise, read it, recite it, and master it, and furthermore reveal and expound it for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings— Śāriputra!

Just as a wheel-turning monarch, through the influence of his prior karma, perceives the seven treasures appearing before him, so too is the Tathāgata Acalo; by the power of his original vow, I now proclaim this Dharma-gate of merit.

Śāriputra! If any bodhisattva mahāsattvas have heard or shall hear this Dharma-gate of praise, they do so all by virtue of the power of the compassionate vows made by the Tathāgata Acalā when he formerly practiced the bodhisattva path; or they shall hear and be shown this Dharma-gate by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, within this Bhadrakalpa, with the same number of names, neither more nor less, as I now expound and reveal.

Śāriputra! Therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to swiftly realize unsurpassed awakening should receive, uphold, read, recite, master, and extensively explain for others this Dharma-gate of praise for these merits.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,
if a son of good family or a daughter of good family, for the sake of seeking this Dharma-gate, hears, receives, upholds, recites, and masters it within those villages and cities.
