“Those who practice the Dharma-realm, Abiding securely within Bodhi,
Attain the state of spontaneity And swiftly become Tathāgatas.”
At that time, the Devaputra A-sthāna-śikṣita praised him in verse, saying:
"Those who perceive what is improper, Yet can take joy in the Tathāgata’s teaching,"
"Even a thousand billion hosts of Māra armies cannot delude them.
At that time, the Devaputra Jñānasthānajña praised him with a verse:
"All those who know what is not the proper place, the wise attain joy."
“As we cultivate awakening, even billions of māras cannot shake us.
At that time, the devaputra Gambhīrārthavyūha praised him in verse:
“Having well studied the sphere of profound wisdom, you abide securely within the True Dharma.”
"One who can mount the Māra Pāpīyān is like one who drives a chariot yoked with well-trained horses.
At that time, the Devaputra Sunāsthāna praised him in verse:
"The non-place is the realm of wholesome dharmas; one trains in the single characteristic."
"If Māra were able to cause affliction, the Buddha said that such a thing is impossible.
At that time, the Devaputra Abiding-in-Abode praised him in verse:
"Regarding what is possible and what is impossible, he reveals these to the ignorant."
"The Tathāgata, having realized it for himself, Then teaches it to sentient beings.
At that time, the Devaputra Sunyagrhīta praised him in verse:
"Due to those objects grasped as causes, And the karma performed in the past,"
"The Blessed One fully knows those causes and the places where they cultivate their karma.
At that time, the devaputra Skillful Karma praised him in verse:
"Greed, hatred, and delusion—the Buddha likewise knows their causes and karma."
"As for causes and karmic actions, the Tathāgata knows them all.
Then, the Devaputra Jñānāgata praised him in verse:
"He knows that future world, and the karma performed by sentient beings."
"Whatever actions they have performed, the Buddha knows them all in every respect.
Then, the Devaputra Cintita-pratyutpanna praised him in verse:
"Throughout the realms of the ten directions, the karma and causes of sentient beings—"
"The Teacher fully understands the locations, causes, karmas, and activities.
Then, the Devaputra Balaviṣaya praised him in verse:
"Whether it be karma or its cause, the location and its arising,"
The Tathāgata knows all things; therefore, he is called the Teacher of Gods and Humans.
At that time, the Devaputra Rati-bala praised him in verse:
“Regarding karma and its locations, within the retributions of the three periods of time,”
Whatever deeds they perform, the Tathāgata knows them all.
At that time, the Devaputra Balapati praised him in verse:
“The deeds performed through karma, their retributive causes and conditions—”
"Since their abiding nature is inherently detached, this Buddha has no equal.
Then the Devaputra Balalakṣmī praised him in verse:
"The activities performed through karma / Abide within the conventional truth of causes and conditions."
"The fruits of retribution that are experienced— The Buddha knows them all to be empty.
Then the Devaputra Balaprīti praised him in verse:
"Actions performed due to karma, Are the sphere of causes and conditions in conventional truth."
The Buddha, having fully realized this himself, taught that they lack intrinsic nature.
At that time, the Devaputra Balavikrīḍita praised him in verse:
“The things produced by causes and conditions exist within the conventional truth of dependent origination.”
"Not arising from self or other, the Buddha knows that [all things] arise from conditions.
*Mahāratnakūṭa Sūtra*, Scroll 70; *Mahāratnakūṭa Sūtra*, Scroll 71.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of the Northern Qi Dynasty.
Chapter Twenty-three, Part Two: Verses of Praise by the Sons of the Gods of the Pure Abodes from the "Bodhisattva’s Vision of Reality" Assembly.
At that time, the Son of the Gods Balajanman spoke in verse, praising [the Buddha]:
“If all causes, conditions, and karmas, As well as the resulting retributions,
Are in their essential nature entirely empty— The Buddha has spoken thus, like a lion.
Then the Devaputra Anulomabala spoke this verse in praise:
“If, by means of karmic causes and conditions, The various fruits are brought to growth, The Honored One among Two-Legged Beings knows this; Therefore, the Buddha is without equal.
At that time, the Devaputra Anulomabalika spoke these verses in praise:
"Cultivating such elements and performing such deeds, one shall receive such retribution; the Buddha’s eye perceives all this.
At that time, the Devaputra Balotpāda spoke these verses in praise:
"Cultivating such elements and accomplishing such natures,
the Buddha knows all sentient beings as clearly as one observes the five fingers of one's own hand.
At that time, the Devaputra Balavīrya spoke this verse in praise:
"Cultivating such elements, one encounters such friends;
by associating with them in such a manner, the Supreme Being knows it all.
At that time, the Devaputra Balādhāna spoke this verse in praise:
“The Guide understands how that realm is empowered;
He approaches all his spiritual friends, And the Honored One among Men perceives them all.
Then, the devaputra Niścayadhātu spoke this verse in praise:
“The Buddha knows with certainty that realm, that vow, those friends, and that association; therefore, he is able to eliminate doubt.
Then, the devaputra Samyaktvadhātuka spoke this verse in praise:
“The realms and the continuities, The worlds wherein they dwell,
Their conduct and their various destinies— All these the Supreme Person knows.
Then the devaputra Śikṣādhātu spoke this verse in praise:
"Within those various realms, the Guide’s wisdom is able to know them;
that wisdom is empty in its essential nature—thus speaks the One of Supreme Wisdom.
At that time, the Devaputra Yānadhātu spoke this verse in praise:
“He cultivates those realms and dwells in the world according to the capacities and times;
the Buddha knows all this as it truly is, and is therefore called the Peerless Body.
Then the devaputra Anulomadhatu spoke these verses in praise:
“The cultivation within that realm, the merits obtained therein,
their causes and their karmic results— the Buddha knows them all without exception.
Then, the Devaputra Sahadhātusthita spoke this verse in praise:
"According to the realms they cultivate, and according to the paths toward which they incline, the Buddha knows them all without exception; therefore, he is revered by the wise.
At that time, the Devaputra Jñānacārin spoke this verse in praise:
"According to the realms they cultivate, and according to the paths toward which they incline, the Buddha knows the conduct of sentient beings; therefore, he is called the Knower of the Learned.
At that time, the Devaputra Vīramati spoke this verse in praise:
“Those of right determination, those of wrong determination, and those of indeterminate beings—
among these three groups, the Buddha knows them with certainty. At that time,
the Devaputra Caritramati spoke this verse in praise:
“If there are beings established in right concentration, capable of proceeding toward nirvāṇa,
for them the Buddha is the sun of the world, his wisdom unimpeded therein.
At that time, the devaputra Vimokṣacārin spoke this verse in praise:
“If there are sentient beings who dwell in the stage of no fixed destiny and fall into the various evil realms, for them too you preach nirvāṇa.
At that time, the Devaputra Balakālāpa spoke this verse in praise:
“The Buddha is merely a provisional name; so too are his powers and wisdom, as well as the four fearlessnesses and the rest—they exist only in accordance with conventional speech.
At that time, the Devaputra Drṣṭatattva spoke this verse in praise:
“There is no Buddha nor the Buddha-dharma, nor is there any other collection of knowledge;
he reveals the ultimate truth—thus the Tathāgata knows it as it truly is.
At that time, the Devaputra Balasthita spoke this verse in praise:
"Abiding in the power of the Buddha-dharma, thereby attaining fearlessness,
acting with mastery according to their wishes— all such ones are children of the Buddhas.
Then the Devaputra Dharmābhaya uttered these verses in praise:
"The conventional truth and the ultimate truth—these two kinds are revealed;
yet within that ultimate truth, verbal expression is unattainable.
At that time, the Devaputra Jñānaguru spoke this verse in praise:
“The verbal expressions of the Dharma differ, and the characteristics of the Dharma likewise differ;
yet these expressions are without characteristic—the Buddha’s wisdom is the characteristic of the Dharma.
At that time, the Devaputra Vīryacārin spoke this verse in praise:
“The Great Muni knows all places: those who are in the wrong state, those of indeterminate destiny, those heading toward other realms, and those fixed in error throughout every situation.
Then, the Devaputra Śraddhābala spoke this verse in praise:
"Cultivating that realm, Just as one gives rise to a mind of faith and joy,
Seeing desire as pure— The Muni fully understands this all.
Then the Devaputra Aśubhayāna spoke a verse in praise, saying:
"Unreal and false conceptualization increases the realm of desire;
the Muni knows according to reality that those who have faith will travel that path.
Then, the devaputra Maitrīyānagati spoke this verse in praise:
"Unreal and false conceptualization increases the realm of hatred;
the Muni fully understands how those who have faith ride upon that path.
Then, the Devaputra Carrying the Path of Causes and Conditions spoke this verse in praise:
"Unreal and false conceptualization increases the realm of ignorance;
those who have faith ride upon that path—the Muni fully understands this.
Then, the devaputra Śamathavāhana spoke these verses in praise:
"Those who harbor fear for their livelihood increase their envy;
they believe in that [false teacher] and practice accordingly—the Muni fully understands this all.
At that time, the Devaputra named *Upāsitasatpuruṣa* (He Who Associates with Good Friends) spoke these verses in praise:
"Associating with friends who are good or evil, one increases those respective realms and forms faith therein; Gautama understands all this completely.
Then, the Devaputra Vijnana-drdha spoke this verse in praise:
“Wandering through the world, according to the realms they cultivate and the faith they follow, the Buddha knows them all without exception.
Then, the Devaputra Drdhavrata spoke this verse in praise:
“Circulating through birth and death, practicing such conduct,
and following with faith in that— the Buddha knows it all without exception.
Then, the Devaputra Śraddhendriya spoke this verse in praise:
“If there are sentient beings who, according to the elements they cultivate, the Buddha is able to fully know them all; therefore, he is called the One of Unobstructed Wisdom.
At that time, the Devaputra Indriyacaryā spoke this verse in praise:
“The Buddha thoroughly knows all faculties, Arising according to their skillful means, Their objects of focus and their spheres; He enters them as they arise.
Then the Devaputra Indriyavāhana spoke this verse in praise:
"Oppressed by physical suffering, / One is driven by the thirst of craving;
/ To sever all such cravings— / Only the Buddha’s wisdom is supreme.
At that time, the Devaputra Indriyaviṣaya spoke this verse in praise:
"To teach beings of inferior faculties, he instructs them to distance themselves from craving for form;
to teach those who are sharp, he instructs them to practice contemplation—this is what was spoken by the Honored One among Two-Legged Beings.
At that time, the Devaputra Indriyavara spoke this verse in praise:
“Those of inferior faculties who dwell in seclusion can extinguish sensual desire;
the One Honored Among Two-Legged Beings knows how they rightly contemplate craving.
Then, the Devaputra Indriyaniyata spoke this verse in praise:
"Regarding that which previously gave rise to craving and desire, the Buddha observed it as unattainable;
knowing that non-knowing is quiescent extinction, he is therefore named the One of Supreme Faculties.
At that time, the devaputra Avirahitendriya spoke this verse in praise:
“Abiding in detachment and free from anger—this is the antidote to hatred;
it is the practice of those with inferior faculties, as the Buddha knows the inclinations of sentient beings.
Then, the Devaputra Śraddhendriya spoke this verse in praise:
"Practicing loving-kindness removes ill-will, It can give rise to the wisdom of sentient beings;
He is able to extinguish the realm of anger— The Honored One among Men knows all this.
At that time, the Devaputra Mūlaparyeṣin spoke a verse in praise, saying:
"Free from anger and devoid of faults, his nature is tranquil through the practice of loving-kindness;
since neither purity nor impurity can be apprehended, he is called the Honored One among Men.
At that time, the devaputra Mūlānuvartaka spoke this verse in praise:
“Engaging in false conceptualization, Teaching false practices to others,
With heavy delusion and lack of skillful means— The Buddha perceives this as liberation from perversion.
Then the Devaputra Jñānodaya spoke a verse in praise:
"Greed, hatred, and delusion, etc., which cling to objects before them and obstruct the attainment of that wisdom-light— all these are fully known by the One of Great Renown.
At that time, the devaputra Vigatājñānarati spoke this verse in praise:
"Regarding greed, hatred, and delusion, as well as the matters of light and darkness, their intrinsic nature cannot be apprehended; the Honored One among Two-Legged Beings knows them all.
At that time, the Devaputra Dharṇatejas spoke this verse in praise:
“The wisdom attained by sentient beings— according to the extent of that wisdom they have acquired,
and according to the vessel of wisdom they have formed— the Tathāgata knows it all.
At that time, the Devaputra Mūlaparyeṣin spoke this verse in praise:
"Knowing wisdom with wisdom, one remains far removed from all afflictions;
the Teacher of Gods and Humans knows this all, and therefore I bow my head in homage.
At that time, the devaputra Ekāntasukhendriya spoke these verses in praise:
“The lands and their seasons, The observation of the skillful means of the Dharma,
And the defilements of afflictions as well as purity— The Tathāgata knows them all to be empty.
At that time, the Devaputra Jñānaketu spoke this verse in praise:
“The faculties, desires, and faiths of sentient beings— Their distinctions of superior,
middling, and inferior, Their bondage and liberation, as well as their wisdom— All are seen, yet there is no conscious awareness.
Then the Devaputra Indradhvaja spoke this verse in praise:
“The faculties—superior, middling, and inferior; afflictions, wisdom, and sensation;
the disciplined and the undisciplined—the Buddha taught that all these are without marks.
Then, the devaputra Śuddhendriya spoke this verse in praise:
“Through dhyāna, liberation, and freedom from afflictions, And through samādhi in right reception,
He rouses sentient beings to purity— The Tathāgata knows them all.
Then the Devaputra Vegavati said in verse as praise:
"Because he has attained the tranquility of dhyāna, he is able to fully comprehend the intrinsic nature of all phenomena; therefore, he is titled 'Omniscient One'.
At that time, the Devaputra Balavarman spoke these verses in praise:
“If one understands phenomena and their intrinsic nature, can explain these phenomena,
and can correctly receive them as they truly are, one will therefore not be attached to the three periods of time.
At that time, the Devaputra Rati-bala spoke this verse in praise:
"Afflictions and false discriminations arise from four kinds;
because he knows that which is produced by karma, he is called the Peerless Man.
At that time, the Devaputra Jñānabala spoke this verse in praise:
“Capable of knowing the pure dharmas, Applying antidotes to the afflictions,
And able to proclaim the workings of karma— Therefore, the Buddha is called the Peerless One.
At that time, the Malla Devaputra spoke this verse in praise:
“The Buddha has declared that the arising from meditative absorptions and liberations,
the attainments of samādhi, and both afflictions and purification are all merely provisional.
Then, the Devaputra Balajanman spoke this verse in praise:
“Dhyāna, liberation, and purity, Samādhi and meditative absorption— These arise from non-negligence; The Buddha knows them all.
Then, the Devaputra Balavardhana spoke this verse in praise:
“The Great Hero, within this state, is able to turn toward dhyāna and the like;
knowing how to enter equanimity without hindrance, he moves through it like the wind through space.
At that time, the Devaputra Jñātapūrvānta spoke this verse in praise:
“Throughout countless billions of eons, Abiding within the various realms of existence, He is not defiled by the faults of existence; Therefore, he is called the Supreme Man.
Then the Devaputra Abiding in the Past Limit spoke this verse in praise:
“Having already performed offerings to countless billions of Buddhas,
seeking the unsurpassed path, I therefore take refuge.
At that time, the Devaputra Dṛṣṭapūrvānta spoke this verse in praise:
“In past lives, you made various offerings to the Buddhas;
thus, O Honored One among Men, you have fully attained all manner of eloquence.
Then, the Devaputra Skillful in the Past spoke this verse in praise:
“In the past, while wandering through the world, I studied according to the Dharma and practiced accordingly;
Having seen immeasurable Buddhas, I am thus able to deeply understand the Dharma.
At that time, the Devaputra Śikṣitapūrvānta spoke this verse in praise:
"In the presence of the Dharma-kings of all Buddhas, the Great Hero practiced in the past;
having learned from the Buddhas, he now bows, knowing all modes of conduct.
At that time, the Devaputra Pūrvopāyasaṃpanna spoke this verse in praise:
“Throughout immeasurable billions of eons, He has practiced the conduct of boundless Buddhas,
Cultivating supreme diligence In order to seek the Buddha’s wisdom. Then,
the Devaputra Original Skillful Means Determination spoke these verses in praise:
"All phenomena are determined; though observed for many billions of eons, all phenomena have no entry, yet it is only said that they are a harmony of conditions.
At that time, the Devaputra Pūrvāntacintin spoke this verse in praise:
“Throughout immeasurable billions of eons, the Guide practiced the path;
because he knows what is possible and what is impossible, he is named ‘Knower of the World.
At that time, the Devaputra Pūrvāntavivecaka spoke this verse in praise:
"Abiding in what is possible and what is impossible, Observing the causes of karma,
the elements, faculties, dhyānas, and liberations— The Buddha is able to know all of these.
Then the Devaputra Pūrvāntadarśin spoke this verse in praise:
"Having observed the past, he increased the power of wisdom;
the Great Hero of Ten Powers observes the world with his wisdom.
At that time, the Devaputra Pūrvāntaviṣaya spoke this verse in praise:
“The Great Hero has fundamentally practiced, Knowing the pure and impure conduct of all sentient beings; Therefore, he is able to discipline sentient beings.
At that time, the Devaputra named Avalokita-pūrvānta-caryā spoke this verse in praise:
"First observe the sentient beings, their past conduct, their faith and inclinations, and their elements; only then do you discipline sentient beings.
At that time, the Devaputra Śraddhābala spoke this verse in praise:
"I now place my faith in the Tathāgata; throughout inconceivable eons, he has observed his original conduct, yet his mind remains entirely free from attachment.
At that time, the Devaputra Jñānaśraddha spoke this verse in praise:
"Throughout countless billions of eons, one might contemplate the Buddha’s past deeds;
yet no son of noble family could ever fathom or exhaust the Tathāgata’s virtues.
Then the Devaputra Skillful in Contemplating the Future spoke this verse in praise:
"With the Buddha-eye, the Tathāgata observes the sentient beings of the ten directions—
those newly born and those who die— as they correspond to their various karmas.
At that time, the Devaputra Śaikṣapaścimaka spoke this verse in praise:
"If causes and karmic actions lead one toward the path of the Buddha, the Muni knows them all; therefore, he is called the Omniscient One.
At that time, the devaputra Vijñānajātijarāmaraṇa spoke this verse in praise:
“If sentient beings, by means of the elements (*dhātu*), perfume and create various karmas,
then both the sentient beings and the karmic habits— the Buddha knows them to be without awakening.
At that time, the Devaputra Jñānajāti spoke this verse in praise:
"Associating with such friends, performing such deeds,
and treading such paths— the Muni fully understands them all. Then,
the Devaputra Skillful in Necessities spoke this verse in praise:
“He knows what is required, and acts accordingly;
having thus performed his work, the Tathāgata fully understands it.
At that time, the Devaputra Karmakauśalya spoke this verse in praise:
"Based upon such matters, one performs such karma;
the Buddha knows them all completely—this is entirely within the Buddha's domain.
At that time, the Devaputra Jñānakārin spoke this verse in praise:
"According to the objects to which one clings, one is able to perform various actions;
because the Buddha understands all faculties, he is fully able to know those karmas.
At that time, the Devaputra Jñānakauśalya spoke this verse in praise:
"If the Buddha knows that both cognition and its objects are mere conceptual constructions,
and understands how they are grasped according to those [conceptions], the Buddha knows them without exception.
Then, the Devaputra Skillful in Practice spoke this verse in praise:
“Following their attachments, they create karma;
because of these afflictions, the Buddha knows them all. Therefore, he is the refuge for the world.
Then, the Devaputra Skillful in Approaching spoke this verse in praise:
"According to the realm they enter, as they have created their karma, so they receive its fruit;
whatever objects they take as conditions for their actions—the Buddha’s eye knows them all.
Then, the Devaputra Skillful in Objects of Cognition spoke this verse in praise:
"Able to know the objects of perception, And how, according to conditions, karma ripens,
Receiving retribution within the various realms of existence— The Buddha knows all this without fail. Then,
the Devaputra Skillful in Latent Tendencies spoke a verse in praise:
"Knowing the habitual tendencies of unwholesome karma, and likewise those of wholesome karma;
knowing the past deeds of sentient beings within each of their various realms of rebirth.
At that time, the Devaputra Skillful in Karma spoke this verse in praise:
"One who can know the three types of karma— those of the present, the future, and the past—
[sees that] sentient beings, within the realms of existence, are everywhere deluded therein. At that time,
the Devaputra Skillful in Time spoke this verse in praise:
“Little is done yet much is received as retribution; much is done yet little is received as retribution.
Even knowing such distinctions of much and little, the non-Buddhists remain deluded therein.
At that time, the Devaputra Śikṣākarman spoke this verse in praise:
"He knows karma that ripens in the present life, And he also knows karma that ripens upon rebirth, As well as karma that ripens in subsequent lives; With his Buddha-eye, he understands them all.
Then the devaputra Jñātapratyutpannakarma spoke this verse in praise:
"If karma is performed in the present life, its retribution is received in the present;
the Buddha understands this all, while ordinary people cannot comprehend it.
At that time, the Devaputra Jñānajātiphalika spoke these verses in praise:
"If such karma is performed, its retribution is received by ordinary beings;
the one of great wisdom knows this all, yet sentient beings cannot comprehend it.
At that time, the Devaputra Jñānapaścādbhava spoke this verse in praise:
"If karma [remains] for many hundreds of millions of eons, and only then receives its retribution—
or even exceeds that duration— the Tathāgata knows it all.
At that time, the Devaputra Jñātakarmāvipāka spoke this verse in praise:
“If any karma has been created, and its karmic conditions have not yet ripened so that its retribution has not yet been received— the Tathāgata fully knows it all. Then,
the Devaputra Observing Unripened Karma spoke this verse in praise:
“The Tathāgata skillfully observes karma; when karma is in accord with its time for producing all sentient beings, he is able to explain it all perfectly.
Then, the Devaputra Well-Knowing-Karma-Ripening spoke this verse in praise:
“When that karma reaches maturity, it can grant a retribution in the future;
the Buddha knows this as it truly is, and he also knows that such wisdom is empty.
Then, the Devaputra Karma-vipāka-niścaya spoke these verses in praise:
"Having fully realized all-knowledge, you understand both light and heavy karma;
because you can know the desires of sentient beings, you have become my honored teacher.
At that time, the Devaputra Jñānakarmagaurava spoke this verse in praise:
“Sentient beings heading toward the evil realms are seen according to their karma;
whether that karma is light or heavy, the wise understand it all.
At that time, the Devaputra Jñātasattvacaryā spoke this verse in praise:
“Beholding the conduct of sentient beings, As well as their various heavy and light karmas, The Heroic One knows them accordingly; This the heterodox cannot comprehend.
Then the Devaputra Avalokita-sattva-caryā spoke this verse in praise:
"Observing the conduct of sentient beings, he proclaims the retribution of karma;
it is like a single *liang* of salt cast into the waters of the Ganges in a vessel.
At that time, the Devaputra Śikṣākarman spoke this verse in praise:
“If one experiences the karma of volition, the Buddha has taught that this is the culmination of karma;
the fruits for those in training and those beyond training have already been proclaimed by the Supreme Sage.
Then, the Devaputra Delighting in the Buddha’s Wisdom spoke these verses in praise:
"What the Buddha’s supreme eye perceives— the foolish and the wise within the three realms receiving retribution according to their karma— I see this in its subtle detail and prostrate before him.
Then, the Devaputra Karmakṣaya spoke a verse in praise, saying:
"Regarding all sentient beings in birth and death, the World-Honored One, the Great Guide, understands them all without exception; therefore, I pay homage to his wisdom and fearlessness.
At that time, the Devaputra Anupalabdha spoke this verse in praise:
“If karma, birth, and death, and the various destinies to which sentient beings go—those retributions are like a dream;
the Honored One Among Two-Legged Beings knows them all.
Then, the Devaputra Seeking Afflictions spoke this verse in praise:
"Greed, hatred, and delusion—these the Honored One Among Two-Legged Beings has utterly exhausted;
he is like a man parched with thirst in a dream who drinks cool, clear water.
At that time, the devaputra Vigatarajasaṃkalpa spoke this verse in praise:
“From conceptual construction arise desire, hatred, and delusion;
they are like play in a dream—to you, the supreme teacher, I pay homage.
Then the devaputra Nivṛttavikalpa spoke this verse in praise:
"If conceptualization is extinguished, it is called the exhaustion of afflictions;
like seeing clouds disperse in a dream, the Honored among Men has manifested this.
At that time, the Devaputra Avalokita-āsrava-kṣaya spoke these verses in praise:
"Just as one sees rain falling in a dream, so too do the outflows arise;
the Great Hero has been able to reveal the causes and conditions for the arising of these outflows.
At that time, the Devaputra Vicāramati spoke this verse in praise:
"Just as one sees a great rain in a dream, so too do the outflows arise;
the Great Hero has been able to reveal that ordinary beings, being deluded, give rise to outflows.
At that time, the Devaputra Dream-like Contemplation spoke this verse in praise:
"Just as one sees rain falling in a dream, The outflows arise accordingly;
The Great Hero has been able to reveal That deluded ordinary beings give rise to these outflows.
Then, the Devaputra Jñānasvabhāva spoke this verse in praise:
"Just as a woman dreams of giving birth to a son, Who, once born, then dies again;
She experiences both joy and sorrow— The Buddha views the world in this same way.
At that time, the Devaputra Sīmāntara spoke this verse in praise:
"Just as one sees the severing of one's head in a dream, so too are the outflows exhausted;
having attained liberation oneself and taught it to others, I pay homage to the One who is Fully Liberated.
Then the devaputra Śikṣitaprajña spoke this verse in praise:
“Seeing the Dharma with clear understanding, one realizes that it is like encountering a pleasant thing in a dream;
by remaining far removed from that which is unreal, one thus brings joy to the world.
At that time, the Devaputra Jñānacitta spoke this verse in praise:
“Hearing the Dharma of the Tathāgata, one finds joy in the Dharma of emptiness;
like one speaking of a dream within a dream, such is the understanding of the world.
At that time, the Devaputra Priyamati spoke this verse in praise:
“The one in meditative concentration can bring joy to the world’s devas and humans;
observing all realms of existence, they are like reflections in a mirror.
At that time, the Devaputra Niyata-mati spoke this verse in praise:
"Having heard the Dharma of the Tathāgata, which is like the sound of a vīṇā, you ferry across the ocean of doubt for gods and humans; therefore, I pay homage to the King among Men.
At that time, the Devaputra Māyānanda spoke this verse in praise:
"Just as when a person performs a magical illusion, it deludes the foolish;
the wise are never deluded, for they know that the illusion is unreal.
At that time, the Devaputra Vimardakṣa spoke this verse in praise:
“Observing all worlds as being like dreams and illusions,
I have no doubt therein, for I have heard the Buddha’s Dharma.
At that time, the Devaputra Śikṣitamaṇḍala spoke these verses in praise:
"Just as a magician creates illusions, He is not deluded by those illusions himself, Because he knows they are empty and illusory; The Buddha’s contemplation of the world is likewise.
Then the Devaputra Vimarśakalpa spoke this verse in praise:
“Deluded thoughts give rise to the world; The Great Teacher knows them all.
Just as one who practices mindfulness with diligence Will see the Buddha even within a dream.
At that time, the Devaputra Extinction-of-Delusion spoke this verse in praise:
"Desire is not produced by external objects; it arises entirely from conceptual construction.
Unreal desires arise through delusion—thus the Honored One among Men knows them as they truly are.
Then, the Devaputra Vijñānavibhūti spoke this verse in praise:
"Just as an echo in a deep valley has no reality, so one does not cling to the world; thus one contemplates the world.
At that time, the Devaputra Skillful in Speech spoke this verse in praise:
“That sound has no reality, yet one hears within it;
the Honored One among Men has proclaimed this to deliver all the foolish and ignorant.
Then, the Devaputra Skillful in Practice According to the Teaching spoke a verse in praise:
"Regarding the distinct meanings within the Dharma, sentient beings falsely grasp at differences;
those who can practice know the Dharma and thereby eliminate doubt therein.
At that time, the Devaputra Anulomacārin spoke this verse in praise:
"If both meaning and phenomena are real, there would be no one capable of understanding them;
there would be neither teaching nor realization—thus spoke the Muni.
At that time, the Devaputra Dharmaprajñapticārin spoke this verse in praise:
“Defilements, stains, outflows, and habitual tendencies— All are conceptualized through false discrimination.
Impurity and purity Are merely conventional designations.
Then the Devaputra Skillful in Discrimination spoke this verse in praise:
"Everything is merely a name— namely, the afflictions, the outflows, and so forth;
both defilement and purification are what the one of great wisdom has taught.
Then the Devaputra Anāśrita-prajñā spoke this verse in praise:
“Unattached to the three realms, his mind is like space;
free from evil, a true field of merit—to him whose mind is extinguished, I prostrate.
Then the Devaputra Adhamaka spoke this verse in praise:
“Neither form nor non-form, neither desire nor nirvāṇa;
the Buddha-mind has no basis of reliance, just like empty space.
At that time, the Devaputra Vītarāga spoke this verse in praise:
“Detached from craving for the desire realm, and likewise for the form and formless realms,
liberated from the obstacles of greed— to the one whose craving is exhausted,
I prostrate. Then, the devaputra Vigatarāga spoke this verse in praise:
“In existence and non-existence, the Buddha has forever severed and distanced himself;
unattached to the three realms, I prostrate to the King of Sages.
Then, the Devaputra Vighuṣṭaśabda spoke this verse in praise:
"Obstructed within the three realms, yet practicing the conduct of a great man, you are able to liberate sentient beings; I take refuge in the Savior.
Then, the Devaputra Vimuktatṛṣṇā spoke this verse in praise:
"Far removed from the fetters and latent tendencies, / Having brought an end to birth and cessation hereafter,
/ With both body and mind utterly pure— / I prostrate to the One Free from Fever.
Then the Devaputra Jñātasvabhāva spoke this verse in praise:
“The Great Hero has attained mastery; he knows that within all phenomena there is nothing to be grasped.
There is neither bondage nor liberation. I prostrate to the one who perceives reality.
Then, the Devaputra Nirgata-paṅka uttered this verse in praise:
“Having distanced oneself from the mire of craving, And likewise departed from all states of existence,
Without grasping and without abandoning— I prostrate to you who have exhausted future becoming.
Then the Devaputra named Abandoning Requisites spoke this verse in praise:
"Having cast off defilements and their conditions, having abandoned sin and distanced yourself from craving,
and having also left behind all hindrances— to the Great Teacher, I pay homage. Then,
the Devaputra Kāmayajña spoke this verse in praise:
“Abandoning both gain and loss, acting with resolve free from attachment, you have escaped the net of Māra; I prostrate to the one who is unattached.
Then the devaputra Priyarati spoke this verse in praise:
“If one’s own path and that of others are free from affliction and fever, the Great Hero beholds that path; I prostrate to the One of Unobstructed Vision.
At that time, the Devaputra named Renown spoke this verse in praise:
"One who accords with the Buddha’s wisdom, practicing as taught and observing as taught, is able to eliminate afflictions; I prostrate to the one who understands the world.
At that time, the Devaputra Abhaya spoke this verse in praise:
"Regarding all phenomena, he is decisive; no one can stand against him.
His lion’s roar is fearless, and so too is the roar of the ocean of wisdom.
At that time, the Devaputra Sarvatrābhaya uttered this verse in praise:
“Skillfully delivering all beings everywhere, Far removed from all poisonous arrows,
Fearless and without timidity— I pay homage to the Most Victorious One.
Then the Devaputra Nirāśa spoke this verse in praise:
“Neither gods nor gandharvas, nor Māras nor Brahmās, can pose a challenging question; therefore, the Buddha is like a lion.
At that time, the Devaputra Siṃhavikrāntagāmī spoke this verse in praise:

“The Buddha is fearless regarding all phenomena; because he has thoroughly understood all dharmas, because he is unimpeded, he is without attachment, and no one is able to challenge him with questions.
At that time, the Devaputra Abhaya spoke this verse in praise:
"Like a lion in the mountain forest, free from fear and without dread,
he subdues all the birds and beasts and lets out a great roar within the woods.
Thus does the World-Honored One roar, striking terror into all the non-Buddhists."
"Neither devas, nāgas, nor gandharvas see anyone who can oppose him.
At that time, the Devaputra Sarvatra-vijaya spoke in verse as praise:
"Throughout all the three realms, there is absolutely nothing [that can compare]."
"One whose power rivals that of a Buddha, therefore I take refuge in him.
At that time, the devaputra Siṃhamati spoke a verse in praise:
"Great wisdom perceives all things; he is fearless regarding all dharmas."
"Unrivaled in the world, I pay homage to the One Who Is Fearless.
Then the Devaputra Sunirmita spoke this verse in praise:
"Knowing himself to be perfectly awakened, he cannot be challenged according to the Dharma."
"If there were anyone capable of challenging this, there would be none at all in the world.
At that time, the Devaputra Dharaṇīdhara spoke these verses in praise:
"The Buddha utters the lion’s roar, revealing and manifesting the treasury of all dharmas."
When the billions of Brahmās heard this teaching, they all resolved their minds upon Bodhicitta.
At that time, the Devaputra Anulomaveśa spoke a verse in praise:
"Those in the assembly have attained great benefit, for they have followed the majestic deportment of the Buddha."
"Having generated the bodhicitta, one will surely become a supreme guide.
At that time, the Devaputra Anulomadharmā spoke this verse in praise:
"Those great beings of the world, having heard the Buddha’s Dharma,"
"One who can give rise to the bodhicitta will surely become a sublime great being.
At that time, the Devaputra Pure Mind spoke a verse in praise, saying:
"Having heard what the Buddha has spoken, there is nothing in the world that can compare to it."
"Trillions of sentient beings alike have resolved upon the supreme mind of enlightenment.
At that time, the devaputra Viśuddhasrotas spoke a verse in praise:
"Throughout the long night, the King of Men has skillfully practiced the Buddha's training."
Therefore, the Buddha’s body is pure, adorned with the thirty-two marks.
At that time, the Devaputra Anāsrvacitta spoke in verse, praising him:
“Because the Buddha has attained the exhaustion of outflows, he lets forth the lion’s roar.”
"Having ascended the mountain of supreme wisdom, there is no one capable of posing difficult questions.
At that time, the Devaputra Anulomika-sattva spoke this verse in praise:
"Within the three realms, there is none at all—neither among devas, humans, nor asuras—"
"It is said that the Buddha’s outflows are not yet exhausted, Therefore the Buddha possesses the ten powers.
At that time, the devaputra Skillful-in-Eliminating-Outflows spoke this verse in praise:
"The Great Victorious Śramaṇa’s outflows Are all entirely exhausted without remainder."
Thus, none were able to challenge him; therefore, the Buddha is my father.
At that time, the Devaputra Nityodyukta spoke a verse in praise:
“Regarding the King of Men, one might challenge him by saying that he still possesses residual afflictions;”
"The world cannot be apprehended; therefore, the Buddha is the Sovereign Father.
Then, the Devaputra Śānticaryā spoke this verse in praise:
"The Buddha has severed greed and hatred, as well as ignorance and its habitual tendencies."
"And having also extinguished the practice of evil karma, I pay homage to the one who has attained tranquility.
At that time, the devaputra Upāyakauśalyacaryā spoke this verse in praise:
"If one observes with skillful means, all afflictions are severed and exhausted."
That Buddha’s wisdom is perfected; therefore, I prostrate to him.
Then the Devaputra Skillful Means-Understanding spoke in verse as praise:
“The Teacher has cultivated within himself immeasurable skillful means;”
"He has severed all those afflictions, exhausting them entirely without remainder.
At that time, the Devaputra Skillful Wisdom spoke this verse in praise:
"The Guide illuminates the world; his skillful wisdom is inexhaustible."
"Therefore, he has severed all afflictions, as well as their habitual tendencies and the like.
At that time, the Devaputra Śāntivihārin spoke this verse in praise:
"Because he has severed all afflictions, his habitual tendencies are entirely without remainder."
"Thus the Buddha of Great Wisdom, unmoving and without fear.
At that time, the Devaputra Tattvadarśin spoke this verse in praise:
"The Buddha has severed all afflictions completely, as well as extinguished all residual habitual tendencies."
"His illumination is like that of a Buddha; in the world, there is nothing comparable.
At that time, the Devaputra Prahīṇakleśa spoke in verse as praise:
"The Buddha has severed all habitual tendencies; there is no longer any trace of foul odor."
"Therefore, the Buddha is the All-Knowing One, possessing the most supreme wisdom among the gods.
At that time, the Devaputra Dwelling on the Edge spoke in verse of praise:
"The Buddha is now in his final body; he has already severed the causes and conditions of birth."
"Because he has exhausted all outflows, the Kinsman of the World has attained fearlessness.
At that time, the Devaputra Immeasurable Wisdom spoke this verse in praise:
"The Great Hero has severed the seeds and burned away the sprouts of suffering and affliction."
"Withered and parched, I fear the spreading creepers; I pay homage to the One who has transcended affliction.
Then the devaputra Niṣkramaṇa-kūpa said in verse:
"The World-Honored One, the All-Knowing, has already left the pit of ignorance behind."
"The Buddha’s practice has already attained purity; therefore, the Buddha has attained fearlessness.
At that time, the devaputra Tudu-you spoke a verse in praise:
"He has already crossed the ocean of existence; the Guide has accomplished what was to be done."
"Having also abandoned the other shore, he has attained fearlessness for his own benefit.
At that time, the Devaputra Nirvāṇapraveśa spoke this verse in praise:
"The Buddha has already attained quiescence; he has utterly destroyed all afflictions."
"Even the slightest habitual tendencies—none remain in the World-Honored One.
At that time, the Devaputra Dharmadhvaja spoke this verse in praise:
"The Buddha has erected the banner of the True Dharma, and has shattered the banner of arrogance."
“The Great Hero has already revealed the immeasurable practices of all dharmas.
At that time, the Devaputra Dharmatā spoke in verse, praising him:
“The nature and the source of all sons, the Muni has realized all dharmas.”
"A virtuous friend to all living beings, I pay homage to the most supreme ocean.
At that time, the Devaputra Dharmapūrṇa spoke this verse in praise:
"Thirsting for and delighting in the Buddha-dharma, he has therefore attained fearlessness."
The sons of the Buddhas, free from attachment, let out the lion’s roar.
Then the Devaputra Dharmaparyeṣin spoke these verses in praise:
“For the sake of seeking all dharmas, the sons of the Buddha have resolved their minds.”
"And seeing the Buddha’s fearlessness, there are those who know and seek awakening.
At that time, the Devaputra Thirsting for the Dharma spoke this verse in praise:
"Because they thirst for and delight in the Buddha-dharma, many hundreds of millions of beings..."
Having heard of the Buddha’s fearlessness, he has deeply aroused great diligence.
At that time, the devaputra Dharmodaya spoke this verse in praise:
“Seeing the excellence of the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, he establishes the True Dharma.”
Having bestowed the gift of fearlessness, the sons of the Buddha seek awakening.
Then the Devaputra Dharmadhara spoke these verses in praise:
“The Dharma taught by the World-Honored One is extremely profound and difficult to perceive;”
"Having heard this, the sons of the Buddha seek unsurpassed bodhi.
At that time, the Devaputra Arati spoke these verses in praise:
"Regarding their bodies, lives, and other wealth, the sons of the Buddha have no stinginess."
"Having heard the Buddha’s lion’s roar, they all seek the wondrous Bodhi.
At that time, the Devaputra Avikalpamati spoke these verses in praise:
"Having heard the Buddha preach the Dharma, their minds reflect upon it without any difference."
"In the presence of the Buddha’s fearlessness, they seek the Dharma and maintain the discipline.
At that time, the Devaputra Avikṣepacārin spoke this verse in praise:
"Having heard the roar of the Dharma King, they do not turn toward divergent paths."
"Stay far removed from the two vehicles, and seek unsurpassed bodhi.
At that time, the Devaputra Upasthita spoke this verse in praise:
"Having seen the Buddha’s lion’s roar, all the sons have heard it."
"You shall certainly attain supreme enlightenment and become the body of a Tathāgata.
At that time, the Devaputra Upapatti-vibhūti spoke these verses in praise:
"Having heard this eloquence from the presence of the Buddha, the World-Honored One..."
Within the Tathāgata’s wondrous Dharma, I have deeply given rise to a heart of joy and delight.
At that time, the Devaputra Prāptapratibhāna spoke this verse in praise:
“When the Buddha roars with fearlessness, What he speaks cannot be refuted.”
"With faith and joy, their minds are resolved, and they never harbor thoughts of turning back.
At that time, the Devaputra Nityapramudita spoke this verse in praise:
"The Lion’s Roar of the Ten Powers is fearless; all the sons of the Buddhas..."
"Always joyful at all times, With minds disciplined, they seek awakening.
Then the Devaputra Acintya-mānasa (No Fearful Heart) spoke this verse in praise:
"Ever joyful and without fear, The sons of the Buddhas, O World-Honored One."
They joyfully seek supreme enlightenment because they have heard the Buddha’s words.
At that time, the Devaputra Unobstructed Mind spoke a verse in praise, saying:
“Those who seek the Buddha-mind will never turn back.”
"The mind is joyful and subtle, because of hearing the Buddha’s excellent teaching.
Then, the devaputra Skillfully Knowing Boundless Dharmas spoke in verse of praise:
"Because the True Dharma is practiced, the faction of pure dharmas does not diminish."
The Teacher, knowing what is not the proper place, does not give rise to a mind of weariness or complacency.
Then the Devaputra Skillful in Preaching the Dharma spoke in verse of praise:
“If those who practice the faction of dark dharmas do not fall back or diminish, [the Teacher remains undaunted].”
“The World-Honored One knows what is impossible; therefore, the Buddha has no fear.
At that time, the Devaputra Fearless of the Dharma-Nature spoke a verse in praise:
“The nature of dark dharmas is such that they will inevitably defile pure dharmas.”
"He whose mind is not defiled— The Buddha knows that for him there is no such state.
Then the devaputra Skillful Correspondence spoke this verse in praise:
"Black dharmas and white dharmas— These two distinct things do not combine."
"The Buddha has explained that meaning; therefore, the Buddha is my teacher.
At that time, the devaputra Skillful Knower of Good and Evil spoke a verse in praise:
"The Great Hero knows all things; he understands that all phenomena are not a confused mass."
"Because of false conceptualization and discrimination, one falls away from wholesome dharmas.
At that time, the Devaputra Yathāvad-vihāra-paripūrṇa spoke these verses in praise:
"One who dwells in the afflictions will never give rise to pure dharmas."
"Because they do not give rise to wholesome qualities (*śukladharma*), you should know that they will certainly decline.
At that time, the Devaputra Abhiratimokṣa spoke this verse in praise:
"If one who seeks liberation practices dark dharmas (*kṛṣṇadharma*),"
“The Buddha taught that those [afflictions] are obstructions; therefore, the Buddha is omniscient.
At that time, the Devaputra Śuddhamati spoke a verse in praise:
“Those whose minds delight in liberation must understand the nature of afflictions.”
"The Great Hero has taught this Dharma; therefore, the Buddha should accept offerings.
Then, the Devaputra Seeing Defilements spoke a verse in praise:
"Moving amidst defilements, yet not recognizing them as defilements,"
"He does not understand the True Dharma," so the Sugata has said.
"If one speaks of various evils yet does not turn back from unwholesome dharmas,
such a person is not a vessel for liberation," as declared by the Honored One among Two-Legged Beings.
At that time, the Devaputra Vinīta spoke these verses in praise:
"Free from desire and worldly clamor, And likewise free from hatred and delusion,
One should practice in accordance with the Dharma As taught by the Buddha."
"Regarding afflictions and pure dharmas, for those who, out of folly, do not know them, the Buddha is not their teacher; thus has the Great Sage spoken.
At that time, the Devaputra Vīryavimukta spoke this verse in praise:
“The Buddha taught the Dharma of remedies in order to eliminate afflictions;
yet one who practices them without exhausting the delusions cannot be struck down by any adversary.
At that time, he spoke this verse in praise to the Devaputra Vimuktipratyanika:
“The Buddha has taught such a Dharma for the sake of severing afflictions;
if one practices it without failing to extinguish delusions, no one will be able to strike or challenge them.
At that time, the Devaputra Upāyasaṃprayukta spoke this verse in praise:
“The Buddha is the teacher of the Dharma; for the sake of the śrāvakas and others, even if they practice without yet attaining realization, none are able to challenge or refute the Buddha.
At that time, the devaputra Vimuktagati spoke this verse in praise:
“The Buddha has preached such a Dharma for the purpose of severing afflictions;
if one does not extinguish delusions, no one is able to challenge or trouble the Buddha.
At that time, the Devaputra Fearless Virtue spoke this verse in praise:
“In order to extinguish the afflictions, the Buddha taught the meditation on impurity;
yet if they are not completely extinguished, no one is able to challenge or trouble the Buddha.
At that time, the Devaputra Suniścita-bhadracitta spoke this verse in praise:
"Loving-kindness can sever ill-will; if one cultivates loving-kindness and does not sever it, no one can strike or assail the Buddha; the World-Honored One has attained fearlessness.
At that time, the Devaputra Viśuddhanetra spoke this verse in praise:
“The Buddha has taught that by cultivating those [practices], wisdom removes delusion;
if one does not sever them, no one can strike down or challenge the Buddha.
Then, the Devaputra Nirodhasaṃjñin spoke this verse in praise:
"To counteract discursive thought, he taught mindfulness of breathing;
for one who cultivates that without ceasing, no one can assail or trouble the Buddha.
Then, the Devaputra Respected by the Signless spoke this verse in praise:
"In order to sever the notion of 'self,' the Buddha taught emptiness and cessation;
because that [self] does not cease, no one can challenge this.
At that time, the Devaputra Chinnamāna spoke this verse in praise:
"To sever arrogance, the Buddha taught the Dharma of signlessness;
if one practices it without ceasing, one will not see anyone able to challenge the Buddha.
At that time, the Devaputra Viśuddhakāya spoke this verse in praise:
"With profound resolve and pure faith, all afflictions are exhausted;
for those who cultivate that which is uninterrupted, no one can strike them with difficulty.
At that time, the Devaputra Gambhīrādhimuktisaṃjñin spoke this verse in praise:
“Regarding antidotes and factions, seeking the path of afflictions,
and those who fearlessly challenge the Buddha— the Tathāgata does not see such as these at all.
At that time, the Devaputra Jñānaprayoga spoke this verse in praise:
“The Blessed One is merely a designation; whether this or that is exhausted or not exhausted, even those who pose fearless challenges are likewise mere conventional names.
At that time, the Devaputra Subdued Physical Action spoke this verse in praise:
"Having thoroughly understood through wisdom, his physical actions flow forth freely;
the World-Honored One knows all things completely, and is therefore titled 'Omniscient' (Sarvajña).
At that time, the Devaputra Jñānakāya spoke this verse in praise:
“Your physical karma is utterly pure; O Great Hero, you are entirely without remainder.
To the one who has compassion for all living beings, I pay homage to the Kinsman of the World.
Then, the Devaputra Viśuddhakāyakarmānta spoke this verse in praise:
“Having skillfully discerned bodily action, out of compassion for all sentient beings, he acts as one who illuminates the world; therefore, he is called the Supreme Man.
At that time, the devaputra Śubhavīkṣitakāyakarman spoke this verse in praise:
“Physical karma has attained purity; the Teacher perceives it all.
Out of compassion for all living beings, he is thus equal to the All-Knowing One.
At that time, the Devaputra Sunirīkṣitakāya spoke this verse in praise:
“Having attained purity through skillful observation, his physical actions are in perfect accord;
out of compassion for all living beings, this Supreme Man wanders forth.
Then, the Devaputra Accomplished in Speech spoke a verse in praise:
“Endowed with sweet and sublime virtues, free from frivolous and harsh speech,
surrounded by the marks of wisdom, the Kinsman of the World speaks.
Then, at that time, the Devaputra Timely Speech spoke this verse in praise:
"Acting in accordance with the meaning of the proper time, And remaining far removed from what is unbeneficial— The Buddha’s words are never unfaithful; All sentient beings receive and practice them.
Then the Devaputra Accomplished Wisdom spoke a verse in praise, saying:
"Without harming or pitying sentient beings, Accomplishing what is appropriate and free from turbidity,
Without destroying the law of cause and effect— Thus did the Buddha originally teach.
Then the Devaputra Asaṃvigna spoke this verse in praise:
"Even for the sake of one's own life, one has never uttered a false word;
therefore, the virtues of the Buddha are unimpeded throughout the world.
At that time, the Devaputra Satyavādin spoke this verse in praise:
“The Buddha acts according to the cause of truthful speech; therefore the world gazes upon him with reverence.
With sincere hearts they joyfully listen, for the sake of attaining the Buddha-dharma.
At that time, the Devaputra Tatsambhava spoke this verse in praise:
“By means of truthful speech, the World-Honored One has gradually perfected and attained Bodhi;
the true nature of all dharmas, the World-Honored One fully knows.
At that time, the Devaputra Real-Vīrya spoke this verse in praise:
"Regarding all conditioned phenomena, the World-Honored One perceives their nature as it truly is;
he fully knows the true characteristics of all dharmas.
At that time, the Devaputra Vīcāritakarma spoke this verse in praise:
"Regarding oneself and others, one knows the actions of body, speech, and mind;
because of the purity of that wisdom, the Buddha is called peerless.
At that time, the Devaputra named Contemplator of Mental Action spoke this verse in praise:
“The mental karma of the king of men, all his deliberations, and his compassionate concern for sentient beings—
for these reasons, I pay homage to the Compassionate One of the World. Then,
the Devaputra Skillful Contemplation of Mind spoke this verse in praise:
“The objects upon which the World-Honored One’s mind rests—this mind is entirely disciplined and supple;
out of compassionate concern for sentient beings, I pay homage to the Compassionate One who benefits the world.
Then, the Devaputra Skillful Means spoke this verse in praise:
"The objects of sentient beings' minds, The activities initiated by mental karma,
And the various kinds of wisdom that arise— The World-Honored One knows them all.
At that time, the Devaputra Vijñānabuddhi spoke this verse in praise:
“Mental karma is the stage of Buddhahood; because of compassionately observing all sentient beings, the wisdom of skillful means is pure, and the Buddha-wisdom has no inherent nature.
At that time, the Devaputra Skillfully Knowing the Past spoke this verse in praise:
“The Buddha knows the past lives, and whatever deeds people have performed— whether their precepts,
patience, diligence, or wisdom— the Buddha knows them all. At that time,
the Devaputra Past-Contemplator spoke this verse in praise:
“Observing past deeds, one can know many billions of Buddhas and the places where they practiced in the past, for the sake of seeking supreme enlightenment.
At that time, the Devaputra Pūrṇacarita spoke this verse in praise:
"Recalling deeds of former lives, For billions of *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas,
The Buddha’s mind is free from attachment— Such was the place where the Buddha formerly practiced.
Then, the Devaputra Observing Former Deeds spoke this verse in praise:
“Countless billions of Buddhas, the Guides, have all been questioned by him regarding the methods for giving birth to samādhi and the various factors of the Buddha-dharma.
At that time, the Devaputra Bhūmicāra uttered these verses in praise:
"Infinite and incalculable are the gateways to the samādhis of the Guides;
in the presence of all the Buddhas of the past, he once inquired about them and practiced them as well.
At that time, the Devaputra Avalokita-pūrvavāsa spoke this verse in praise:
“Within birth and death there are many faults; having observed those who are worthy of offerings and those who are not, he transforms sentient beings and delivers them from blindness and darkness.
At that time, the Devaputra Tired of Past Lives spoke this verse in praise:
“They have eaten one another, And likewise played and delighted together;
They have also killed and harmed each other— The World-Honored One knows all of this.
Then, the Devaputra Jñānāgata-viṣaya spoke this verse in praise:
"When the Guide appears in the future, his wisdom shall be unimpeded;
sentient beings will have faith in karmic retribution, and the Buddha will know all their realms of existence.
At that time, the Devaputra Pūrvacaryāgata spoke these verses in praise:
“The World-Honored One, in the past, possessed wisdom without obstruction;
through his wholesome karma and samādhi, he transcended the realms of existence and knew all destinies.
Then, the Devaputra Skillfully Knowing the Future spoke this verse in praise:
“The Buddha, in future times, possesses unobstructed wisdom regarding his final death and place of birth; it is likewise so regarding the retribution of karma.
At that time, the devaputra Vigatasaṃskāra spoke this verse in praise:
“The World-Honored One rules over the three realms; among the three times, he is supreme in teaching.
The Buddha’s wisdom is ever unimpeded, skillfully knowing all objective spheres.
At that time, the Devaputra Yongxing spoke this verse in praise:
“The courses of action taken by sentient beings, And the manner in which they receive their retributive fruits— These are all merely provisional names; Thus has the World-Honored One spoken.
Then the Devaputra Vicāraṇa-pratyutpanna spoke a verse in praise, saying:
“The Honored King of Kings, dwelling in the present, possesses wisdom that is ultimately unimpeded;
throughout countless Buddha-fields, the Muni knows them all.
At that time, the Devaputra Abhayamati spoke this verse in praise:
“The World-Honored One observes correctly that the three periods of time are entirely equal;
ultimately there is nothing at all, yet deluded ordinary beings possess such cognition.
At that time, the Devaputra Wisdom Without Abiding spoke this verse in praise:
“The Guide perceives thus: the three times have no abiding place;
for they rely upon the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), and all phenomena are without intrinsic event.
At that time, the Devaputra Teaching the Three Times spoke this verse in praise:
“Past and future, the aggregates that arise must perish;
they are without objective reality and lack intrinsic nature—this is what the Teacher has revealed.
Then, the Devaputra Manomayavi spoke this verse in praise:
“The World-Honored One has taught that the three periods of time are entirely without solidity;
they are like illusions and like mirages, and are said to be like echoes.
At that time, the Devaputra Trisaṃyavinirjita uttered these verses in praise:
“The World-Honored One, throughout the three periods of time, Constantly and diligently increases his wisdom;
Knowing all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) are like illusions, His faculties are free from attachment.
Then, the Devaputra Desiring to Reach the Other Shore spoke this verse in praise:
"On that very night, the Great Hero attained supreme enlightenment;
the World-Honored One’s diligent striving and desire have remained undiminished until this day.
At that time, the Devaputra named *Abhikāma* (Desirous of Diligence) spoke this verse in praise:
"The desires of the Lamp of the World never diminish;
the sons of the World-Honored One likewise possess a profound delight in the desire for diligence.
At that time, the devaputra Jianli yu zuo (Establishing the Desire to Act) spoke this verse in praise:
“The World-Honored One has arisen from desire, like a lotus in the water;
he is not defiled by the world, just as a lotus remains amidst the water.
At that time, the devaputra Vimuktarāga spoke this verse in praise:
“Desire and the worldly kin—these two are called the Dharma-realm.
They are non-dual and without dual essence; the World-Honored One perceives them both.
Then, the Devaputra Jinsheng (Born of Diligence) spoke this verse in praise:
“By the power and majesty of diligence, one realizes great enlightenment;
regarding both what is Dharma and what is not Dharma, one never abandons diligence.
At that time, the Devaputra Smṛtivibhūta spoke this verse in praise:
"The Buddha, in all circumstances, Acts in accordance with his initial resolve;
Regarding both wholesome and unwholesome dharmas, The Buddha’s mindfulness never diminishes.
Then, the Devaputra Samāhṛtacitta spoke this verse in praise:
“Vasubandhu constantly gathers his mind; knowing the conduct of all sentient beings, he preaches the Dharma for them according to their respective practices.
At that time, the Devaputra Prajñāgaurava spoke this verse in praise:
“The ocean of the World-Honored One’s wisdom has no attainable limit;
even throughout billions of *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, the Buddha could not exhaustively describe it.
At that time, the Devaputra Śikṣavimukti spoke this verse in praise:
“The peerless Buddha, the World-Honored One, is liberated and undiminished;
as for liberation and the one who is liberated, even the Buddha cannot find them.
At that time, the Devaputra Vimuktiprajñā spoke this verse in praise:
“The World-Honored One is liberated; His knowledge and vision of liberation are equal;
He understands reality without diminution, For he knows that there is no intrinsic nature.
At that time, the Devaputra Avalokita-kāya spoke this verse in praise:
"From the time of Dīpaṃkara onwards, the Buddha constantly cultivated the practice of true reality;
because his three karmas were free from fault, he is praised and hailed as a Buddha.
At that time, the Devaputra Gambhīracaryā spoke this verse in praise:
“The World-Honored One is without fault, unlike other sentient beings;
he knows the intrinsic nature of all phenomena, and the Buddha is never deluded regarding that intrinsic nature.
At that time, the Devaputra Mahāmati spoke this verse in praise:
"In all aspects, the Buddha’s mind is never deluded;
his mindfulness is ever-present, like a bowl filled to the brim with oil.
At that time, the Devaputra Asaṃkīrṇacitta spoke this verse in praise:
"Even for the briefest moment, his mind is never distracted;
the Buddha has attained the unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma) that all sentient beings do not know.
Then, the Devaputra Well-Understanding Wisdom spoke this verse in praise:
"If there were any conceptualization of relinquishment, the Sugata would not possess such a thing;
this is the unique quality of the World-Honored One, a dharma that is inconceivable.
Then, the devaputra Sarvābhibhū spoke a verse in praise:
"Thus, within the three realms, he knows all phenomena;
since nothing is equal to the Buddha in any respect, he is called 'The One Difficult to Subdue.
At that time, the Devaputra Dṛḍhadhara spoke this verse in praise:
“Unsurpassed and steadfast hero, you have no fear regarding the Dharma;
equal to all Buddhas, you are able to awaken those who have not yet awakened.
— *Mahāratnakūṭa Sūtra*, Fascicle 71.
The Great Treasure Accumulation Sutra, Volume Seventy-Two, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of the Northern Qi Dynasty.
Chapter Twenty-Four: The Non-Buddhist Cālakalpabharadvāja; from the *Bodhisattvadarśanabhūta-parivarta*, the section concerning the non-Buddhist Cālakalpabharadvāja.

Chapter Twenty-Four: On the Non-Buddhists. At that time, eight thousand non-Buddhist followers of Cārvāka Parivrājaka saw the asuras, garuḍas, nāga maidens and various nāgas, kumbhāṇḍas, gandharvas, yakṣas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, the gods who traverse the air, the gods of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, the Yāma heaven, the Tuṣita heaven, the Nirmāṇarati heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin heaven, the Brahmā heavens, the Ābhāsvara heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna heaven, the Bṛhatphala heaven, and the Śuddhāvāsa heavens, all making offerings to the World-Honored One; and hearing their praises, they conceived a sense of rare wonder.
Upon hearing this Dharma-gate, they immediately gave rise to doubt and uncertainty, having heard a teaching never before heard.
Those non-Buddhists addressed the Buddha, saying: “Gautama!
Having heard this Dharma never heard before, we do not rejoice.

The non-Buddhist Cārikā Parivrājaka also does not rejoice in the household life; we too have given rise to doubt and lack reverent faith regarding this Dharma, all because we have not heard it since the past.
Therefore, I also have a karmic connection with the śramaṇa Gautama. Why is this?
Because the śramaṇa Gautama has performed such supernatural transformations and miracles.

Having performed such supernatural transformations, because of those transformations, we saw these various devas obtain subtle and wondrous bodies; we also saw that the great multitude who had gone for refuge and submission to Gautama was exceedingly numerous. Because we knew that Gautama skillfully preached the Dharma, we consequently conceived renewed faith in Gautama.
"Gautama has further preached such a Dharma to the devas of the Vast Fruit (Bṛhatphala) heaven, saying that all dharmas are the Tathāgata.
We have developed great doubt and uncertainty regarding this: in what sense are all dharmas called the Tathāgata?"
"We have conceived such faith in Gautama that only Gautama knows our intentions.
Please speak to us in this way and in that way, so that we may understand the meaning of what you say and be freed from the net of doubt."
Having risen from their seats and made this request, the World-Honored One replied to them as follows:
"Therefore, I shall now question you in return; answer according to your own understanding."
The non-Buddhist said to the Buddha:
“Excellent, Gautama! Since Gautama asks me, I shall now speak.”
The Buddha then asked them:
"Do you know? How does the embryo enter the mother's womb?"
Having been asked thus, the non-Buddhist replied to the Buddha:
"Gautama! In our various treatises, we have heard it said that through the conjunction of three causes and conditions, the embryo enters the mother's womb."
"When the parents draw near, a state of greedy attachment arises and they contemplate sexual matters; because of this contemplation, they engage in desire, and thus the embryo enters.
In this way, the embryo is formed. The Buddha said, "What do you think, you followers of external paths?"
"When the parents think of it, does that craving arise from the mother's mind? The outsider replied, "No."
"Gautama! The Buddha said,
"Could it arise from the mother's deliberation?"
The non-Buddhist replied, “No, Gautama!”
The Buddha asked,
"Can that greed arise from the father's mind?
The non-Buddhist replied:
"No, Gautama," he replied. The Buddha said:
“Does it arise from the father’s deliberation?
The non-Buddhist replied, “No.”
"Gautama! The Buddha said, "What do you think?"
"Can that father's craving enter the mother's womb?
The outsider replied, "No."
"Gautama! The Buddha said, "What do you think?"
"Does the father's mind enter the mother's womb? The outsider replied, "No."
"Gautama! The Buddha said, "What do you think?"
“Does the father enter the mother’s womb separately?
The non-Buddhist replied, “No.”
"Gautama! The Buddha said, "What do you think?"
"Does that fetus come from the end of its life as a deva to enter the mother's womb?
The outsider replied, "I do not know."
"Gautama! The Buddha said, "What do you think?"
“Does that fetus come from having ended its life in hell before entering the mother’s womb?
The outsider replied, “I do not know.”
"Gautama! The Buddha said, "What do you think?"
“Does that fetus come from having ended its life as an animal to enter the mother’s womb?
The non-Buddhist replied, “I do not know.”
"Gautama! The Buddha said, "What do you think?"
“Does that embryo enter the mother’s womb after having passed away from the realm of hungry ghosts?
The outsider replied, “I do not know.”
"Gautama! The Buddha said, "What do you think?"
“Does that fetus come from having ended its life as an asura to enter the mother’s womb?
The outsider replied, “I do not know.”
"Gautama! The Buddha said, "What do you think?"
"Could that embryo enter the mother's womb as something non-material?
The outsider replied, "I do not know."
"Gautama! The Buddha said, "What do you think?"
"Does that embryo enter the mother's womb as form?
The non-Buddhist replied, "I do not know."
"Gautama! The Buddha said, "What do you think?"
"Do feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness come into the mother's womb?
The non-Buddhist replied, "I do not know."
"Gautama! Having given this reply, the Buddha addressed the non-Buddhist practitioner with these words:
"Non-Buddhist practitioner!..."
This Dharma is profound, peaceful, and well-expounded; it is subtle and difficult to fathom, beyond the sphere of discursive thought, hard to demonstrate, and not within the scope of your knowledge.

These various non-Buddhists possess divergent views, divergent tolerances, and diverse inclinations; they exert themselves in practice toward what is not the true path, remaining resolutely intent upon their divergent views.
The Buddha said,
“O non-Buddhists!
If good sons and good daughters encounter such spiritual friends, they will gain the faculty of vision regarding the profound Dharma.”
"O non-Buddhist!

It is like a person who suffers from a disease of the visual faculty; upon meeting a skilled physician and having his eyes cured, he uses those purified eyes to perceive in the present forms that he had never seen before."
"Thus it is, O outsider!

If there are good sons or good daughters who do not possess the five faculties such as faith, yet encounter a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) and purify their eye of wisdom, they shall, by means of that purified eye of wisdom, perceive the profound Dharma."

Therefore, you followers of external paths, having long been deluded by false doctrines throughout the night of ignorance, have formed divergent views; you perceive the characteristics of wholesome Dharma where there is no Dharma, the characteristics of liberation where there is no liberation, and the characteristic of emergence where there is no way out. Your teacher has brought ruin upon himself and shall likewise bring ruin upon you.
"O non-Buddhist!
It is like a man who is himself blind telling another blind man:
'I will lead you away.'"
"The wise should know that these two persons will inevitably fall upon that which is not the path and encounter suffering and hardship.
It is the same, O outsider!"

Whether they be śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas, those who are not actually guides yet claim to be guides; who are not actually perfectly awakened yet say, "I am perfectly awakened"; who do not actually know the supramundane path yet say, "I know it"; who do not actually see the supramundane path yet say, "I see it"; who do not actually know the shallow crossing-places yet say, "I know them"; and who are not actually teachers yet say, "I am a teacher"—the teaching they impart is a false doctrine.
Unless one is a Perfectly Awakened One, those whom one teaches to awaken are likewise awakened through false awakening.
If one does not truly understand liberation yet claims, "I can understand it," then that which one teaches for liberation is a false liberation.
Not knowing the truth, he claims to know it; all that he teaches is a false path.
Not knowing shallow waters, he claims to know them; those whom he leads across are instead brought to distress.
"O outsider!
It is like a cowherd who, not knowing the shallow places, drives his cattle into deep water to cross over.
Those cattle, abandoning this shore yet not having reached the other shore, fall into distress in the middle of the stream with no one to rescue them."
Why is this? Because the cowherds do not know the shallow places,
O outsiders!
It is so. You are not true guides, yet you conceive yourselves to be guides; those whom you seek to transform instead suffer distress and calamity.
O followers of external paths!
I am the Teacher truly capable of guiding; those who are to be guided, I guide them correctly.
My awakening is not in vain; those whom I have awakened, I cause them to awaken correctly.
I am one who can emerge; what I say is not in vain, and those whom I instruct to emerge, I cause to emerge correctly.
Having seen the path of emergence, I am further able to show it to others; to those whom I guide, I show the correct road.
I know shallow waters, and thus my words are not false; therefore, those whom I deliver I cause to cross over correctly.
I know the method of teaching and transforming, and thus I am able to transform others.
I know the Buddha-dharma and am able to awaken others.
I know the way of transcendence and can cause others to attain it.
By virtue of my right view, I am further able to correctly demonstrate it to others.
Because I know the places where beings may be delivered, I am able to deliver others; those whom I lead across shall cause them to attain the Good Path.
You outsiders who delight in liberation, I am your guide, standing here before you now.

"You all should come; I am one who has attained right awakening, who fully understands the Dharma that leads out [of suffering], who clearly perceives the path leading out, and who can provide a shallow crossing-place. You all should listen attentively with a single mind and reflect well; let the aspiration for liberation arise in you all and let right mindfulness be present before you. Your minds should flow toward this and exert diligent effort, so that what has not yet been realized may be realized, what has not yet been attained may be attained, the path not yet traveled may be entered, the place not yet reached may be reached, Māra not yet subdued may be subdued, those who have not sought companions may find them, and those who have not obtained the skillful means of the Dharma may obtain those skillful means."
“O non-Buddhists!
As I have taught, conception occurs through the conjunction of three factors.
I shall now speak; you non-Buddhists, listen with single-minded attention. I shall explain for you the Dharma-gate of conception.”
"O non-Buddhist!
What I call the mother is the condition for past karma; what I call the father is the cause of past karma; and what I call the gandharva refers to consciousness summoned by karma."
"O non-Buddhist!
When I speak of the *kalala*, I mean that which is established by karma.
O non-Buddhist!"
I say that the mother’s womb is the locus where karma establishes the support for consciousness.
Once consciousness has entered the womb, it is born, attains growth, and gradually expands.
O outsider!
"O non-Buddhists! It is just as medicinal herbs and forests depend upon the great earth to grow and gradually expand. It is even so."
Once that consciousness has entered the mother’s womb, its growth and expansion proceed in the same manner.
The infant within the mother’s womb grows until it is finally born; having been born, it continues to increase in size.

Once they have grown up, their conduct proceeds according to the nature established by their past habits and the place from which they have come; that which was practiced in the past arises as a present habituation.
This is known through wisdom, not by the ignorant who can comprehend it; only through constant observation while living together with them as friends and associates can one know their true nature.
"O non-Buddhists, listen attentively! If a person has passed away from hell and is reborn among humans, they will possess these signs, which the wise should recognize.

Their voice will be hoarse and broken like that of a donkey, hurried and urgent, fearful, loud, and shallow. They will have a small mind constantly filled with dread; they will frequently tremble with terror until their body hair stands on end. In their dreams, they often see great fires blazing, or see mountains moving, or see masses of fire, or see cauldrons and vats boiling over, or see people running while brandishing staves, or see themselves being pierced by spears and lances, or see rākṣasīs, or see packs of dogs, or see herds of elephants pursuing them, or see themselves running in all four directions without any place of refuge."
Their minds have little faith, and they have no close friends.
O non-Buddhists!
There are such immeasurable signs as these; I have now briefly described these signs, which are called those who, having ended their lives in hell, are reborn among humans.
This is known by wisdom; it cannot be fathomed by the ignorant.
"O non-Buddhists, listen well: if that person has passed away from the animal realm and been reborn among humans, they will possess these signs; the wise should know this."
Dull-witted and lacking in intelligence, indolent and gluttonous, they delight in eating clay;
their nature is timid and weak, and they are inarticulate in speech. They take pleasure in befriending fools, find joy in dark places, and love turbid water.
They enjoy gnawing on grass and wood, delight in scratching the earth with their toes, and are fond of such pleasures.
He constantly moves his head to drive away flies and gadflies; he always delights in lifting his head and yawning while chewing empty air;
he always delights in curling his limbs and lying on the ground as he pleases, regardless of filth; he always delights in sniffing at nothing and taking pleasure in nakedness;
he always delights in vain pretenses, strange speech, and strange actions; he frequently delights in frivolous talk; and in dreams, he sees himself smeared with mud, or he sees...
One sees oneself grazing on grass in a field, or dreams that one's body is entwined by many snakes,
or dreams that one has entered into mountain valleys and dense forests.
"O outsider!
There are such immeasurable varieties of signs; I have now briefly described these signs, which are called those who pass away from the animal realm and are reborn among humans."
"The wise can know this; the foolish cannot perceive it.
Listen attentively, O non-Buddhists: if such a person has passed away from the realm of hungry ghosts and is reborn among humans, they will possess these signs, which the wise should recognize."
