Chapter 26: The Four Universal Monarchs (Part One) At that time, the Buddha addressed King Śuddhodana, saying:
"Great King! Regarding the Dharma as explained above, you should apply your mind with diligence, observing and practicing it for yourself, and not follow others.

This Dharma is the Bodhi of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present; it enables one to transcend all worlds with mastery, to eliminate all craving, to subdue pride, and to extinguish transgressions, thereby attaining equanimity toward all phenomena."

It is not the stage of ordinary beings; it is beyond the reach of all śrāvakas, it is not within the domain of any pratyekabuddhas, it is that which is practiced by all bodhisattvas, and it is that which is realized by all buddhas.
"Great King!
Within this Dharma, you should settle your mind and reflect thus:
'How may I become an eye for gods and humans; how may I become a lamp, a great torch, a raft that well knows the waterways, a guide, a caravan leader, and a chief conductor?'"

How shall I, having first delivered myself, be able to deliver others; having myself attained liberation, cause others to attain liberation; having myself attained peace and security, cause others to attain peace and security; and having myself realized nirvana, cause others to realize nirvana?
"Great King, you should know that one should not dwell upon the past limits of having been wealthy, powerful, and sovereign. Great King!
The sense faculties are like illusions; there is no time at which they are satisfied, nor is there anyone who can satisfy them."
"Sensory realms are like dreams; one never finds satiety in forms, sounds, odors, tastes, or tactile objects.
Great King! In ages past, there was a wheel-turning monarch named King Anantayaśas."

That King Anantayaśas possessed immeasurable multitudes of treasures, including palanquins, chariots, and hosts of elephants and horses; he was fully endowed with the seven precious jewels, foremost among them the unimpeded wheel-treasure (*cakraratna*), such that none could destroy any of his military vehicles or mounts.
Having planted various roots of goodness under previous Buddhas, his mental power was perfected such that whatever he recollected was accomplished immediately.
Great King! There was nothing that King Immeasurable Fame could not achieve according to his will whenever he brought it to mind.
Why is this? Because he has fully accomplished the power of roots of goodness,
O Great King!
At that time, King Aparimitayaśas had this thought:
"I shall now test the power of my own merit.
Then, King Aparimitayaśas immediately formed this thought:
"By my power, I shall cause all the trees throughout these four continents to always bear flowers and fruit, so that they may be used without end.
Great King! After King Immeasurable Fame had formed this thought, all the groves of trees throughout the four continents became profuse with flowers and fruit, which could never be exhausted.
"Great King!
King Immeasurable Renown again had this thought:
'May all the people throughout the four continents have whatever desires and aspirations they wish for fulfilled according to their will, without any hindrance.'"
"Great King! Once King Immeasurable Fame had formed this thought, all the people throughout the four continents had every one of their wishes completely fulfilled."
"Great King!
King Immeasurable Fame again had this thought:
'I shall further test the power of my roots of goodness.'"
"If I possess merit, may the four heavenly kings pour down fragrant water.
Having formed this thought, a rain of fragrance immediately descended upon the four continents.
Great King!
At that time, King Immeasurable Fame again had this thought:
"I shall now further test my own power of merit. Great King!
At that time, King Immeasurable Fame (Amitayaśas) thought to himself:
"If my power of merit is such, may it cause exquisite flowers to rain down everywhere throughout the four continents.
As soon as he had this thought, exquisite flowers immediately began to rain down across the four continents.
"Great King!
At that time, King Immeasurable Fame again had this thought:
'I shall now further test the power of my own merit.'"
"If I possess merit, may fine garments rain down everywhere throughout the four continents.
Having formed this thought, celestial garments from the *karpāsa* trees immediately rained down across the four continents.
"Great King!
That King Immeasurable Renown (Amitayaśas) further thought to himself:
'I shall now test the power of my merit.'"
"If I possess merit, may a rain of silver fall everywhere throughout the four continents.
Having formed this thought, a rain of silver immediately descended upon the four continents,
O Great King!
King Aparimitayaśas again thought to himself:
"I shall now further test my own power of merit.
He then thought again:
"If I possess merit, may a rain of gold fall everywhere throughout the four continents.
Having formed this thought, a rain of gold immediately fell upon the four continents.
Why is this? Because King Aparimitayaśas’s aspirations were fulfilled according to his wishes entirely due to his cultivation of shared virtuous karma toward all sentient beings in the past.
"Great King!..."
At that time, this land of Jambudvīpa was exactly eighteen thousand yojanas in length and breadth.
At that very moment, there were six hundred million great cities and towns in this Jambudvīpa.
"Great King!
At that time, within this Jambudvīpa, a walled city was established named Ratnavyūha.

That city was twelve yojanas in length and breadth; its four sides were level and straight, constructed with exquisite craftsmanship, and its streets and lanes were adorned with clearly demarcated boundaries."

Outside its city walls, there were seven rows of tāla trees arranged in succession; these tāla trees were composed of the four jewels—namely gold, silver, lapis lazuli, and crystal—and were so magnificently adorned and stately that they were exceedingly delightful.
As for those golden trees, their roots, trunks, branches, and twigs are all gold, while their leaves, flowers, and fruits are all white silver.
As for those silver trees, their roots, trunks, branches, and twigs are all silver, while their leaves, flowers, and fruits are all gold.
As for the Vaiḍūrya trees, their roots, trunks, branches, and twigs are all made of Vaiḍūrya, while their leaves, flowers, and fruits are all of crystal (sphaṭika).
As for the crystal trees, their roots, trunks, branches, and twigs are all made of crystal, while their leaves, flowers, and fruits are all of Vaiḍūrya.
"Great King!

At that time, the Jewel-Adorned City was surrounded on all sides by seven tiers of hanging nets of precious bells, most exquisite and supreme in their various adornments; furthermore, it was completely covered above by nets made of various kinds of jewels."
Outside its city walls are seven tiers of precious moats; each individual moat is half a yojana deep and one yojana wide.
The bottoms and banks of these seven tiers of moats are level and even, filled with the pure water of eight virtues, which is easy for various birds to drink from.
Furthermore, there were various flowers—namely, utpala flowers, kumuda flowers, padma flowers, and puṇḍarīka flowers—which filled it completely.
The bottom is spread with golden sand.

The steps and pathways surrounding the four sides of the moat are adorned with the four treasures—namely gold, silver, lapis lazuli, and crystal—which are of various exquisite qualities and most delightful.

Those stairways and paths were composed of the four precious substances: golden steps with silver treads, and silver steps with golden treads, with lapis lazuli and crystal interspersed throughout from top to bottom, mutually adorning one another.
The surrounding railings are composed of the seven precious gems, their majesty and beauty being beyond compare.
Each flight of stairs has seven tiers of jeweled gates, adorned with various exquisite and supreme ornaments; on both sides of each flight of stairs stand golden plantain trees.
The moat was surrounded on all four sides by stairways, at both ends of which there were seven-jeweled thrones.
All the various kinds of adornments therein were brought about solely by the merit of King Anantayaśas.

Surrounding the city of Ratnavyūha were eighty thousand gardens; King Anantayaśas created these gardens without giving rise to any sense of attachment or possessiveness, bestowing them all upon sentient beings so that they might enjoy them together.
In each of these gardens there are eight great ponds, and each great pond is half a yojana in length and breadth.

Within these ponds are various kinds of flowers—blue lotuses (utpala), red lotuses (padma), yellow lotuses (kumuda), and white lotuses (puṇḍarīka)—such that these many flowers completely cover their surfaces.
Alongside each pond there are eight stairways, each stairway being composed of the four precious substances, exquisite and most wonderful in their beauty.
At the head of each stairway stands a gate-tower made of the seven treasures, namely gold, silver, lapis lazuli, agate, and so forth.
On both sides of the steps, *jambūnada* gold forms plantain trees, exquisitely adorned and magnificent.
The water of eight virtues fills the ponds, fit for the drinking of various birds.

On all four sides of that pond were planted various exquisite flowers, namely: the *ati-muktaka*, the *campaka*, the *aśoka*, the *kuraṇṭaka*, the *pāṭalī*, the *kaṇikāra*, the *bakula*, the *bāliśaka*, the *mallikā*, the *sumana*, the *māluda*, and the *cīnusi* flowers.

Such land-growing flowers as these, King Immeasurable Fame planted in various exquisite varieties for the sake of providing pleasure and delight to all people; thus, the populace sports therein, enjoying themselves with joy and happiness.
"Great King!
All the jeweled bells, nets, and precious tala trees in that city of Jewel Adornment produce harmonious and elegant sounds when stirred by a gentle breeze."
For example, suppose there were someone skilled at playing five kinds of exquisite music, whose sound was harmonious and elegant, most delightful to hear.
The wonderful sounds produced by the nets of bells, jeweled trees, groves, and musical instruments within the royal palace city of King Aparimitayaśas were likewise most delightful.
"Great King!
At that time, all the people within the city of Ratnavyūha enjoyed themselves with that exquisite music.
Then, that city of Ratnavyūha was prosperous, joyful, peaceful, and secure; it was filled with people who were wealthy, noble, and independent."
"In every place there were blue lotuses (utpala), red lotuses (padma), yellow lotuses (kumuda), and white lotuses (puṇḍarīka).
'Great King! At another time, King Aparimitayaśas again had this thought:"
"I shall now go to Aparagoyānī.
Having formed this thought, the king and his fourfold army ascended into the air and proceeded to Aparagoyānī.
Once the king had arrived there, the local minor kings all came forth to welcome him, each offering their own kingdom as a tribute.
"Great King!
At that time, King Immeasurable Fame resided there for hundreds of thousands of millions of years.
Under his reign, Great King!"
King Aparimitayaśas again thought to himself,
"I shall now go to Pūrvavideha. Having had this thought,
he immediately ascended into the air with his fourfold army and proceeded to Pūrvavideha.
When the King arrived there, the minor kings of that land also came forth to welcome him and further offered their kingdoms to him.
Great King! King Immeasurable Fame resided there for hundreds of thousands of myriads of years.
"O Great King! Within that realm, at another time, King Aparājitābhibhū (Immeasurable Fame) reflected thus:
'I shall go to that northern continent of Uttarakuru.'"
Having formed this thought, he immediately ascended into the air with his fourfold army and proceeded to Uttarakuru.
Once the king arrived there, the people of that land joyfully submitted to him and were converted.
The king dwelt there for many hundreds of thousands of years,
experiencing pleasure and instructing his retinue. Great King!
After a long time had passed, King Aparimitayaśas again thought to himself:
"I have heard that there are the Thirty-three Gods dwelling upon the summit of Mount Sumeru; I should now go to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven."
Having formed this thought, he immediately mounted a dragon-elephant and, together with his fourfold army, soared into the void and ascended Mount Sumeru.
Great King! At that time, King Immeasurable Fame questioned his charioteer:
"You see Mount Sumeru, the great ocean, and the four continents;
what do you make of this?
The minister replied to the king:
"I see Mount Sumeru, the great waters of the ocean, and the four continents all spinning together,
just as a potter turns his wheel with a staff.
My vision of Mount Sumeru and the four continents all spinning is exactly like this."
The king said to his charioteer:
"This great elephant king has not yet ceased its great journey. O Great King!
At that time, King Immeasurable Fame proceeded further forward and asked his charioteer:
"What do you see of Mount Sumeru, the great ocean, and the four continents?
Furthermore, what else is there?"
The minister replied,
"I saw Mount Sumeru, the waters of the great ocean, and the four continents all tremble.
The king answered the minister:
"We are now about to reach the summit of Mount Sumeru;
this king of nāga-elephants has not yet finished his minor urination.
"Great King! [he continued.]
King Immeasurable Fame proceeded further and asked his charioteer:
"What do you see of Mount Sumeru, the waters of the great ocean, and the four continents? What are their appearances like?"
The minister replied to the king:
"I see Mount Sumeru, the great waters of the ocean, and the four continents as unmoving and unswerving.
The king said to the minister:
"This king of elephants has now reached the summit of that Mount Sumeru.
Great King! At that time, King Immeasurable Fame, together with his fourfold army, immediately arrived at the summit of that Mount Sumeru.
"Great King!
At that time, Śakra, seeing King Anantayaśas from afar, came forward to welcome him with joy and spoke these words:
'Welcome, Great King!'"
He immediately divided his seat in half and bade the king take a seat.
The king then took his place.
For immeasurable years thereafter, he remained in that celestial realm, ruling as co-sovereign with that lord of devas by sharing half of his throne.
"Great King!
At that time, after a long period, King Immeasurable Fame again thought thus:
'I would now rather displace that Lord of Devas and dwell therein alone as the Heavenly King.'"

Having formed this thought, King Immeasurable Fame and his fourfold army immediately descended from the Heaven of the Thirty-three and returned to the city of Jewel Adornment in Jambudvīpa, falling into the Garden of Seven Jewels.

At that time, the people of the city of Ratnavyūha went outside the city to the Jewel Casket Garden (Ratnakoṭi-udyāna), where they saw King Anantayaśas and his fourfold army descending from the heavens into that garden.
Having seen this, the multitude quickly entered the city and addressed the people therein, saying:
"Now there is a Son of Heaven, together with his fourfold army, who has come from heaven and is present within the Ratnakoṭi Garden."
At that time, in the city of Ratnavyūha, there was another king named Kāraṇa who governed the affairs of state.

When King Kāraṇa heard that a son of heaven, together with the fourfold army, had descended from the heavens into the Ratnakośa Garden, he immediately issued urgent orders to his fourfold army to prepare excellent vehicles. Accompanied by the citizens of the city, he departed from Ratnavyūha and proceeded to the Ratnakośa Garden.
When King [Name] and the people of the city saw King Aparimitayaśas, they marveled at this unprecedented occurrence.

Thereupon, King Kāmadarśin immediately commanded that various kinds of incense, flowers, powdered incense, and ointments be quickly prepared; he then proceeded swiftly to King Aparimitayaśas, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms, and prostrating before King Aparimitayaśas, spoke these words: "Who are you?"
The king immediately replied:
"Have you ever heard before of King Anantayaśas?
Then King Kāraṇḍu and all the ministers and subjects said:

"I have previously heard from those of old that there was once a great king named Amitayaśas who ruled over the four continents; he ascended to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven together with his fourfold army."
King Aparimitayaśas replied to him, saying:
"As you have heard, King Aparimitayaśas is none other than my own self.

At that time, as King Aparimitayaśas first descended from heaven, he heard the savory essence of food and drink among the human realm; his heart felt no joy and could not endure it. His body became heavy and昏厥 (stupefied), like clarified butter cast into hot sand, immediately sinking down so that he could not remain suspended for even a moment.
King Immeasurable Fame felt no attachment to the flavors of food and drink in Jambudvīpa; his body and mind became utterly despondent in the same way.

At that time, King Making-Love saw that King Immeasurable Fame could not endure the fragrances and foods of the human realm, and as his body and mind were suddenly exhausted and unable to remain, he spoke these words:
"What virtuous words does King Immeasurable Fame have for me? What shall I proclaim to future generations?"
"Great King! At that time, King Immeasurable Fame said to King Kāmadarśana: 'You should know this:

since ancient times, King Immeasurable Fame has reigned over the four continents with sovereign majesty and power. Whatever he desires or thinks of is never contrary to his will. The trees, forests, flowers, fruits, and even the wish-fulfilling fruits can eliminate the suffering and affliction of all sentient beings, providing whatever necessities they require so that all may have their wishes fulfilled.'"
I was further able to bring down celestial fragrances, rain down divine garments and heavenly flowers, and shower down silver and gold, ruling over the four continents with wealth and sovereignty.
He ascended to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, where Śakra shared his seat with him to govern the affairs of the devas.
Because he was insatiable in his greed, he fell from that heavenly realm; descending to Jambudvīpa, he eventually met his end.
Then King Aparimitayaśas said to King Kāmakāra:
"Regarding all these matters, you shall speak thus in the future:
'King Aparimitayaśas, though possessed of great wealth and power, died of his own accord due to insatiable greed.'"
Having spoken these words, he immediately passed away.
The Buddha said:
"Great King, you should know that you must not view this otherwise; do not give rise to a mind of hesitation or doubt."
"Was King Immeasurable Renown at that time anyone else?
It was I myself, Great King!"
Therefore, you should know that the sense faculties are like illusions and their objects are like dreams.
Great King!
In this way, you should bind your mind to correct contemplation and not rely on others.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
"Always delighting in the Dharma and attaining mastery, One should repeatedly urge on one's own mind.
Amidst the mastery of craving and desire, The wise mind should remain far removed."
Having attained mastery over freedom from desire, one dwells within mastery over the Dharma;
if one can subdue the mind, then one can subdue the afflictions.
If one can subdue the afflictions, one immediately attains liberation from the path of karma.
If one has departed from the paths of karma, one becomes a stūpa for the world.
Untainted by the defilement of desire, one reveals the faults of afflictions and brings to mind the benefit of sentient beings; therefore, such a person is called a caitya.
Having heard of the faults of craving, one is able to abandon craving;
because his mind of omniscience is pure, he is called a *caitya*.
This most excellent Great Being contemplates the extinguishing of the evils of sentient beings.
Because he has liberated others from hatred, he is called a *caitya*.
Because that most excellent Great Man, mindful of extinguishing the delusion of sentient beings,
has liberated them from their ignorant minds, he is called a *caitya*.
The Tamer of Gods and Humans, who contemplates the cessation of the pride of sentient beings and purifies their minds, is therefore called a *caitya*.
